domain: Models, Training, Evaluation, Uncertainty — models/{base,glm,huber_glm,rf,nn_whuber,registry_wrappers}.py, ml/{model_registry,baseline_models,eval,bootstrap,calibration,sensitivity,nn_recommender,estimator_utils}.py, plus the orchestration that actually implements the contract in pages/06_Train_and_Compare.py

modules.purpose: Declares BaseModelWrapper, the ABC every model wrapper inherits. Only fit() and predict() are @abstractmethod; predict_proba/get_model/supports_proba are CONCRETE defaults (None / self.model / False), so a subclass silently inherits 'no probabilities' rather than failing to instantiate. Zero streamlit, zero test coverage.

keyFunctions.name: BaseModelWrapper.__init__
keyFunctions.signature: __init__(self, name: str)
keyFunctions.does: Sets self.name, self.model = None, self.is_fitted = False. is_fitted is a plain bool set by each subclass's fit(); nothing validates it.

keyFunctions.name: BaseModelWrapper.fit
keyFunctions.signature: @abstractmethod fit(self, X_train: np.ndarray, y_train: np.ndarray, X_val: Optional[np.ndarray] = None, y_val: Optional[np.ndarray] = None, **kwargs) -> Dict[str, Any]
keyFunctions.does: Abstract. Docstring promises 'Dictionary with training history/metrics' but does NOT specify keys — every subclass invents its own (see landmine on history schema).
keyFunctions.transitionNote: TurboTab must add an explicit return TypedDict and a progress/cancel parameter here; today the base signature has neither, so only the NN can report progress.

keyFunctions.name: BaseModelWrapper.predict
keyFunctions.signature: @abstractmethod predict(self, X: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray
keyFunctions.does: Abstract. No shape/dtype contract stated; NN returns flattened float array for regression and ORIGINAL class labels (self.classes_[idx]) for classification, sklearn wrappers return whatever the estimator returns.

keyFunctions.name: BaseModelWrapper.predict_proba
keyFunctions.signature: predict_proba(self, X: np.ndarray) -> Optional[np.ndarray]
keyFunctions.does: CONCRETE default returning None. Not abstract — this is why HuberGLMWrapper needs no override.

keyFunctions.name: BaseModelWrapper.get_model
keyFunctions.signature: get_model(self) -> Any
keyFunctions.does: Returns self.model. NNWeightedHuberWrapper OVERRIDES this to return an sklearn shim rather than self.model — the single deviation from the base contract.

keyFunctions.name: BaseModelWrapper.supports_proba
keyFunctions.signature: supports_proba(self) -> bool
keyFunctions.does: CONCRETE default returning False. This runtime method — not ModelCapabilities.supports_predict_proba — is what every call site actually consults.

modules.purpose: 638 loc: SimpleMLP, weighted_huber_loss, two sklearn-compatible shims, and NNWeightedHuberWrapper (the only model with a real training loop). This is the only file in the whole domain that has ANY progress hook, and the only one holding process-global state (torch device, RNG seeding).

keyFunctions.name: SimpleMLP.__init__
keyFunctions.signature: __init__(self, input_dim: int, hidden: list = [32, 32], dropout: float = 0.1, output_dim: int = 1, activation: str = 'relu', use_batchnorm: bool = False)
keyFunctions.does: Builds nn.Sequential of Linear->[BatchNorm1d]->activation->Dropout blocks. NOTE: a SINGLE activation module instance is appended to every block (activation_fn is constructed once and reused), and `hidden: list = [32,32]` is a MUTABLE DEFAULT ARGUMENT.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Mutable default and shared activation instance are latent bugs the moment someone adds a parameterized activation (PReLU) or mutates the default list.

keyFunctions.name: weighted_huber_loss
keyFunctions.signature: weighted_huber_loss(y_pred: torch.Tensor, y_true: torch.Tensor, t0: float = 180.0, s: float = 20.0, alpha: float = 2.5) -> torch.Tensor
keyFunctions.does: Huber (delta=1.0) reweighted by 1 + alpha*exp(-((y_true-t0)/s)^2), clamped to [0.1, 10.0]. The 180/20 defaults are legacy glucose constants; callers are supposed to derive t0/s from the training target.

keyFunctions.name: NNWeightedHuberWrapper.__init__
keyFunctions.signature: __init__(self, hidden_layers: List[int] = None, dropout: float = 0.1, task_type: str = 'regression', activation: str = 'relu', loss_function: str = 'mse', use_batchnorm: bool = False)
keyFunctions.does: hidden_layers defaults to [128,128,128]. Sets self.device from torch.cuda.is_available() at CONSTRUCTION time. Declares REGRESSION_LOSSES = {'mse','huber','weighted_huber','mae'}.

keyFunctions.name: NNWeightedHuberWrapper.fit
keyFunctions.signature: fit(self, X_train, y_train, X_val=None, y_val=None, epochs: int = 200, batch_size: int = 256, lr: float = 0.001, weight_decay: float = 1e-5, patience: int = 30, progress_callback: Optional[callable] = None, random_seed: Optional[int] = None, lr_scheduler: str = 'reduce_on_plateau', grad_clip_norm: Optional[float] = None, **kwargs) -> Dict[str, Any]
keyFunctions.does: THE long-running op. Full epoch loop with Adam, one of 3 LR schedulers, early stopping on val, best-state cloning, and per-epoch progress_callback(epoch+1, train_loss, val_loss, val_metric). Derives self._whuber_t0 = percentile(y_train,90) and self._whuber_s = max(std*0.5,1e-6) only when loss_function=='weighted_huber'. Returns {'history': {...}, 'best_val_rmse': ..., 'best_val_accuracy': ...}.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: TO MAKE IT AN OBSERVABLE JOB: (1) progress_callback fires only when X_val is not None with real metrics — with no val set it fires progress_callback(epoch+1, train_loss, train_loss, 0.0), a fake val metric. (2) NO cancel hook exists — add a `should_cancel: Callable[[], bool]` checked at the top of each epoch AND each batch (a single epoch on a large batch_size can be seconds). (3) progress is per-epoch only, so a 200-epoch run yields 200 ticks but a single epoch is opaque. (4) It calls torch.manual_seed / np.random.seed GLOBALLY — must move to a torch.Generator + np.random.default_rng before two jobs can run concurrently.

keyFunctions.name: NNWeightedHuberWrapper.get_model
keyFunctions.signature: get_model(self) -> Any
keyFunctions.does: CONTRACT DEVIATION: does NOT return self.model (the torch Module). Returns self.get_sklearn_estimator() — a SklearnCompatibleNNRegressor/Classifier shim. Raises ValueError if not is_fitted.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Every generic `clone(wrapper.get_model())` path must keep excluding the NN, or produce garbage silently (see landmines).

keyFunctions.name: NNWeightedHuberWrapper.get_sklearn_estimator
keyFunctions.signature: get_sklearn_estimator(self)
keyFunctions.does: Lazily builds and memoizes self._sklearn_estimator, then sets is_fitted_=True, n_features_in_ from model.layers[0].in_features, and classes_ from self.classes_. The memo means the shim and the wrapper are permanently aliased.

keyFunctions.name: SklearnCompatibleNNRegressor.fit / SklearnCompatibleNNClassifier.fit
keyFunctions.signature: fit(self, X, y)  # both classes
keyFunctions.does: DOES NOT TRAIN ANYTHING. Sets is_fitted_=True, n_features_in_=X.shape[1] (and classes_=np.unique(y) for the classifier), returns self. Docstring says 'The actual training is done by wrapper_instance.fit() before this is called.'
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Highest-risk object in the domain. It satisfies sklearn's duck-type for fit/predict/predict_proba while being a no-op trainer. Keep it only as an explicitly-named PredictOnlyAdapter that RAISES on fit(), and give it a distinct type the jobs layer can refuse to cross-validate.

keyFunctions.name: SklearnCompatibleNN
keyFunctions.signature: SklearnCompatibleNN(wrapper_instance=None, task_type='regression')
keyFunctions.does: Factory returning Classifier shim if task_type=='classification' else Regressor shim.

keyFunctions.name: SklearnCompatibleNN*.get_params / set_params
keyFunctions.signature: get_params(self, deep=True) -> {'wrapper_instance': ...} ; set_params(self, **params)
keyFunctions.does: get_params reports ONLY wrapper_instance; set_params SILENTLY IGNORES every key except 'wrapper_instance' and returns self without error.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: set_params silently swallowing unknown params means any hyperparameter sweep against the shim appears to work and changes nothing.

keyFunctions.name: NNWeightedHuberWrapper.get_architecture_summary
keyFunctions.signature: get_architecture_summary(self) -> Dict[str, Any]
keyFunctions.does: Returns hidden_layers, num_layers, dropout, activation, use_batchnorm, loss_function, total_params. Consumed by pages/06 (stored into results['architecture']) and pages/10 for the manuscript.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Does NOT include _whuber_t0/_whuber_s, epochs actually run, or the seed — the manuscript's architecture block is therefore not sufficient to reproduce the fit.

keyFunctions.name: NNWeightedHuberWrapper.get_training_history
keyFunctions.signature: get_training_history(self) -> Optional[Dict[str, List[float]]]
keyFunctions.does: Returns self.history (set at end of fit). Read by pages/10_Report_Export.py:1420.

modules.purpose: RegistryModelWrapper — the generic adapter that makes any sklearn-compatible estimator satisfy BaseModelWrapper. Used for all 18 registry models that are not nn/rf/glm/huber.

keyFunctions.name: RegistryModelWrapper.__init__
keyFunctions.signature: __init__(self, estimator, name: str)
keyFunctions.does: Sets self.model = estimator AND self.estimator = estimator (aliases to the same object). Does not record task_type.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: The alias plus pages/06 storing get_model() into fitted_estimators means three references to one mutable fitted estimator live in different state slots.

keyFunctions.name: RegistryModelWrapper.fit
keyFunctions.signature: fit(self, X_train, y_train, X_val=None, y_val=None, **kwargs) -> Dict[str, Any]
keyFunctions.does: The ONLY wrapper that honors kwargs['sample_weight']. Returns {'history': {'val_metric': [v]}, 'best_val_metric': v} — DIFFERENT KEYS from every other wrapper. Infers task type from data with the heuristic `len(np.unique(y_train)) < 20 and y_train.dtype in [np.int64, np.int32, 'int64', 'int32', 'int']`.

keyFunctions.name: RegistryModelWrapper.supports_proba
keyFunctions.signature: supports_proba(self) -> bool
keyFunctions.does: return hasattr(self.model, 'predict_proba') — purely structural, never consults task_type or ModelCapabilities.

modules.purpose: One docstring line, no exports. All imports are deep paths (from models.glm import GLMWrapper).

739 loc. Answer to (b): it is a STATIC dict, DYNAMICALLY REBUILT. get_registry() is a plain function whose body is 22 literal `registry['key'] = ModelSpec(...)` assignments returning a fresh dict on every call. There is NO decorator registration, NO entry-point discovery, NO plugin hook, NO mutable module-level singleton. Instantiation is indirected exactly once, through spec.factory(task_type, random_state).

keyFunctions.name: get_registry
keyFunctions.signature: get_registry() -> Dict[str, ModelSpec]
keyFunctions.does: Builds and returns a NEW dict of 22 ModelSpecs each call: ridge, lasso, elasticnet, logreg, knn_reg, knn_clf, extratrees_reg, extratrees_clf, histgb_reg, histgb_clf, svr, svc, gaussian_nb, lda, nn, glm, huber, rf, xgb_reg, xgb_clf, lgbm_reg, lgbm_clf.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Because it returns a fresh dict, ModelSpec object identity is NOT stable across calls; pages/05, /06 and /07 each wrap it in their own @st.cache_resource, so there are 3 independent cached copies today. TurboTab should make it a module-level frozen mapping.

keyFunctions.name: ModelSpec
keyFunctions.signature: @dataclass ModelSpec: key: str; name: str; group: str; factory: Callable[[str, int], Any]; default_params: Dict[str, Any]; hyperparam_schema: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]; capabilities: ModelCapabilities
keyFunctions.does: NOT frozen; default_params and hyperparam_schema are mutable dicts shared by everyone holding the registry.

keyFunctions.name: ModelCapabilities
keyFunctions.signature: @dataclass ModelCapabilities: supports_regression: bool; supports_classification: bool; supports_predict_proba: bool; supports_partial_dependence: bool; supports_shap: Literal['none','linear','tree','kernel']; requires_scaled_numeric: bool; recommended_for_high_dim: bool; interpretability_tier: Literal['high','medium','low'] = 'medium'; notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list); supports_class_weight: bool = False; supports_sample_weight_balancing: bool = False
keyFunctions.does: The cross-layer contract. requires_scaled_numeric drives per-model preprocessing (pages/05:487,801,847,1059); supports_regression/classification gate the offered model list (pages/05:345, /06:804); supports_shap picks the SHAP explainer (pages/07:263,434); supports_class_weight / supports_sample_weight_balancing gate class balancing (pages/06:1469,1477,1757,1758).

The Router is the natural consumer; it must not trust these three until they are corrected and tested.

keyFunctions.name: _create_nn
keyFunctions.signature: _create_nn(task_type: str, random_state: int)
keyFunctions.does: Imports NNWeightedHuberWrapper INSIDE the function (torch is ~1.1 GB and optional) and returns NNWeightedHuberWrapper(dropout=0.1, task_type=task_type) — i.e. hidden_layers=[128,128,128], loss 'mse'. NOTE: this factory is never reached in production; pages/06 special-cases model_name=='nn' in both _train_models and the Optuna objective and constructs the wrapper directly.

keyFunctions.signature: _create_rf(task_type: str, random_state: int) -> RFWrapper(n_estimators=100, max_depth=None, min_samples_leaf=1, task_type=task_type)
keyFunctions.does: These three factories return BaseModelWrapper instances, not bare sklearn estimators — so spec.factory's return type is heterogeneous (wrapper for nn/glm/huber/rf, raw estimator for the other 18). pages/06 works around it by branching on model_name.

modules.purpose: 527 loc of pure metric/CV/residual functions. Fully stateless — no module globals, no caching, no session_state. The cleanest engine candidate in the domain.

keyFunctions.name: calculate_regression_metrics
keyFunctions.signature: calculate_regression_metrics(y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray) -> Dict[str, float]
keyFunctions.does: Ravels to float, DROPS non-finite pairs with a logging warning, returns all-NaN if fewer than 2 pairs remain, else {'MAE','RMSE','R2','MedianAE'}.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Silently computes on a SUBSET without reporting the surviving n; the UI caption still claims n=len(X_test). Return the effective n.

keyFunctions.name: calculate_classification_metrics
keyFunctions.signature: calculate_classification_metrics(y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray, y_proba: Optional[np.ndarray] = None) -> Dict[str, float]
keyFunctions.does: Always returns Accuracy and F1(average='weighted'). ROC-AUC / LogLoss / PR-AUC are computed inside a try/except with a bare `pass` — on any failure they are simply ABSENT from the dict.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: The bare except means a wrong-shaped y_proba produces a leaderboard silently missing AUC rather than an error. Record the failure reason.

keyFunctions.name: perform_cross_validation
keyFunctions.signature: perform_cross_validation(model: Any, X: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, cv_folds: int = 5, task_type: str = 'regression', scoring: Optional[str] = None, cv_strategy: str = 'standard', groups: Optional[np.ndarray] = None) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]
keyFunctions.does: Matches the fold scheme to the split's leakage semantics: 'group' -> StratifiedGroupKFold/GroupKFold with n_splits clamped to the number of groups, 'time' -> TimeSeriesSplit, else StratifiedKFold/KFold(shuffle=True, random_state=42). Calls cross_val_score(..., n_jobs=-1). Flips sign when 'neg_' in scoring. Returns {'scores','mean','std','folds','strategy'}.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: LONG-RUNNING, no progress, no cancel. n_jobs=-1 is hardcoded — inside a job worker this oversubscribes every core. random_state=42 is hardcoded and ignores the project seed. To observe it, replace cross_val_score with an explicit fold loop emitting per-fold progress and checking cancel between folds.

keyFunctions.name: make_cv_pipeline
keyFunctions.signature: make_cv_pipeline(preprocessing, estimator)
keyFunctions.does: Returns Pipeline([('prep', clone(preprocessing)), ('densify', FunctionTransformer(_to_dense)), ('est', estimator)]) so preprocessing is re-fit inside every fold.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: This is the leakage-prevention invariant made executable. Do not let a refactor 'optimize' it into scoring a pre-transformed matrix.

keyFunctions.name: _to_dense
keyFunctions.signature: _to_dense(A)
keyFunctions.does: Named module-level densifier so the pipeline stays picklable under n_jobs=-1.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Exists ONLY because of joblib pickling. If jobs move to a different executor, keep it named anyway.

keyFunctions.signature: analyze_residuals_extended(y_true, y_pred) -> Dict[str, Any]

keyFunctions.does: Equal-frequency bins (deduped), per-bin mae/rmse/mean_bias/n and a bias_direction label using the |mean_bias| > 0.1*mae rule. Returns {'bins', 'overall_bias_direction'}.

keyFunctions.signature: compare_models_paired_cv(model_names: List[str], model_results: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]], task_type: str = 'regression') -> Dict[Tuple[str, str], Dict[str, Any]]

modules.purpose: 263 loc. Answer to (d) for CIs: BCa bootstrap, STATELESS and DETERMINISTIC — a local np.random.RandomState(random_state) is the only randomness, no global RNG is touched, no caching, no module state. The statefulness problem is elsewhere (call sites choosing seeds/resample counts).

keyFunctions.name: BootstrapResult
keyFunctions.signature: @dataclass BootstrapResult: estimate: float; ci_lower: float; ci_upper: float; ci_level: float; n_resamples: int; metric_name: str
keyFunctions.does: Carries the CI. __str__ gives 'est [lo, hi]' at 4dp.

keyFunctions.name: BootstrapResult.to_dict
keyFunctions.signature: to_dict(self)
keyFunctions.does: Returns ONLY {'estimate','ci_lower','ci_upper','ci_level','formatted'} — DROPS n_resamples and metric_name, and there is NO from_dict.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: The Record layer needs round-trippable uncertainty. Add from_dict and stop dropping n_resamples (it is the audit trail for how many resamples were degenerate).

keyFunctions.name: bootstrap_metric
keyFunctions.signature: bootstrap_metric(y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray, metric_fn: Callable, n_resamples: int = 1000, ci_level: float = 0.95, metric_name: str = 'metric', random_state: int = 42, y_proba: Optional[np.ndarray] = None) -> BootstrapResult
keyFunctions.does: pred_input = y_proba if given else y_pred. Computes the point estimate (returns all-NaN result on exception), then n_resamples resamples leaving degenerate ones as NaN and DROPPING them (deliberate: substitution would narrow the interval). Bails to NaN CI if fewer than max(50, n_resamples//2) valid replicates survive. Then a jackknife CAPPED at n_jack = min(n, 200) and BCa.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: LONG-RUNNING (~1200 metric evaluations per metric at defaults), a plain Python for-loop, no progress, no cancel. It is trivially instrumentable: add an optional on_progress(i, n_resamples) inside both loops and a cancel check every ~50 iterations. Do not change random_state semantics — published CIs are keyed to it.

landmines.what: SklearnCompatibleNNRegressor.fit() and SklearnCompatibleNNClassifier.fit() do not train. They set is_fitted_=True, record n_features_in_ (and classes_), and return self. Any sklearn utility that refits will 'succeed' using the already-trained network.
landmines.where: models/nn_whuber.py:115-128 (regressor) and 174-188 (classifier); reachable through NNWeightedHuberWrapper.get_model() (line 577-582) and get_sklearn_estimator() (561-575). Currently fenced off by two string comparisons: pages/06_Train_and_Compare.py:1529 (`model_name != 'nn'`) and pages/08_Sensitivity_Analysis.py:121.
landmines.silentFailure: Feed the shim to cross_val_score / GridSearchCV / RFECV / CalibratedClassifierCV / learning_curve and every fold returns predictions from a model fitted on the full dataset. No exception, no warning — just uniformly excellent CV scores that get written into the manuscript. sklearn's clone() makes it worse: clone reconstructs from get_params() (which reports only wrapper_instance), so is_fitted_ resets to False, fit() flips it back to True without training, and predictions still come from the original network.
landmines.mitigation: Before moving anything: write a test that asserts SklearnCompatibleNNRegressor(wrapper).fit(X, y) does NOT change the network's parameters. Then rename the class PredictOnlyAdapter, make fit() raise NotImplementedError, and give it a marker attribute the jobs layer checks — replace the two `model_name != 'nn'` string guards with `not isinstance(est, PredictOnlyAdapter)`. Keep permutation_importance working (it never refits) by leaving predict/predict_proba intact.

landmines.what: Three disagreeing sources of truth for Random Forest and Neural Network defaults. RF: RFWrapper.__init__ says n_estimators=500/min_samples_leaf=10; ModelConfig says 500/10; ml/model_registry._create_rf says 100/1 and registry['rf'].default_params says 100/1. NN architecture: NNWeightedHuberWrapper.__init__ defaults to [128,128,128]; registry['nn'].default_params says num_layers=3, layer_width=128; but pages/06:1351-1352 and 1153-1154 fall back to `params.get('num_layers', 2)` and `params.get('layer_width', 32)` — a [32,32] network.
landmines.where: models/rf.py:12-13; utils/session_state.py:96-98 (ModelConfig); ml/model_registry.py:142 (_create_rf) and 594 (default_params). models/nn_whuber.py:253; ml/model_registry.py:512-513; pages/06_Train_and_Compare.py:1351-1352, 1153-1154, 1410-1412 (which reads model_config.rf_*, i.e. 500/10, NOT the registry's 100/1).
landmines.silentFailure: Consolidating on 'the registry' — the obviously correct engine choice — changes RF from 500 trees / min_leaf 10 to 100 trees / min_leaf 1, and changes the untuned NN from [32,32] to [128,128,128]. Both still train, both still report metrics, and every previously published number shifts. Nobody will suspect the defaults; they will suspect the migration broke the data.
landmines.mitigation: Before consolidating, run every registry model on a fixed dataset and snapshot the exact constructor kwargs and the resulting metrics to a golden file. Then pick ONE source, and diff against the golden file — accept the deltas explicitly, in writing, or reproduce the old defaults exactly in the registry.

landmines.what: Each wrapper returns a differently-shaped training result, and the regression-named keys hold classification values. NN: {'history': {'train_loss','val_loss','val_rmse','val_accuracy'}, 'best_val_rmse', 'best_val_accuracy'}. GLM/Huber/RF: {'history': {'val_rmse': [v]}, 'best_val_rmse': v} where for CLASSIFICATION v is accuracy stored under the name val_rmse. RegistryModelWrapper: {'history': {'val_metric': [v]}, 'best_val_metric': v} — a different key entirely.
landmines.where: models/nn_whuber.py:432-437 and 551-555; models/glm.py:44-47; models/huber_glm.py:39-42; models/rf.py:64-67; models/registry_wrappers.py:51-54. Consumed at pages/06:1572 (`results.get('history', {})`) and rendered by visualizations.py:12 plot_training_history, which bare-subscripts history['train_loss'], ['val_loss'] and ['val_rmse'].
landmines.silentFailure: Two ways. (1) Any generic 'lower is better' ranking on best_val_rmse silently INVERTS for classification, picking the worst model. (2) A TurboTab feed that renders learning curves uniformly KeyErrors on all 21 non-NN models — currently masked only by the `if name == 'nn'` guard at pages/06:2586. The mislabeling is currently harmless only because best_val_* has ZERO consumers anywhere in the codebase — verified by grep; the moment the Router starts ranking on it, it breaks.
landmines.mitigation: Define one TrainResult TypedDict now: {history: {metric_name: [values]}, best: {metric_name: value}, epochs_run: int, task_type: str} with metric names that state what they are. Write a parametrized test that constructs every wrapper for both task types and asserts the exact returned keys — that test does not exist today and is the single highest-value test in this domain.

landmines.what: task_type_final and data_config.task_type can diverge (the user's task-type override), and the training loop mixes them. y_test_proba is assigned only in the classification branch but read unconditionally when data_config.task_type == 'classification'.
landmines.where: pages/06_Train_and_Compare.py:161 (`task_type_final = task_type_detection.final if task_type_detection.final else data_config.task_type`; TaskTypeDetection.final returns override_value when override_enabled, utils/session_state.py:22-27). Assignment at 1502 under `task_type_final == 'classification'`; read at 1575 under `data_config.task_type == 'classification'`; and perform_cross_validation is called at 1558 with `task_type=data_config.task_type` while everything else uses task_type_final.
landmines.silentFailure: Three distinct failures. (a) override=regression + config=classification: UnboundLocalError on y_test_proba at line 1575, swallowed by the broad `except Exception` at 1605 into a red 'Training failed' box that names a variable, not the cause. (b) override=classification + config=regression: probabilities ARE computed then discarded as None, so ROC/PR at line 2722-2730 does `y_proba[:, 1]` on None. (c) CV silently picks the wrong scorer and fold strategy (StratifiedKFold on a continuous target), fails, and is swallowed at 1562 into 'Cross-validation failed... Skipping CV' — the user just loses CV and never learns why. Additionally, because y_test_proba is a function-scope local reused across loop iterations, a stale value from a previous model can be written into a later model's results.
landmines.mitigation: Resolve task_type ONCE at the top of the engine's train function, pass it as a parameter, and never read data_config.task_type below that point. Initialize y_test_proba = None before the branch. Add a test that sets override_enabled=True with an opposing override_value and asserts training completes and CV runs.

landmines.what: The 'Cancel Training' button is decorative — st.session_state.cancel_training is written and NEVER read anywhere in the codebase.
landmines.where: pages/06_Train_and_Compare.py:1252-1253 (init), 1263-1264 (set to True). grep for 'cancel_training' across the whole repo returns only these lines plus the button key. No file in models/ or ml/ contains any cancel, abort, stop, or interrupt hook.
landmines.silentFailure: Users believe long runs are cancellable. They are not — the flag is set and the loop never consults it. Migrating the training loop verbatim into a job worker carries the illusion forward: the job API will expose a cancel() that appears wired (the flag exists!) but cannot interrupt anything.
landmines.mitigation: Treat cancellation as NEW code, not a port. Thread `should_cancel: Callable[[], bool]` into (1) NNWeightedHuberWrapper.fit — check per epoch AND per batch; (2) the bootstrap_metric resample and jackknife loops — check every ~50 iterations; (3) the Optuna callback at pages/06:1227 — call study.stop(); (4) perform_cross_validation — requires replacing cross_val_score with an explicit fold loop. Nothing else in the domain can be interrupted at all.

landmines.what: NNWeightedHuberWrapper.fit mutates PROCESS-GLOBAL RNG state, and RandomForest / cross_val_score hardcode n_jobs=-1.
landmines.where: models/nn_whuber.py:313-317 — `torch.manual_seed(random_seed)`, `np.random.seed(random_seed)`, `torch.cuda.manual_seed(random_seed)`. models/rf.py:34 and 42 (`n_jobs=-1`); ml/eval.py:161 (`cross_val_score(..., n_jobs=-1)`). Also models/nn_whuber.py:259 fixes self.device at CONSTRUCTION time from torch.cuda.is_available().
landmines.silentFailure: Under a job queue running two trainings concurrently, np.random.seed from job B silently reseeds the global numpy RNG that job A's sklearn estimators (any without an explicit random_state) are drawing from — results become non-reproducible in a way that only shows up as small metric drift between identical runs. Separately, n_jobs=-1 inside N concurrent workers spawns N x cores threads; the symptom is a machine that thrashes and a job that 'hangs', not an error. torch.cuda.manual_seed (not manual_seed_all) leaves multi-GPU nondeterministic.
landmines.mitigation: Replace the global seeding with a local torch.Generator passed to the DataLoader plus np.random.default_rng(seed) for any numpy draws, before any concurrency exists. Make n_jobs a parameter defaulting to 1 inside workers. Pin the current behavior first: a test that fits an NN twice with the same random_seed and asserts identical predictions, and a second asserting a different seed gives different predictions.

landmines.what: Bootstrap CIs and baselines ignore the project seed and disagree on resample count. Every call site takes bootstrap's random_state=42 default while models are trained with st.session_state['random_seed'], and page 06 uses n_resamples=1000 while page 07 uses 500 for the same conceptual quantity.
landmines.where: pages/06:2046 and 2067 call bootstrap_all_*_metrics with no random_state; pages/06:2135-2139 calls train_baseline_models with no random_state (so its LogisticRegression is seeded 42 regardless of the project); ml/baseline_models.py:56 and 132 pass their own default through. pages/07_Explainability.py:1156-1158 uses n_resamples=500 against page 06's 1000.
landmines.silentFailure: A user changes the project seed to 7, reruns everything, and the CIs are byte-identical — they will reasonably conclude the CIs are stable when in fact they were never reseeded. And the external-validation CIs in the manuscript are computed from half as many resamples as the internal ones, with no annotation anywhere.
landmines.mitigation: Thread Project.seed and a single Project.n_bootstrap through every call site, and record both in the Record next to each interval. If you change the effective seed, expect every published interval to shift — snapshot the current intervals to a golden file first.

landmines.what: ModelCapabilities.supports_predict_proba is never read by any code, and its declared values are wrong for the four task-dual models.
landmines.where: ml/model_registry.py — registry['nn'] (line 536), registry['glm'] (557) and registry['rf'] (604) all declare supports_predict_proba=True, but for a REGRESSION task the corresponding wrapper's supports_proba() returns False (models/nn_whuber.py:636-638, models/glm.py:63-65, models/rf.py:95-97). grep across the entire repo finds zero consumers of supports_predict_proba. Same for recommended_for_high_dim and interpretability_tier.
landmines.silentFailure: The Router is exactly the component that would naturally read declarative capability metadata to decide which question to ask next. If it consults supports_predict_proba it will offer calibration, ROC curves, and decision-curve analysis for regression models — the branches then call predict_proba, get None back (base default, no exception), and render an empty or crashed panel. The metadata LOOKS authoritative because 8 sibling fields on the same dataclass are load-bearing.
landmines.mitigation: Either delete supports_predict_proba, recommended_for_high_dim and interpretability_tier, or make them task-parameterized (supports_predict_proba(task_type) -> bool) and add a test that asserts, for every registry key and both task types, that the declared capability equals the constructed wrapper's runtime supports_proba(). That test will fail today for nn, glm and rf — which is the point.

landmines.what: Baselines are transformed through whichever model's preprocessing pipeline happens to have been trained FIRST.
landmines.where: pages/06_Train_and_Compare.py:2122-2124 — `first_model = list(st.session_state.get('fitted_preprocessing_pipelines', {}).keys())` then `pipe = st.session_state['fitted_preprocessing_pipelines'][first_model[0]]`. Because pipelines are per-model (requires_scaled_numeric differs), the baseline's feature space depends on dict insertion order. The transform is wrapped in a bare try/except that falls back to np.array(X_train_base) — the raw, untransformed frame.
landmines.silentFailure: Train {ridge, rf} and the baselines run on a scaled/imputed matrix; train {rf, ridge} and they run on an unscaled one. The LinearRegression baseline's R2 changes, so the headline claim 'our model beats the linear baseline by X' changes — with no indication that anything about the baseline moved. If the transform raises (a pipeline expecting engineered columns), the except swallows it and the baseline silently trains on raw data that may contain NaNs or strings.
landmines.mitigation: Give baselines their OWN explicit pipeline (scaled numeric + simple imputation) recorded in the Record, independent of any user model. Remove the bare except or make it record a visible failure. Pin current baseline metrics before changing this.

landmines.what: The 'slow model' cost model keys off strings that are not registry keys, so the warning is wrong for the models that need it.
landmines.where: pages/06_Train_and_Compare.py:1248 — `slow_models = {'nn', 'extratrees', 'svc', 'svr'}`. The registry has NO key 'extratrees'; it has 'extratrees_reg' and 'extratrees_clf' (ml/model_registry.py:322, 345). It also omits 'svc'/'svr' siblings correctly but misses xgb/lgbm/histgb entirely, and SVC is built with probability=True (ml/model_registry.py:108), which forces an internal 5-fold Platt calibration.
landmines.silentFailure: ExtraTrees never triggers the slow-model warning or the cancel affordance, so a multi-minute run presents with no warning at all. Ported into a jobs layer as a duration estimator, this becomes wrong ETAs and wrong queue priorities — plausible-looking numbers that nobody validates.
landmines.mitigation: Move cost class onto ModelSpec as an explicit field (cheap/moderate/expensive) so it is impossible to key off a string that does not exist, and assert in a test that every cost-class reference resolves to a real registry key.

landmines.what: RegistryModelWrapper re-derives the task type from the data with a fragile heuristic instead of being told, and it is the only wrapper honoring sample_weight.
landmines.where: models/registry_wrappers.py:44 — `if len(np.unique(y_train)) < 20 and y_train.dtype in [np.int64, np.int32, 'int64', 'int32', 'int']`. Its fit is also the only one reading kwargs['sample_weight'] (line 32-36); pages/06:1477-1480 relies on that for XGBoost class balancing.
landmines.silentFailure: A regression target that is integer-valued with under 20 distinct levels (ordinal scores, counts, Likert sums — common in the clinical datasets this app targets) is scored as ACCURACY and reported under 'val_metric'. Conversely a float-encoded class label is scored as RMSE. Nothing errors. The value lands in a history key nobody currently reads, which is exactly why it has survived — it becomes live the moment the Router or the feed starts reading history generically. Separately, routing rf/glm/huber through RegistryModelWrapper during consolidation would silently DROP their sample_weight support, since RFWrapper/GLMWrapper/HuberGLMWrapper ignore **kwargs entirely.
landmines.mitigation: Pass task_type into RegistryModelWrapper.__init__ from the registry key and delete the heuristic. Before consolidating wrappers, add a test asserting class-weight balancing actually reaches the estimator for every key where capabilities.supports_class_weight or supports_sample_weight_balancing is True.

landmines.what: BCa acceleration is computed from a jackknife that is capped at 200 leave-one-out replicates and then PADDED to length n with the mean of those 200.
landmines.where: ml/bootstrap.py:152-166 — `n_jack = min(n, 200)`, `jack_stats = np.full(n, np.nan)`, the loop runs only `for i in range(n_jack)`, then `jack_stats[~np.isfinite(jack_stats)] = jack_fill` fills all n - 200 remaining slots with nanmean of the computed ones, and the full length-n array is passed to _bca_ci as jackknife_stats.
landmines.silentFailure: For n > 200 the acceleration term a is computed over an array whose tail is constant, shrinking both the third and second moments in a way that depends on n. The intervals are still produced, still look reasonable, and are still labeled 'BCa' — but the acceleration correction is progressively damped as the test set grows. Any refactor that 'fixes' this (uncapping the jackknife, or passing only the 200 computed values) CHANGES EVERY PUBLISHED INTERVAL WIDTH, and the change will be attributed to the migration rather than to a deliberate statistical correction.
landmines.mitigation: Do not touch this during the move. Snapshot BootstrapResult values for a fixed (y_true, y_pred, seed) with n well above 200 into a golden file, port byte-identically, verify the golden file passes, and only then open a separate, explicitly-reviewed change to the jackknife with before/after interval widths documented.

landmines.what: The weighted_huber emphasis window is derived during fit and stored only on the instance as _whuber_t0 / _whuber_s, with legacy glucose constants (t0=180.0, s=20.0) as the getattr fallback.
landmines.where: models/nn_whuber.py:376-378 sets them only in the `elif self.loss_function == 'weighted_huber'` branch; lines 459-461 and 494-496 read them via `getattr(self, '_whuber_t0', 180.0)` / `getattr(self, '_whuber_s', 20.0)`. They appear in NEITHER get_architecture_summary() (line 265-275) nor anywhere in provenance.
landmines.silentFailure: The fallbacks are silent by construction — getattr with a default never raises. Any path that reconstructs the wrapper from recorded config and refits (a Job retry, a sensitivity re-run, a reproducibility check) that fails to re-enter the weighted_huber branch trains against a Gaussian window centered at 180 with width 20 on a target that may live in [0,1]. The weight collapses to a near-constant 1.0, so it degrades to plain Huber and simply performs slightly worse — no error, no warning, and the manuscript still claims a weighted loss was used.
landmines.mitigation: Compute t0/s in __init__ or make them explicit constructor parameters, include them in get_architecture_summary(), and record them in the Record. Delete the 180.0/20.0 getattr defaults so the failure becomes an AttributeError instead of a silent wrong answer.

landmines.what: NN classification silently remaps unseen validation classes to index 0, and models/base, glm, huber_glm, rf and registry_wrappers have literally zero test coverage.
landmines.where: models/nn_whuber.py:337 — `y_val_mapped = np.array([class_to_idx.get(cls, 0) for cls in y_val])` (note: the TRAIN mapping at line 327 uses class_to_idx[cls] and would KeyError, but validation uses .get with a 0 default). Coverage: grep across tests/ and scripts/ shows models.glm and models.rf appear ONLY in scripts/smoke_check.py:140-147 as bare import checks; models.base, models.huber_glm and models.registry_wrappers appear nowhere. (nn_whuber IS covered by tests/test_nn_modernization.py via function-scope imports, which a static import graph misses.)
landmines.silentFailure: A stratified split that leaves a rare class out of training maps every such validation row to the FIRST class. Validation accuracy is computed against those fabricated labels, early stopping optimizes against them, and the selected 'best' epoch is chosen on corrupted signal. Meanwhile, with no tests on the other five wrapper files, ANY behavioral change made during the move — the RF duplicate-method deletion, a shared base-class refactor, normalizing the fit() return shape — lands with nothing to catch it.
landmines.mitigation: WHAT A MIGRATION SUITE MUST PIN FIRST, in order: (1) for every one of the 22 registry keys and both task types, construct via spec.factory and assert the exact constructor kwargs — this is the defense against landmine 2; (2) fit each wrapper on a fixed tiny dataset and snapshot predict() shape, dtype, and for classification that predict() returns ORIGINAL class labels (models/nn_whuber.py:604-605 maps back through self.classes_ — nothing else does); (3) assert the exact keys of every fit() return dict (landmine 3); (4) assert supports_proba() equals the declared capability for every key/task pair (landmine 8); (5) assert predict()/predict_proba() raise ValueError before fit; (6) assert SklearnCompatibleNN*.fit does not alter network parameters (landmine 1); (7) golden-file the BootstrapResult values for n>200 (landmine 12); (8) same-seed-same-predictions and different-seed-different-predictions for the NN (landmine 6). Raise the unseen-class mapping to an explicit error or a recorded warning as part of (2).

domain:
Feature engineering, feature selection, preprocessing pipelines, and splits (ml/pipeline.py, ml/feature_steps.py, ml/preprocess_operators.py, ml/feature_selection.py, ml/splits.py, ml/compat.py, ml/estimator_utils.py, plus the state + page code that owns them: utils/session_state.py, utils/test_lockbox.py, pages/03/04/05/06, ml/eval.py CV composition)

VERDICT ON THE CRITICAL QUESTION — per-model vs global pipeline:
PER-MODEL IS REAL IN THE DATA MODEL. It is not a UI gap and it is not a shared-pipeline flaw on the mainline path. The full chain is per-model, end to end:
  - build: pages/05_Preprocess.py:870 `for model_key in model_keys:` -> 974 `pipeline = build_preprocessing_pipeline(...)` -> 1005 `pipelines_by_model[model_key] = pipeline`
  - store: utils/session_state.py:463 `def set_preprocessing_pipelines(pipelines_by_model: Dict[str, Pipeline], configs_by_model: Dict[str, Any], base_config: Dict[str, Any])` -> `st.session_state.preprocessing_pipelines_by_model = pipelines_by_model`
  - read: utils/session_state.py:448 `def get_preprocessing_pipeline(model_key: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[Pipeline]` -> returns `pipelines[model_key]` when present
  - train: pages/06_Train_and_Compare.py:1286 `model_pipeline = get_preprocessing_pipeline(model_name) or pipeline` then 1312 `model_pipeline.fit(X_train)`; 1596 `fitted_preprocessing_pipelines[model_name] = model_pipeline`
  - config forking is genuine: 05:845 `apply_model_requirements()` upgrades `numeric_scaling` to 'standard' when `spec.capabilities.requires_scaled_numeric`; RF keeps 'none'. tests/workflow/test_per_model_pipelines.py::test_ridge_and_rf_get_different_training_data asserts the transformed matrices actually differ.
So AnalysisProject MUST have per-model pipeline slots. A single global slot is a regression.

BUT the warning the UI shows is ALSO literally true, and it describes a REAL DATA-MODEL FLAW in the FALLBACK path, not in the mainline:
  1. utils/session_state.py:468 `default_pipeline = pipelines_by_model.get('default') or next(iter(pipelines_by_model.values()), None)` — the "global" `preprocessing_pipeline` is set to an ARBITRARY member of the per-model dict, chosen by dict insertion order. Insertion order comes from pages/05:816 `_sel = [k.replace("train_model_","") for k,v in st.session_state.items() if k.startswith("train_model_") and v]` — i.e. session_state key insertion order, which is checkbox-render order. If RF was checked first, RF's pipeline literally becomes the global default.
  2. pages/06:1286 `get_preprocessing_pipeline(model_name) or pipeline` silently falls back to that arbitrary pipeline for any model the user selects in Train & Compare but did NOT configure in Preprocess. The model then trains under another model's log/power/PCA/KMeans/scaling choices, with only a small "⚠️ No pipeline" badge (06:896) as warning.
  3. It is worse than "shared config": it is a SHARED OBJECT. `get_preprocessing_pipeline` returns the same Pipeline instance stored in `preprocessing_pipelines_by_model`, and 06:1312 `model_pipeline.fit(X_train)` mutates it in place. `fitted_preprocessing_pipelines[A]` and `[B]` then alias one object.
So: the model is per-model; the DEFAULT/FALLBACK SLOT is the flaw. Fix in the rebuild = drop the global slot entirely; make pipeline resolution total (every selected model gets an explicit pipeline, auto-derived from its registry capabilities if the user never opened its panel) and make it a VALUE, not a shared reference.

SPLITS: built inline in pages/06_Train_and_Compare.py:349-720 (the "Prepare Splits" button). Four mutually exclusive branches, in priority order: (a) group/GroupShuffleSplit when `cohort_structure_detection.final=='longitudinal'` and an entity id exists; (b) chronological sort-and-slice when `split_config.use_time_split` and `data_config.datetime_col`; (c) LOCKBOX branch — the frozen test labels ARE the test set, only train/val are drawn (06:552-582); (d) plain/stratified train_test_split. There is no `ml/splits.py` split function — ml/splits.py contains ONE helper, `to_numpy_1d`. This whole block is unextracted, untested engine logic living in a Streamlit page.

LEAKAGE PREVENTION (four independent mechanisms, all real):
  1. Test lockbox (utils/test_lockbox.py): row LABELS frozen at upload before FE/FS can see them; `train_row_mask(index)` gates target-aware steps; page 04 uses it (04:128), page 03 uses it for PCA/UMAP/binning/scaler fits (03:637,775,910,954).
  2. Pipelines are configured but NOT fitted at Preprocess time on the mainline — they are re-fit on X_train at 06:1312, then only `.transform()` on val/test.
  3. CV re-fits preprocessing inside every fold: ml/eval.py:182 `make_cv_pipeline(preprocessing, estimator)` clones the preprocessing and composes it with the estimator so `cross_val_score` sees raw training rows.
  4. CV fold scheme mirrors split semantics: `st.session_state['cv_strategy']` in {'standard','group','time'} set at split time (06:496,507,528), consumed by `perform_cross_validation(..., cv_strategy=, groups=)`.
All four have silent-failure modes documented in landmines.

ml/compat.py RECONCILES NOTHING ABOUT THIS DOMAIN. Despite the name it is unrelated to pipeline/column reconciliation. It is a single monkeypatch, `patch_gtda_for_sklearn()`, that rewrites giotto-tda's imported `check_array` reference to translate the `force_all_finite` kwarg (removed in sklearn 1.8) to `ensure_all_finite`. Called from exactly one place: pages/03_Feature_Engineering.py:764, immediately before importing gtda for TDA features. The column-reconciliation function the name suggests is `ml/pipeline.py:504 reconcile_pipeline_columns(pipe, available_columns)`.

modules.purpose: The preprocessing pipeline builder (557 loc). Constructs sklearn Pipeline(ColumnTransformer) per model, plus unit-harmonization/plausibility config builders, a human-readable recipe renderer used by the manuscript, feature-name recovery, and a self-healing column reconciler. ZERO streamlit imports — already pure.

keyFunctions.signature: class PlausibilityGate(BaseEstimator, TransformerMixin): def __init__(self, lower_bounds: Sequence[Optional[float]], upper_bounds: Sequence[Optional[float]]); fit(X, y=None) -> self; transform(X) -> np.ndarray

keyFunctions.transitionNote: Two defects: (1) `self.params = params or {}` — when params is None or {} the stored dict is a DIFFERENT object than the one passed, so clone() raises RuntimeError (only bites when the caller omits params, which build_preprocessing_pipeline does via `params or {}` when a treatment is set with no params). keyFunctions.does: Per-feature pearsonr (regression) / spearmanr (classification) then statsmodels multipletests for FDR-BH or Bonferroni.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Uses spearmanr against integer class labels for classification — a rank correlation on nominal classes is not a valid screen for multiclass. Also its NaN mask expression `np.issubdtype(type(xi[0]) if len(xi) > 0 else float, np.floating)` silently disables NaN masking for integer feature columns.

keyFunctions.signature: stability_selection(X: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, feature_names: List[str], task_type: str = 'regression', n_bootstrap: int = 100, threshold: float = 0.6, sample_fraction: float = 0.5, random_state: int = 42) -> FeatureSelectionResult
keyFunctions.does: Meinshausen-Buhlmann: fits Lasso(alpha=0.01) or L1-LogisticRegression(C=100) on 100 random half-samples, selects features with selection probability >= threshold.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: HARD-CODED alpha=0.01 on UNSCALED inputs (page 04 only median-imputes, never scales). Selection probability then depends on each feature's raw measurement unit. Bare `except Exception: continue` swallows every failed bootstrap, so a systematically failing fit reports selection_prob=0 rather than an error. Requires X to be a numpy array (`X[idx]` fancy indexing) — a DataFrame silently misbehaves.

keyFunctions.transitionNote: Methodologically correct. Wrapped in `except Exception as cv_error: st.warning(f'Cross-validation failed for {model_name}: {cv_error}. Skipping CV.')` — so any clone failure degrades to no-CV with a transient banner and a fully-populated results table.

modules.purpose: 513 loc. Drives ml/feature_selection.py and is the ONLY consumer of consensus_features. Correctly quarantines the lockbox.

keyFunctions.signature: pages/04_Feature_Selection.py:126-153

Non-numeric features are silently excluded from ranking entirely (04:110) though they remain in the model.

keyFunctions.signature: pages/04_Feature_Selection.py:202-313

modules.purpose: ~1330 loc. Creates engineered columns and writes df_engineered. Fits stateful transforms on lockbox training rows only (correctly), but stores NO reusable transformer.

keyFunctions.name: _build_transform_map
keyFunctions.signature: _build_transform_map(engineered_features, engineering_log) -> Dict[str, str]  [03:26]

keyFunctions.name: [lockbox-aware stateful fits]
keyFunctions.signature: pages/03_Feature_Engineering.py:637-651 (KBinsDiscretizer), 775-782 (StandardScaler), 909-913 (PCA), 954-960 (UMAP)

keyFunctions.name: [Save Engineered Features button body]

modules.purpose: Only the two CV-composition functions are in this domain. Zero streamlit.

keyFunctions.name: make_cv_pipeline
keyFunctions.signature: make_cv_pipeline(preprocessing, estimator) -> Pipeline
keyFunctions.does: `Pipeline([('prep', clone(preprocessing)), ('densify', FunctionTransformer(_to_dense)), ('est', estimator)])`. Docstring: 'Cross-validating this composite on raw training data re-fits the preprocessing inside every fold, so no fold's held-out rows contribute to imputer/scaler/encoder/PCA statistics.'
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Correct and load-bearing. Its dependence on clone() is what makes the PlausibilityGate clone break silently disable CV. _to_dense is a module-level named function specifically so it stays picklable for n_jobs=-1 — do not inline it into a lambda during the port.

keyFunctions.name: perform_cross_validation
keyFunctions.signature: perform_cross_validation(model: Any, X: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, cv_folds: int = 5, task_type: str = 'regression', scoring: Optional[str] = None, cv_strategy: str = 'standard', groups: Optional[np.ndarray] = None) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]
keyFunctions.does: Selects the fold scheme to match split semantics: 'group' -> StratifiedGroupKFold (classification, with GroupKFold fallback on ImportError) capped at n_groups folds; 'time' -> TimeSeriesSplit; else StratifiedKFold/KFold(shuffle=True, random_state=42). Returns {'scores','mean','std','folds','strategy'}.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: The random_state=42 for the standard KFold is HARD-CODED and ignores project random_seed — CV folds do not follow the seed the manuscript reports.

modules.purpose: Legacy data utilities. Two functions matter here: the numeric-column definition every pipeline depends on, and a fully parallel split-and-scale path.

keyFunctions.name: get_numeric_columns
keyFunctions.signature: get_numeric_columns(df: pd.DataFrame) -> List[str]

keyFunctions.transitionNote: The 'at least one non-null' filter is data-dependent: a column that is all-NaN within an active cohort is reclassified from numeric to CATEGORICAL (05:111-112 puts everything not in numeric_cols into categorical_features), so it silently gets one-hot encoded instead of imputed+scaled. Cohort runs can therefore produce structurally different pipelines for the same nominal config.

modules.purpose: Two analyses that re-fit this domain's pipelines: seed sensitivity and feature dropout. Both call sklearn clone() on the stored pipeline.

keyFunctions.name: [seed sensitivity loop]
keyFunctions.signature: pages/08_Sensitivity_Analysis.py:110-215
keyFunctions.does: Pools X_train+X_val+X_test back together, re-splits with each seed, then `_pipe_seed = clone(pipeline); _pipe_seed.fit(X_tr_raw)` per seed. Correctly re-fits preprocessing per split.

keyFunctions.name: [feature dropout loop]
keyFunctions.signature: pages/08_Sensitivity_Analysis.py:383-470
keyFunctions.does: Neutralizes each feature to its training median/mode, `_pipe_abl = clone(pipeline); _pipe_abl.fit(X_tr_abl)`, retrains, measures degradation. The comment documents two previously-fixed bugs (cloning the wrapper not the estimator; comparing a pipeline-transformed baseline against raw retrains).

modules.purpose: Borderline for this domain: the coach's evidence probe builds its OWN parallel preprocessing (impute + scale) rather than reusing the configured pipeline.

keyFunctions.name: _prepare
keyFunctions.signature: _prepare(X, y, task_type, rng) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, List[str], bool]

Because the probe verdict steers which models the router will recommend, an optimistically biased probe score becomes a routing decision. Mark it as a probe, not a measurement, in Record.

keyFunctions.signature: _linear_pipeline(task_type, wide: bool = False) -> Pipeline
