landmines.what: apply_plausibility_filter calls reset_index(drop=True), and its output becomes the app's active dataframe — which silently voids the test lockbox for every downstream step.
landmines.where: ml/pipeline.py:124 `return df.loc[mask].reset_index(drop=True)` -> pages/05_Preprocess.py:863 `st.session_state['filtered_data'] = filtered_df` -> utils/session_state.py:211-212 get_data() returns filtered_data ahead of raw_data -> utils/test_lockbox.py:237 train_row_mask(index) and pages/06:401 `is_test_row = np.array([lbl in _test_label_set for lbl in orig_labels])`.
landmines.silentFailure: The lockbox stores index LABELS precisely so membership survives row filtering — its module docstring (test_lockbox.py:16-17) states: 'stores index LABELS (not positions) so membership survives feature engineering and row filtering, which preserve the original index.' apply_plausibility_filter is the one filter that does NOT preserve it. After enabling plausibility_mode='filter', the frozen labels are matched against a fresh 0..n-1 RangeIndex, so `is_test_row` selects an arbitrary, wrong set of rows. If enough rows happen to match, pages/06:411 does not trip its `< 2 / < 4` guard and the run proceeds with a test set that is not the quarantined one — while every UI chip and the exported manuscript still say 'held out since upload, never seen by feature engineering or selection'. Feature selection at pages/04:128 is simultaneously quarantining the wrong rows. Nothing errors. Related second-order bug: if df_engineered exists, get_data() never looks at filtered_data at all, so plausibility 'filter' mode silently does nothing after Feature Engineering.
landmines.mitigation: Change apply_plausibility_filter to `return df.loc[mask]` (labels intact) or, better, return the boolean mask and let the Project apply it. Then add an assertion at the lockbox boundary: `matched = len(set(lockbox['labels']) & set(df.index)); if matched < 0.8 * lockbox['n_test']: raise`. In the rebuild, key the lockbox on an explicit immutable row-id column materialized at upload rather than on the pandas index — the index is a shared mutable resource that ~30 call sites can reset.

landmines.what: PlausibilityGate cannot be sklearn-cloned. It mutates its constructor parameters in __init__, violating the sklearn clone identity contract — and reconcile_pipeline_columns clones UNCONDITIONALLY on every training run.
landmines.where: ml/preprocess_operators.py:50-55 `self.lower_bounds = np.array([np.nan if v is None else float(v) for v in lower_bounds], dtype=float)`. Clone sites: ml/pipeline.py:531/534/553 (inside reconcile_pipeline_columns, called at pages/06:1299 every run), ml/eval.py:190-194 (make_cv_pipeline), pages/08_Sensitivity_Analysis.py:163 and :447.
landmines.silentFailure: sklearn.base.clone reads get_params(), deep-copies each value, reconstructs the class, then asserts `param_new is param_old` and raises RuntimeError('Cannot clone object ... as the constructor either does not set or modifies parameter lower_bounds'). PlausibilityGate's __init__ builds a NEW array from whatever it is handed, so the identity check always fails. Consequences, all silent: (1) CROSS-VALIDATION IS SILENTLY DISABLED — pages/06:1561 catches it as `st.warning(f'Cross-validation failed for {model_name}: {cv_error}. Skipping CV.')`, a transient banner, while the results table and the manuscript render complete without CV; (2) SEED SENSITIVITY RETURNS ALL NaN — pages/08:211 appends `{'seed': seed, primary_metric: nan, '_error': str(e)}` per seed; (3) FEATURE DROPOUT reports no impact; (4) TRAINING ITSELF FAILS for any plausibility-gated model, because reconcile_pipeline_columns clones before checking whether anything drifted — the failure surfaces as a generic 'Training failed' expander at pages/06:1604. The same defect exists in OutlierCapping (`self.params = params or {}` at line 79) whenever params is empty or None, which build_preprocessing_pipeline produces via `numeric_outlier_params or {}`. There is ZERO test coverage: grep 'PlausibilityGate' across tests/ returns nothing, and tests/test_feature_drift.py exercises reconcile with a plain scaler pipeline only.
landmines.mitigation: Move all coercion out of __init__ into fit(), storing as fitted attributes (self.lower_bounds_, self.upper_bounds_); keep __init__ as bare assignment, exactly as UnitHarmonizer does. Change OutlierCapping to `self.params = params` and default inside fit. THEN add the missing test before anything moves: `@pytest.mark.parametrize('est', [UnitHarmonizer([1.0]), PlausibilityGate([1.0],[2.0]), OutlierCapping(), OutlierCapping('mad',{'threshold':3.5}), KMeansFeatures()]) def test_clonable(est): clone(est)`. Three lines, catches the whole class of bug, and any custom transformer added during the rebuild is automatically covered.

landmines.what: unit_harmonization_factors and plausibility_bounds are POSITIONAL lists aligned to the full numeric_features, but pages/05 passes a FILTERED numeric_features to build_preprocessing_pipeline. PlausibilityGate then silently applies bound j to column j' != j.
landmines.where: Built against the full list: ml/pipeline.py:45 `for col in numeric_features` (build_unit_harmonization_config) and ml/pipeline.py:84 `for col, factor in zip(numeric_features, conversion_factors)` (build_plausibility_bounds), both called at pages/05:825,827 with the FULL numeric_features. Consumed with a DIFFERENT list: pages/05:974-987 passes `numeric_features=numeric_features_safe` (the double-transform partition from 05:971) while still passing `unit_harmonization_factors=uf` and `plausibility_bounds=pb`. The silent truncation is ml/preprocess_operators.py:62 `n_cols = min(X_arr.shape[1], len(self.lower_bounds), len(self.upper_bounds))` and the same pattern at line 34 in plausibility_row_mask.
landmines.silentFailure: UnitHarmonizer fails LOUDLY (numpy broadcast ValueError, caught by pages/05's try/except into st.error), but PlausibilityGate does NOT: min() truncates to the shorter length and applies the first k bounds to the first k columns of a differently-ordered, differently-sized column set. A glucose bound of [70, 140] mg/dL gets applied to, say, creatinine; every creatinine value becomes NaN and is then median-imputed by the very next pipeline step. The output has no NaNs, the shape is right, the model trains, and the recipe string cheerfully says 'Plausibility gate (NHANES)'. The same truncation makes reconcile_pipeline_columns dangerous even after the clone bug is fixed: dropping one column from the numeric selector shifts every subsequent bound by one position. Triggers whenever unit harmonization + plausibility gating are on AND any engineered log/power/PCA feature is present.
landmines.mitigation: Delete the positional interfaces. build_plausibility_bounds already returns 'bounds_by_feature': {col -> {lower, upper, unit}} — make that the ONLY return, and have PlausibilityGate take a dict keyed by column name plus the ordered column list it is actually being applied to, resolving alignment at construction. Same for conversion factors ('inferred_units' / a factors-by-column dict already exists). As an interim guard, make PlausibilityGate.fit raise when len(bounds) != X.shape[1] instead of min()-truncating.

landmines.what: The pipelines stored in preprocessing_pipelines_by_model are FITTED ON THE FULL DATASET at build time — including the lockbox test rows — and they are what gets exported as the reproducibility artifact and previewed as CSV.
landmines.where: Fit on all rows: pages/05_Preprocess.py:945 `temp_pipeline.fit(X_sample)` and :999 `pipeline.fit(X_sample)`, where X_sample = df[all_features] (05:864 or :867). Stored fitted at 05:1005 -> set_preprocessing_pipelines. Consumed WITHOUT refit at pages/05:1275 `X_t = pipeline.transform(X_sample_preview)` (with a Download-as-CSV button at 05:1293) and at pages/10_Report_Export.py:2285-2290 `joblib.dump(model_pipeline, ...)` into preprocessing/{model_key}_pipeline.joblib.
landmines.silentFailure: Two distinct silent failures. (1) The exported joblib is NOT the pipeline the model was trained with — pages/06:1312 refits on X_train and stores that in the separate `fitted_preprocessing_pipelines` dict, which page 10 never exports. A reviewer who loads preprocessing/ridge_pipeline.joblib and applies it to new data gets different scaler means/imputer medians/encoder categories than the published model saw. The manifest calls it the model's pipeline. (2) The Preprocess-page CSV download contains data transformed with statistics learned from the held-out test rows. Neither is detectable from the artifact. The exported config JSON is correct, which makes the mismatch harder to notice.
landmines.mitigation: Export fitted_preprocessing_pipelines (train-fitted), not preprocessing_pipelines_by_model. Better, in the rebuild: never store fitted objects in the Project at all — store PreprocessSpec, and have the job that trains a model emit a single sealed artifact bundle {spec, fitted_preprocessor, fitted_estimator, train_row_ids, feature_names_out} so the three can never diverge. For the preview, fit on train rows only and label the download.

landmines.what: get_preprocessing_pipeline(model_key) silently falls back to an arbitrary other model's pipeline, and returns a SHARED MUTABLE OBJECT that the caller then fits in place.
landmines.where: utils/session_state.py:448-454 (the fallback) and :468 `default_pipeline = pipelines_by_model.get('default') or next(iter(pipelines_by_model.values()), None)` (which model becomes the default). Consumed at pages/06_Train_and_Compare.py:1286 `model_pipeline = get_preprocessing_pipeline(model_name) or pipeline`, then :1312 `model_pipeline.fit(X_train)`. Insertion order comes from pages/05:816 scanning `st.session_state.items()` for `train_model_*` keys.
landmines.silentFailure: Two effects. (A) FALLBACK: a model selected in Train & Compare but never configured in Preprocess trains under a different model's entire transform chain — log transform, Yeo-Johnson, PCA, KMeans replacement, scaling — chosen for a model with different assumptions. The only signal is a small '⚠️ No pipeline' badge at pages/06:896, and it is rendered only when `_has_preprocessing` is truthy (06:903). Which model donates its pipeline depends on checkbox render order, so the same project can behave differently between sessions. The manuscript's per-model preprocessing section (pages/10:1223) lists only the CONFIGURED models, so the borrowed one is invisible in the writeup. (B) ALIASING: reconcile_pipeline_columns returns `(pipe, [])` — the SAME object — when nothing drifted, so `.fit(X_train)` mutates the object stored in preprocessing_pipelines_by_model, and fitted_preprocessing_pipelines[A] and [B] become the identical instance. Page 08's per-model clone(pipeline) and page 07's per-model SHAP then operate on one shared object under two model names.
landmines.mitigation: This is the question the brief asked, and the answer is: keep per-model, DELETE THE GLOBAL. In AnalysisProject, pipeline resolution must be total and explicit — when the interview lands on a model with no spec, the Router asks the question or the engine synthesizes a spec from that model's registry capabilities and RECORDS that it was auto-derived. Never inherit another model's transform silently. And return specs (values) not fitted objects, which removes the aliasing class entirely.

landmines.what: pages/03_Feature_Engineering.py hand-rolls its own cascade invalidation instead of calling reset_downstream_results(), and the copy has drifted.
landmines.where: pages/03_Feature_Engineering.py:1229-1252 (the block after `st.session_state['engineered_feature_transforms'] = ...`), versus the real thing at utils/session_state.py:283-416.
landmines.silentFailure: Saving engineered features clears pipelines, models, and X/y splits — but leaves behind: train_indices/val_indices/test_indices (stale row positions into a dataframe whose column set just changed), feature_names and feature_names_by_model, target_transformer and y_train_original/y_val_original/y_test_original (so a stale log1p inverse can be applied to a fresh untransformed target), cv_strategy and cv_groups_train (a 'group' strategy leaks into a subsequent standard split), preprocess_built_model_keys and preprocessing_summary (page 06 still believes preprocessing exists; page 10's Methods section still describes the deleted pipelines), cv_results, explainability_robustness, and every report artifact. It also never rolls back ledger resolutions or clears provenance sections, both of which reset_downstream_results does. Nothing errors — the app simply carries a self-consistent-looking description of work that no longer exists into the manuscript.
landmines.mitigation: Replace the block with `reset_downstream_results(clear_feature_engineering=False)` before porting anything. Then, in the rebuild, make invalidation IMPOSSIBLE to hand-roll: AnalysisProject nodes declare `derives_from`, and there is exactly one `invalidate(node)` walker. The existing docstring at session_state.py:293 ('Any page that introduces a new result key must add it here') is an admission that the current design relies on discipline it cannot enforce.

landmines.what: Split provenance reads three attributes that SplitConfig does not have, so target trimming is never recorded in the Methods section.
landmines.where: pages/06_Train_and_Compare.py:704-706: `target_trim_enabled=bool(getattr(split_config, 'trim_target', False)), target_trim_lower=float(getattr(split_config, 'trim_lower', 0.0)), target_trim_upper=float(getattr(split_config, 'trim_upper', 1.0))`. The real field names are utils/session_state.py:78-80: `target_trim_enabled`, `target_trim_lower`, `target_trim_upper`.
landmines.silentFailure: getattr with a default never raises. record_split() is always told trimming was off with bounds [0.0, 1.0], regardless of what the researcher configured. Meanwhile pages/06:441-458 DOES log the trim correctly to methodology_log, so the two provenance channels disagree and whichever one the Methods generator reads determines whether a published paper discloses that rows were removed from the outcome distribution before splitting. This one is worth fixing before the port simply because the fix is renaming three strings and the consequence is an undisclosed exclusion criterion.
landmines.mitigation: Rename to the real attributes. Then eliminate the class of bug: provenance recorders should take the SplitConfig object itself (or a typed dict built from it), not string-named getattr lookups. Any getattr(obj, 'literal', default) against a dataclass in the ported code is a silent-drift site — grep for the pattern during the migration.

landmines.what: The pipeline recipe rendered into the manuscript omits or misreports real preprocessing steps, including reporting the WRONG outlier threshold.
landmines.where: ml/pipeline.py:326-424 get_pipeline_recipe(). Consumed at pages/10_Report_Export.py:1226 and :1243 (manuscript) and pages/06:2576 (UI).
landmines.silentFailure: The renderer has no branch for: the 'power_transform' / 'log' / 'power_nan_guard' steps in most configurations (only step_name=='log' is handled, so Yeo-Johnson is invisible), MinMaxScaler (only StandardScaler and RobustScaler have branches at :382-385), TargetEncoder and OrdinalEncoder (only OneHotEncoder at :399), and the entire 'numeric_passthrough' transformer (the loop at :341 only matches names 'numeric' and 'categorical'). Worse, the outlier branch reads attributes OutlierCapping never sets: `hasattr(step_transformer, 'lower_percentile')` is always False so percentile capping degrades to the generic 'Outlier treatment (percentile)' with no thresholds, and the mad branch does `getattr(step_transformer, 'mad_threshold', getattr(step_transformer, 'n_mad', 3))` — OutlierCapping stores the value in self.params['threshold'], so the manuscript reports 'MAD capping (3× MAD)' even when the researcher set 3.5. Also pages/10:1226 calls get_pipeline_recipe(pl) WITHOUT plausibility_mode, dropping the 'Plausibility: rows filtered to NHANES range' line that the function is specifically designed to emit. Every one of these produces plausible-looking prose in a publishable manuscript.
landmines.mitigation: Do not port get_pipeline_recipe as an introspector. Render the recipe from the PreprocessSpec — the spec knows every option by construction, so omissions become impossible rather than merely unlikely. Add a round-trip test: for each option in the spec, build, render, assert the option appears in the string.

landmines.what: reset_downstream_results() does not clear preprocess_built_model_keys, preprocessing_summary, or engineered_feature_transforms, so three consumers keep describing deleted work.
landmines.where: utils/session_state.py:283-416 (the function; grep it for these three keys — absent). Writers: pages/05:1011, pages/05:1037, pages/03:1227. Readers: pages/06:810 and :825 (`_prep_built` -> `_has_preprocessing`), utils/coaching_ui.py:52, utils/session_manager.py:680, pages/10_Report_Export.py:632 (`prep_summary` -> Methods section), pages/05:162 (double-transform guard).
landmines.silentFailure: After any data change, preprocessing_pipelines_by_model is emptied but preprocess_built_model_keys still lists the old models. pages/06:826 computes `_has_preprocessing = len(_prep_built) > 0 or pipeline is not None` -> True, so the 'you are about to train with unprocessed data' warning at 06:830 is SUPPRESSED exactly when it is needed, and 06:812 re-checks the same model checkboxes. Separately, preprocessing_summary still feeds the manuscript's missing-data/scaling/encoding paragraph (pages/10:632) describing pipelines that no longer exist. And a stale engineered_feature_transforms keeps the double-transform guard excluding columns from log/power/PCA by name after the engineered columns are gone — which is also the trigger for the positional-misalignment landmine above.
landmines.mitigation: Add all three to reset_downstream_results now (engineered_feature_transforms belongs in the `if clear_feature_engineering:` block next to engineering_log). Longer term this is the same fix as the DAG: derived state should not be reachable except through a node that knows what it derives from.

landmines.what: Feature selection runs LASSO with absolute alphas on UNSCALED features, so which predictors enter the published model depends on each variable's measurement unit.
landmines.where: pages/04_Feature_Selection.py:139-141 does median imputation only — no scaler. ml/feature_selection.py:241 `Lasso(alpha=0.01, max_iter=10000, ...)` in stability_selection, and :43 LassoCV in lasso_path_selection.
landmines.silentFailure: A variable measured in mg/dL versus mmol/L has ~18x different coefficient scale, so an L1 penalty at a fixed alpha shrinks one and keeps the other purely on units. stability_selection's per-bootstrap `except Exception: continue` (feature_selection.py:252) additionally swallows every failed fit and reports those features at selection probability 0.0 — indistinguishable from 'reliably not selected'. The result flows into consensus_features, into selected_features, into every downstream pipeline, and into the manuscript's variable-selection paragraph. Note also that consensus_threshold is `max(1, len(results) // 2)` (04:280), so running one or two methods makes 'consensus' mean 'any single method'. And non-numeric features are excluded from ranking entirely (04:110) while remaining in the model.
landmines.mitigation: Insert StandardScaler before the selectors (fit on the training rows the lockbox already isolated), or switch to a standardized-coefficient formulation. Replace the bare `except: continue` with a counted failure that surfaces in FeatureSelectionResult.details. Record the effective consensus threshold in Record so the manuscript cannot say 'consensus' when n_methods == 1.

landmines.what: KMeansFeatures REPLACES the feature matrix with cluster features rather than appending them — the opposite of what the UI tells the researcher.
landmines.where: ml/feature_steps.py:100-104: comment 'For now, we are replacing X with cluster features (not appending). To append, would need: np.hstack([X, result])' followed by `return result`. UI claim at pages/05_Preprocess.py:784: 'Adds derived columns (distance to each KMeans centroid). Increases feature count.'
landmines.silentFailure: Enabling the KMeans option discards every original predictor and trains the model on nothing but 5 distance-to-centroid columns. Shapes stay valid, the pipeline fits, metrics compute, SHAP renders on the cluster columns. The recipe line at ml/pipeline.py:407 says 'KMeans features added: 5 clusters, distances to centroids' — 'added'. Nothing indicates the predictors are gone. Two secondary hazards in the same class: if both add_distances and add_onehot_label are False, transform returns X unchanged, which may be a SPARSE matrix from OneHotEncoder(sparse_output=True) and then hits PCA, which raises TypeError('PCA does not support sparse input'); and __init__ sets self.kmeans_ = None / self.cluster_centers_ = None, so sklearn check_is_fitted (and therefore ml/estimator_utils.is_estimator_fitted) reports an unfitted instance as fitted.
landmines.mitigation: Decide the semantics explicitly and make code and copy agree — most likely np.hstack([X, result]) plus an updated recipe line. Move the None initializations out of __init__ (trailing-underscore attributes must only exist after fit). Add a shape assertion test: transform output width >= input width when add_distances is True.

landmines.what: data_processor.prepare_data is a complete, leakage-shaped alternative split path that no page uses — and it looks exactly like the API someone would reach for during the rebuild.
landmines.where: data_processor.py:576-650. Imputes with `X.fillna(X.median())` at :615 and again at :629 BEFORE splitting at :633, then fits a StandardScaler on train. Only caller in the repo: scripts/smoke_check.py:598.
landmines.silentFailure: It ignores the lockbox entirely, imputes on the full dataset before the split, and returns pre-scaled arrays that bypass the per-model pipeline architecture completely. If the migration moves data_processor.py into the engine wholesale (it also contains get_numeric_columns, which pages/05:110 genuinely depends on), this function arrives with a name that reads as the canonical entry point. Anyone wiring the new backend who calls prepare_data gets a working, plausible, silently-leaking baseline.
landmines.mitigation: Delete it in the same commit that moves get_numeric_columns. If it must survive for smoke_check, rename it `_legacy_unsafe_prepare_data` and have it emit a warning. Also note get_numeric_columns' own quiet hazard: its 'at least one non-null' filter means an all-NaN-within-cohort column is reclassified from numeric to categorical (pages/05:111-112 sweeps everything not numeric into categorical_features), so it gets one-hot encoded instead of imputed — making pipelines structurally different between cohort runs that are supposed to be comparable.

landmines.what: Seed sensitivity pools train+val+test and re-splits, dissolving the lockbox for numbers that appear beside lockbox-derived metrics.
landmines.where: pages/08_Sensitivity_Analysis.py:130-141 builds X_pool/y_pool from all three partitions, then :150 `_seed_tts(X_pool, y_pool, test_size=_test_frac, random_state=seed)` per seed.
landmines.silentFailure: The pooling is deliberate and commented ('Re-seeding a model on a FIXED split measures only model-internal randomness'), and the reasoning is sound — but the resulting spread is computed against test sets that include rows the lockbox had quarantined, and the manuscript presents it alongside lockbox metrics with no distinction. Combined with the clone landmine, a failure here produces an all-NaN table rather than an error (08:211).
landmines.mitigation: Tag these results in Record with `lockbox_applied=False` and have the manuscript renderer state the distinction. Every metric in the Project should carry the provenance of the split it was computed on — that flag is what lets the Router refuse to publish mixed-provenance numbers.

landmines.what: The 370-line split builder — the single most leakage-sensitive function in the app — lives inside a Streamlit button handler with zero unit tests, and writes its outputs through two separate branch-on-split-type blocks that must stay in sync by hand.
landmines.where: pages/06_Train_and_Compare.py:349-720. The split arrays are written via set_splits() at :610 or :646; the index lists are written by a SECOND independent branch at :682-693 keyed on the same three conditions.
landmines.silentFailure: Any future edit that adds or reorders a branch in one block and not the other produces splits whose stored train_indices/test_indices describe a different partition than X_train/X_test — used by Explainability to map rows back to the original dataframe. The mismatch is a wrong-rows-in-the-SHAP-plot bug, not a crash. Additionally the whole block mixes positional and label identity: `original_indices = np.where(mask)[0]` is POSITIONAL while `orig_labels = df.index[mask]` is LABEL-based, and both are live in the same scope; train_indices is stored as positions while the lockbox is labels.
landmines.mitigation: Extract `build_splits(df, data_config, split_config, lockbox, cohort_detection) -> SplitResult` FIRST, before any frontend work, with SplitResult as one immutable value object written atomically (arrays + index lists + strategy + seed + lockbox_applied + cv_strategy + cv_groups_train). Unit-test all four branches plus the lockbox-too-small fallback and the trim-with-lockbox interaction. This extraction is the highest-value single action in the whole migration: it is the piece with the most invariants, the most silent failure modes, and currently no test coverage at all.

domain: THE COACH → ROUTER. Files audited: ml/model_coach.py (1443 loc), ml/coach_probe.py (243), utils/insight_ledger.py (1405), ml/triage.py (282), plus every call site: pages/05_Preprocess.py, pages/06_Train_and_Compare.py, pages/02_EDA.py, pages/01_Upload_and_Audit.py, utils/coaching_ui.py, utils/storyline.py, utils/workflow_provenance.py, utils/session_state.py, ml/eda_recommender.py, ml/narrative_engine.py, ml/import_doctor.py, ml/join_doctor.py. VERDICT SUMMARY (detail in invariants/landmines): the coach is a PURE ANNOTATOR with one accidental control-flow act (auto-checking model checkboxes at pages/05_Preprocess.py:291-294). It is deterministic and explainable enough to ORDER questions, but it cannot GATE them: it never emits a `blocker` severity (only 02_EDA does, at lines 212 and 246), it has no confidence tier of its own, and 100% of its trigger logic lives in pages/.

modules.purpose: The coach's whole brain: a static model-metadata table, shape-based shortlist selection (select_top_picks), per-registry-key viability verdicts (model_viability), model-scoped preprocessing advice (generate_preprocessing_insights), and 7 post-training detectors (run_post_training_diagnostics). Emits plain dicts and dataclasses; owns NO state, NO storage, NO navigation. Import-clean of streamlit but NOT call-clean (see landmines).

keyFunctions.name: select_top_picks
keyFunctions.signature: def select_top_picks(profile: Any, probe: Any = None) -> Tuple[List[TopPick], List[Tuple[str, str]], str]
keyFunctions.does: Returns (picks, skip_list, headline). Picks 1-3 models by a fixed constraint cascade evaluated in this order: is_wide (p_n_ratio>1.0) → low_epv (classification and events_per_variable<10) → imbalanced → small_n (n<150) → else unconstrained. Slot 1 is always a linear model; slot 2 (tree) is SUPPRESSED when is_wide or low_epv; slot 3 (wildcard) is suppressed when low_epv. Headline names the dominant constraint with real numbers. Probe evidence, when present, PREPENDS to the headline and appends measured clauses to the `why` strings.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: This is the single most Router-shaped function in the repo: it already names a dominant constraint and returns a ranked, role-labelled list ('Start here'/'Try next'/'Alternative'). It should become the Router's model-question planner unchanged. But it decides WHICH MODELS, never WHICH QUESTION — it has no vocabulary for pages, steps, or prerequisites.

keyFunctions.name: model_viability
keyFunctions.signature: def model_viability(profile: Any, probe: Any = None) -> Dict[str, Tuple[str, str]]
keyFunctions.does: One (verdict, clause) per registry model key, verdict in {'good','ok','poor'}. Purely a function of n, p, p_n_ratio, events_per_variable, target outlier rate, plus optional probe gain. Covers all 22 keys in ml/model_registry.get_registry() (asserted by tests/test_coach_intelligence.py::TestModelViability::test_covers_full_registry).
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Task-BLIND: it emits v['logreg']=('good',…) and v['lda'] even for a regression profile. Today the Train page hides them because it iterates the task-filtered registry. A Router that reads model_viability directly will propose logistic regression for a regression outcome.

keyFunctions.name: generate_preprocessing_insights
keyFunctions.signature: def generate_preprocessing_insights(selected_models: List[str], profile: Any) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]
keyFunctions.does: Produces up to 4 insight-shaped dicts with fixed ids: preprocess_skewness_transform, preprocess_outlier_handling, preprocess_feature_scaling, preprocess_missing_tree_native. Each carries model_scope narrowed to the families the user actually selected, via ISSUE_MODEL_RELEVANCE.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Does `from utils.insight_ledger import ...` INSIDE the function body (line 634) — so calling it imports streamlit. Also: none of these 4 set manuscript_text, and 3 of the 4 are never resolved anywhere in the app.

keyFunctions.name: run_post_training_diagnostics
keyFunctions.signature: def run_post_training_diagnostics(model_results: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]], task_type: str, tolerance: float = 0.05, bootstrap_results: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, primary_model: str = "") -> List[Dict[str, Any]]
keyFunctions.does: Runs the 7 detectors in fixed order and concatenates their findings. No exception handling inside — one detector raising discards ALL findings.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Detector order is deterministic; detector CONTENT is not (see _detect_* notes). Two of its seven detectors are dead in production.

keyFunctions.name: _detect_prefer_simpler
keyFunctions.signature: def _detect_prefer_simpler(model_results: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]], task_type: str, tolerance: float = 0.05) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]
keyFunctions.does: Buckets models by _get_model_info()['interpretability'] ('high'=simple, 'low'=complex, 'medium'=ignored), compares best-of-each on RMSE (reg) or F1/Accuracy (clf), emits `train_prefer_simpler` when the simple model is within `tolerance`.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: min()/max() over a dict — exact ties resolve by insertion order, i.e. by the order the user checked the training boxes.

keyFunctions.name: _detect_low_overall_performance
keyFunctions.signature: def _detect_low_overall_performance(model_results: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]], task_type: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]
keyFunctions.does: Emits `train_low_performance` when best R2 < 0.15 (regression) or best AUC < 0.60 (classification).
keyFunctions.transitionNote: DEAD ON THE CLASSIFICATION PATH: it reads metrics['AUC'] but ml/eval.py:80-82 writes 'ROC-AUC'. `.get('AUC', 0)` → 0 → the `best_auc <= 0` early return fires every time. tests/test_complexity_coaching.py:111 feeds the fictional key 'AUC' so the test passes.

keyFunctions.name: _detect_high_cv_variance
keyFunctions.signature: def _detect_high_cv_variance(model_results: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]], task_type: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]
keyFunctions.does: Emits `train_cv_variance` when max fold SD exceeds half the between-model score range. Requires results[k]['cv_results']['std'] and >=2 scored models.

keyFunctions.name: _detect_overfit
keyFunctions.signature: def _detect_overfit(model_results: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]], task_type: str, gap_threshold: float = 0.10) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]
keyFunctions.does: One `train_overfit_{key}` per model whose train-minus-test R2/F1 gap exceeds 0.10. Maps the model key to a canonical ledger family via MODEL_TO_FAMILY for model_scope.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Second in-function `from utils.insight_ledger import MODEL_TO_FAMILY` (line 1080) — the other streamlit leak. Its own comment (lines 1076-1079) documents that a non-canonical model_scope makes the warning vanish behind '✅ no issues'.

keyFunctions.name: _detect_accuracy_vs_nir
keyFunctions.signature: def _detect_accuracy_vs_nir(model_results: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]], task_type: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]
keyFunctions.does: Computes the no-information rate from the first non-empty results[k]['y_test'] and emits `train_accuracy_below_nir` when best Accuracy <= NIR + 0.02.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: `for r in model_results.values(): ... break` picks the FIRST model's y_test — fine while all models share a split, silently wrong the moment per-model splits exist.

keyFunctions.name: _detect_ci_overlap
keyFunctions.signature: def _detect_ci_overlap(model_results: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]], task_type: str, bootstrap_results: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]
keyFunctions.does: Emits `train_ci_overlap_top_models` when the top two models' bootstrap CIs on RMSE/F1 overlap. Accepts either objects with .ci_lower/.ci_upper or dicts.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: EFFECTIVELY DEAD: pages/06_Train_and_Compare.py:1713 passes st.session_state.get('bootstrap_results') from inside the training block, but that key is only written far later at line 2072, and diagnostics are never re-run after bootstrapping.

keyFunctions.name: _detect_heteroscedastic_residuals
keyFunctions.signature: def _detect_heteroscedastic_residuals(model_results: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]], task_type: str, primary_model: str = "") -> List[Dict[str, Any]]
keyFunctions.does: Spearman rho between |residual| and prediction for ONE model; emits `train_heteroscedastic_residuals` when |rho| >= 0.3 and >=20 finite pairs.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Line 1263: `key = primary_model if primary_model in model_results else next(iter(model_results))`. pages/06:1714 passes st.session_state.get('primary_model',''), and NOTHING in the codebase ever writes st.session_state['primary_model'] — so the fallback always fires and the manuscript_text asserts heteroscedasticity for an arbitrarily-ordered model.

keyFunctions.name: _get_model_info
keyFunctions.signature: def _get_model_info() -> Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]
keyFunctions.does: Static metadata for the same 22 keys as the registry. Only 6 of its 11 fields are ever read: name, group, requires_scaling, handles_missing, min_samples, interpretability.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: training_time, requires_encoding, min_epv, good_for_high_dim, robust_to_outliers are written and never read — a second, stale copy of knowledge that ml/model_registry.py ModelSpec.capabilities also holds. Merge or drop; do not carry two.

keyFunctions.name: _model_display_name_coach

modules.purpose: The coach's only empirical input: three seeded, subsampled, cross-validated measurements on TRAINING ROWS ONLY — signal floor vs permuted targets, non-linearity gain (shallow HistGB vs penalized linear), and learning-curve slope. Returns a ProbeResult whose properties are the verdicts the coach cites. No streamlit, no state.

keyFunctions.name: run_probe
keyFunctions.signature: def run_probe(X_train, y_train, task_type: str = "regression") -> ProbeResult
keyFunctions.does: Seeds np.random.default_rng(SEED=42), prepares numeric-only imputed subsamples (MAX_ROWS=1500; MAX_FEATURES=100, or MAX_FEATURES_WIDE=2000 when p>n), scores a linear pipeline, N_PERMUTATIONS=3 permuted baselines, a shallow HistGB, and a half-data linear fit — all over N_FOLDS=3 shared folds. Bails with a note when len(X)<20 or no numeric columns; skips the learning-curve leg when len(X)<80.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: This is the one genuinely long-running coach operation (the UI advertises '~10 s'). It is the natural first Jobs citizen: already pure, already seeded, already time-bounded. It needs cancellation and a progress channel it does not currently have, and it must keep receiving PRE-MASKED training rows — it does not enforce the lockbox itself.

keyFunctions.name: ProbeResult.has_signal
keyFunctions.signature: @property def has_signal(self) -> Optional[bool]
keyFunctions.does: True when max(linear_score, tree_score) clears BOTH an absolute chance floor ({'R²':0.0,'AUC':0.5}) + SIGNAL_MARGIN AND permuted_score + max(SIGNAL_MARGIN, 2*permuted_spread). Returns None when both scores are NaN — a real tri-state.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Tri-state (True/False/None) plus the separate `underpowered` flag is the closest thing the coach has to a confidence tier. The Router should promote this pattern, not the boolean.

keyFunctions.name: ProbeResult.nonlinearity_gain
keyFunctions.signature: @property def nonlinearity_gain(self) -> Optional[float]
keyFunctions.does: tree_score - linear_score, or None if either is NaN.

keyFunctions.name: ProbeResult.data_hungry
keyFunctions.signature: @property def data_hungry(self) -> Optional[bool]
keyFunctions.does: linear_score - half_data_score > LEARNING_SLOPE (0.03).

keyFunctions.name: ProbeResult.underpowered
keyFunctions.signature: @property def underpowered(self) -> bool
keyFunctions.does: n_rows_used < 60. Exists so the coach says 'cannot tell' instead of 'no signal'.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: THE honesty valve. select_top_picks branches on it at lines 436-443 to downgrade a scary '⚠️ Expect null results' headline into a neutral note. Any Router that gates on has_signal alone reintroduces the confident-wrong failure the FINDINGS_LEDGER governing rule forbids.

keyFunctions.name: ProbeResult.summary
keyFunctions.signature: def summary(self) -> str
keyFunctions.does: One-line advisory sentence in the coach's voice; falls back to 'probe inconclusive'.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Its output is stored verbatim into Insight.finding (pages/05_Preprocess.py:238) AND into CoachProvenance.probe_summary, which narrative_engine.py:947-951 splices into the Methods draft. UI prose is already load-bearing manuscript text.

keyFunctions.name: probe thresholds
keyFunctions.signature: SIGNAL_MARGIN = 0.05; NONLINEAR_GAIN = 0.04; LEARNING_SLOPE = 0.03; SEED = 42
keyFunctions.does: The interpretation thresholds, deliberately coarse.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: ml/model_coach.py does NOT import them: it hardcodes 0.04 and 0.02 at lines 497, 523, 1361 and 1363. Two copies of the same decision boundary.

modules.purpose: The Record. Insight dataclass + InsightLedger with the full lifecycle (add/upsert/resolve/acknowledge/auto_acknowledge_gate/rollback_resolutions/prune_auto_generated/remove/clear), the query surface every page reads, the TRIPOD roll-up, the methodology log, and the three manuscript renderers. Also the canonical model-family vocabulary that model_coach reaches back into.

keyFunctions.name: InsightLedger.upsert
keyFunctions.signature: def upsert(self, insight: Insight) -> bool
keyFunctions.does: IDENTITY IS `insight.id` AND NOTHING ELSE. Linear scan for a matching id; on hit, replaces the object wholesale but first copies forward: the entire resolution block if the existing one is resolved and the incoming one is not, plus affected_features / model_scope / metadata / tripod_keys / relevant_pages whenever the incoming value is falsy. Returns True only on a NEW insert.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Deduplication is by string id, so id conventions ARE the schema. Producers pick ids by hand ('preprocess_skewness_transform', f'train_overfit_{key}', f'eda_leakage_{col}'); tests/test_insight_id_integrity.py is the only thing keeping producers and consumers in sync, and it does it with an AST scan, not types.

keyFunctions.transitionNote: The only lifecycle method that reports its own failure. Every caller ignores the return value.

keyFunctions.signature: def acknowledge(self, insight_id: str, acknowledged_by: str) -> bool
keyFunctions.does: Marks reviewed-and-accepted-without-action. Refuses to downgrade an already-resolved insight but STILL returns True in that case.

keyFunctions.signature: def auto_acknowledge_gate(self, gate_name: str, source_pages: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int
keyFunctions.does: Bulk-acknowledges every unresolved, unacknowledged, NON-BLOCKER insight from the named source pages, stamping acknowledged_by=gate_name. Returns the count. Skipping blockers is explicitly justified in-code (lines 789-794): passing a gate is not evidence the user reviewed the worst findings.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: This IS a Router primitive wearing a Record method's clothes — it is the app's only formal notion of 'the user moved past this stage'. Two call sites define the two gates that exist: pages/05_Preprocess.py:1241 ('Proceeded to preprocessing', scoped to 02_EDA) and pages/06_Train_and_Compare.py:1698 ('Training completed', scoped to 02_EDA/03/04/05). keyFunctions.signature: def rollback_resolutions(self, resolved_on_pages: set) -> int
keyFunctions.does: WHY IT EXISTS: when a downstream reset destroys the results a resolution was earned on, the FINDING may still hold but the RESOLUTION CLAIM does not. Keeps the insight, clears resolved/resolved_by/resolved_on_page/resolved_at/resolution_details, so the manuscript stops asserting a target transform / imputation config / training run that no longer exists.

keyFunctions.transitionNote: Sole caller utils/session_state.py:407-411 passes {'02_EDA','05_Preprocess','06_Train_and_Compare'}. keyFunctions.signature: def detect_task_type(df: pd.DataFrame, target: str) -> Dict
keyFunctions.does: Returns {'detected','confidence','reasons'}. confidence is 'high' | 'med' | 'low'. 'high' only for: object/category/bool dtype, exact binary {0,1} ints, or continuous floats with >10 uniques and >=2% unique ratio. Low-cardinality integers (<=10 uniques) are deliberately rated 'low' with an in-code justification (lines 54-64): class codes, counts and 0-10 ratings all look identical.

invariants.rule: The evidence probe must only ever see TRAINING rows. It never touches the held-out test set.
invariants.enforcedBy: NOT enforced inside ml/coach_probe.py — its docstring (lines 19-21) states 'the probe must ONLY ever see training rows (callers apply the lockbox mask)'. The single enforcement is at pages/05_Preprocess.py:224: `_pm = df[target_col].notna() & train_row_mask(df.index)` before `run_probe(df.loc[_pm, _feats_probe], df.loc[_pm, target_col], …)`.
invariants.breaksIf: run_probe moves into Jobs and is invoked from a job spec that hands it the whole frame — which is the natural thing to do, since the function signature `run_probe(X_train, y_train, task_type)` merely NAMES its arguments X_train/y_train and validates nothing. Every probe number then silently becomes contaminated, and because probe verdicts flow into CoachProvenance and from there into narrative_engine's Methods draft, the leakage reaches the manuscript.

invariants.rule: Probe numbers are advisory diagnostics, never reportable results.
invariants.enforcedBy: ml/coach_probe.py:20-23 (contract docstring); pages/05_Preprocess.py:269-274 renders the caption '_Advisory only — computed on training rows, never a reportable result._'; ml/narrative_engine.py:947-951 emits 'screen scores were advisory and are not reported as results'; the two probe Insights (pages/05_Preprocess.py:243-247, 262-266) carry hedged manuscript_text.
invariants.breaksIf: A Router surfaces probe.linear_score / probe.tree_score as numbers in a results table or a metric tile. Nothing in ProbeResult marks the fields as non-reportable — the discipline lives entirely in prose.

invariants.rule: Blockers are never bulk-acknowledged: passing a workflow gate is not evidence the user reviewed the worst findings.
invariants.enforcedBy: utils/insight_ledger.py:789-794 — the explicit `if i.severity == 'blocker': continue` inside auto_acknowledge_gate, with a four-line in-code justification.
invariants.breaksIf: The Router reimplements gating with its own sweep loop, or calls a generalized `acknowledge_all(...)`. The consequence is fabricated 'accepted risk' provenance for target leakage and insufficient-sample findings — the exact class of confidently-wrong assertion the governing rule forbids.

invariants.rule: The Methods draft may cite the coach's rationale only when the trained lineup actually overlaps the shortlist.
invariants.enforcedBy: ml/narrative_engine.py:933-936 — `_pick_keys = {p.get('model_key') for p in coach_picks…}; _followed = bool(_pick_keys & set(models))`, then both the headline sentence (937) and the probe sentence (946) are gated on `_followed`.
invariants.breaksIf: The Router auto-runs its own picks. Overlap then becomes tautological, `_followed` is always True, and the Methods section claims a rationale the user never adopted. Note pages/05_Preprocess.py:290-294 ALREADY partially defeats this by auto-checking the picks.

invariants.rule: An insight's identity is its `id` string, and nothing else.
invariants.enforcedBy: utils/insight_ledger.py:670-675 (`add`) and 677-707 (`upsert`) both scan `i.id == insight.id`. Cross-file consistency is enforced only by tests/test_insight_id_integrity.py, an AST scan that collects `*Insight(id=…)` constructor kwargs plus coach finding-dict literals as PRODUCERS and `<ledger>.resolve/acknowledge/get/remove('literal')` plus `_ACTION_TO_INSIGHT_MAP` entries as CONSUMERS, then fails on any consumer with no producer.
invariants.breaksIf: (a) Two producers pick the same id — the second silently overwrites the first, and upsert's field-preservation makes the result a chimera. (b) The scanner's shape assumptions change: it keys on the constructor name ENDING in 'Insight', on the variable name `_ACTION_TO_INSIGHT_MAP`, and on the receiver expression containing the substring 'ledger'. Rename the map, alias the ledger as something without 'ledger' in it, or build Insights via a factory function, and the guard goes quiet without failing.

invariants.rule: model_scope must use the canonical family vocabulary ('linear','tree','neural','distance','margin','prob'), never display groups.
invariants.enforcedBy: utils/insight_ledger.py:609-615 — Insight.__post_init__ lowercases and maps every scope entry through FAMILY_ALIASES ('trees'->tree, 'boosting'->tree, 'neural net'->neural, …); and ml/model_coach.py:1076-1082, where _detect_overfit deliberately looks the family up via MODEL_TO_FAMILY with an in-code note that a non-matching model_scope 'makes grouped coaching silently hide the warning behind ✅ no issues'.
invariants.breaksIf: A Router constructs scoped questions from TopPick.group (which is the string 'Trees/Boosting' at ml/model_coach.py:540 — not in FAMILY_ALIASES) or from ml/model_coach.GROUP_DISPLAY_NAMES. Normalization yields 'trees/boosting', matches no family, and utils/coaching_ui.py:170-173 discards the insight with no trace.

invariants.rule: Every model key in ml/model_registry.get_registry() has a viability verdict.
invariants.enforcedBy: tests/test_coach_intelligence.py::TestModelViability::test_covers_full_registry — `missing = registry_keys - set(v.keys()); assert not missing`.
invariants.breaksIf: A model is added to the registry without adding a branch to model_viability. The test catches it — this is the healthiest invariant in the domain and must survive the split intact.

invariants.rule: The probe is seeded and reproducible.
invariants.enforcedBy: ml/coach_probe.py SEED=42 threaded through np.random.default_rng, KFold/StratifiedKFold(random_state=SEED), LassoCV(random_state=SEED) and HistGradientBoosting*(random_state=SEED); asserted by tests/test_coach_intelligence.py::test_seeded_and_deterministic (`r1.linear_score == r2.linear_score`).
invariants.breaksIf: Jobs parallelizes the probe legs, or run_probe is handed a differently-ordered dataframe (feature selection by variance uses nlargest, whose ties break on column order). The test only compares linear_score, so tree_score / permuted_score drift would pass.

invariants.rule: A resolution claim must not outlive the results that earned it.
invariants.enforcedBy: utils/session_state.py:396-411 → InsightLedger.rollback_resolutions({'05_Preprocess','06_Train_and_Compare','07_Explainability','08_Sensitivity_Analysis','09_Hypothesis_Testing'} plus {'03','04'} when clear_feature_selection) and prune_auto_generated({'02_EDA','05_Preprocess','06_Train_and_Compare'}).

A Record class that renames or splits either method makes invalidation a NO-OP with no error, and the manuscript keeps asserting a target transform / imputation config / training run that no longer exists.

invariants.rule: Coaching voice must never reach the manuscript verbatim.
invariants.enforcedBy: utils/insight_ledger.py:1188 — `text = (i.manuscript_text or '').strip() or _clean_for_manuscript(i.finding)`, with _clean_for_manuscript (lines 388-445) stripping coaching parentheticals, bracket tags and stock phrases and rewriting model keys to display names.

invariants.rule: 'high' confidence is the only tier the UI pre-selects, so 'high' means the app is asserting (docs/FINDINGS_LEDGER.md, Governing rule, lines 20-27).
invariants.enforcedBy: PARTIALLY, and only in the import/join domain: ml/join_doctor.py:922 `if include_low or c.confidence != 'low'` in suggest_best; utils/combine_ui.py:262 `usable = [c for c in cands if c.confidence != 'low']`; utils/import_ui.py auto-applies nothing (every fix is an st.button) and adds a hedge via _CONFIDENCE_NOTE; pages/01_Upload_and_Audit.py:1003-1017 `if _det_conf == 'high': st.success(...) else: st.info('Best guess … Please verify')`. ml/import_doctor.py:93-96 ShapeFinding.auto_suggestable encodes the rule as a property with ZERO callers.

domain: Record and Narrative — provenance, manuscript compilation, validation, export

modules.purpose: The Record. 13 dataclasses: 11 optional section slots + ModelPreprocessingConfig + WorkflowProvenance container. Records WHAT HAPPENED (the InsightLedger records what was considered). Zero top-level streamlit; the only streamlit touch is a lazy import inside get_provenance(). Section slots and what each records: UploadProvenance(target_col, task_type, feature_cols, n_samples, n_features, data_source, timestamp, cleaning_actions[]); EDAProvenance(analyses_run[], table1_generated, key_findings[], timestamp); FeatureEngineeringProvenance(transforms_applied[], n_features_created/before/after); FeatureSelectionProvenance(method, n_before, n_after, features_kept[], consensus_methods[]); SplitProvenance(strategy, train_n/val_n/test_n, train_pct/val_pct/test_pct, random_seed, target_transform, target_trim_enabled/lower/upper); PreprocessingProvenance(shared{}, per_model{model_key: ModelPreprocessingConfig}, models_configured[]); TrainingProvenance(models_trained[], hyperparameters{}, primary_model, selection_criteria, use_cv, cv_folds, use_hyperopt, class_weight_balanced, metrics_by_model{}, nn_config_source/reasoning/modifications); ExplainabilityProvenance(methods_used[], models_explained[]); SensitivityProvenance(seed_stability, seed_stability_cv, feature_dropout); StatisticalValidationProvenance(tests_run[]); CoachProvenance(headline, picks[], probe_summary). EDAProvenance.key_findings is declared 'populated by insight ledger' and is never written by anything.

keyFunctions.does: asdict() out; per-section reconstruction in, filtering unknown keys through each dataclass's __dataclass_fields__. schema_version is read into the object but never branched on. Consumed by utils/session_manager.py:268-276 (save, json.dumps(default=str)) and :544-556 (restore).
keyFunctions.transitionNote: The `default=str` on save is the single most dangerous line for the Record — see landmines. from_dict must gain a version dispatch and a numeric-coercion pass.

keyFunctions.name: get_provenance
keyFunctions.signature: get_provenance() -> WorkflowProvenance
keyFunctions.does: Lazily imports streamlit, creates st.session_state['workflow_provenance'] if absent, returns it. On ImportError returns a DETACHED instance whose writes go nowhere.

modules.purpose: The manuscript compiler. ManuscriptDraft (typed sections + markdown/LaTeX renderers + ownership contract) and NarrativeEngine (WorkflowProvenance + InsightLedger + frozen manuscript_context -> ManuscriptDraft). Also owns _MODEL_NAMES, the model-key vocabulary that manuscript_validator imports privately. Zero direct streamlit refs but imports utils.insight_ledger at module top level, which imports streamlit at ITS top level.

keyFunctions.name: ManuscriptDraft
keyFunctions.signature: @dataclass ManuscriptDraft(study_design='', predictor_variables='', missing_data='', data_preprocessing='', model_development='', model_evaluation='', sensitivity_analysis='', statistical_validation='', results='', discussion='', data_observations='', software_environment='', warnings: List[str]=[], completeness: Dict[str,bool]={})
keyFunctions.does: How evidence is represented: 12 plain-string section fields plus warnings (completeness gaps) and completeness (the raw provenance boolean map). There is NO structured evidence object — traceability lives entirely in generate_evidence_map(), which is computed separately and is NOT a field of the draft.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: For a feed, evidence must move INTO the draft as per-section source references, not stay in a side artifact that can disagree with it.

keyFunctions.name: ManuscriptDraft.OWNERSHIP_PREAMBLE
keyFunctions.signature: OWNERSHIP_PREAMBLE: str (class attribute, not a dataclass field)
keyFunctions.does: The ownership contract shipped in every markdown draft: Methods/Results are compiled from logged events; [AUTHOR REQUIRED — …] passages belong to the authors. to_latex() emits it only as % comments, so it is INVISIBLE in the compiled PDF.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: In TurboTab the preamble is the feed's framing statement and should be a first-class UI element, not prose glued onto a markdown blob.

keyFunctions.name: ManuscriptDraft.sections / all_sections
keyFunctions.signature: @property sections(self) -> Dict[str, str]  /  @property all_sections(self) -> Dict[str, str]
keyFunctions.does: sections = the 10 Methods-level subsections (Study Design, Predictor Variables, Missing Data, Data Preprocessing, Model Development, Model Evaluation, Sensitivity Analysis, Statistical Validation, Data Observations, Software Environment), non-empty only. all_sections adds Results and Discussion. These two orderings are the canonical manuscript order.

keyFunctions.name: ManuscriptDraft.count_author_inputs
keyFunctions.signature: count_author_inputs(self) -> int
keyFunctions.does: Counts '[AUTHOR REQUIRED' occurrences across all_sections, deliberately excluding the preamble. UNUSED IN THE APP — pages/10:2068 counts the raw markdown string instead and therefore includes the preamble.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: The feed's 'N answers still needed from you' badge should call this, not re-count a string.

keyFunctions.name: ManuscriptDraft.to_markdown
keyFunctions.signature: to_markdown(self) -> str
keyFunctions.does: Preamble + '## Methods' with '### <title>' subsections + '## Results' + '## Discussion'. This is the ONLY renderer used by the running app (pages/10:618).

keyFunctions.name: ManuscriptDraft.to_latex / _md_to_latex
keyFunctions.signature: to_latex(self) -> str  /  @staticmethod _md_to_latex(text: str) -> str
keyFunctions.does: Emits \\section{Methods} + \\subsection per section, warnings as % comments, Results, and Discussion with ### promoted to \\subsection. _md_to_latex escapes ONLY & % # _ then converts **bold**/*italic* and ²/×/−/–/—. DEAD CODE in the app path — pages/10 never calls it; generate_latex_report re-parses the markdown instead.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Two independent LaTeX escapers exist (this one and latex_report._escape_latex, which also handles $ { } ~ ^ < >). Pick one before switching TurboTab to draft.to_latex(), or hostile column names will break compilation.

keyFunctions.name: NarrativeEngine.__init__
keyFunctions.signature: __init__(self, provenance: WorkflowProvenance, ledger: Optional[InsightLedger] = None, manuscript_context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None)
keyFunctions.does: Stores prov/ledger, snapshots ctx = provenance.get_methods_context(), then _apply_manuscript_context() (frozen export facts overwrite live provenance) and _normalize_metrics() (metric keys title-cased).
keyFunctions.transitionNote: manuscript_context is the 'freeze' boundary. In TurboTab it becomes an explicit immutable ExportSnapshot produced by the Project, not a loose dict assembled by a page.

keyFunctions.name: NarrativeEngine.generate
keyFunctions.signature: generate(self) -> ManuscriptDraft
keyFunctions.does: Runs all 12 _gen_* generators plus _check_completeness(). All-or-nothing: no incremental/per-section regeneration.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: The feed needs per-event narration. Only _gen_missing_data, _gen_data_preprocessing, _gen_model_evaluation, _gen_sensitivity_analysis and _gen_statistical_validation map 1:1 to a single provenance section; _gen_study_design/_gen_predictor_variables/_gen_results/_gen_discussion each fuse 3-5 sections plus the ledger.

keyFunctions.name: NarrativeEngine.generate_evidence_map
keyFunctions.signature: generate_evidence_map(self) -> str
keyFunctions.does: Markdown table | Draft section | Compiled from | Recorded values |. Rows: Study Design (upload+split records, incl. seed), Predictor Variables (feature-selection or upload record), Missing Data/Preprocessing (per-model configs), Model Development shortlist rationale (coach record, only when coach data exists), Model Development/Evaluation (training record), Results (recorded per-model metrics), Sensitivity, Statistical Validation, Data Observations & Strengths/Limitations (contributing insight IDs, first 8), and a hardcoded final row 'Discussion — interpretation, prior work, implications | AUTHOR | author-owned'. Missing stages print 'NOT RECORDED'.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: This is the closest existing artifact to a feed manifest — it already enumerates (section, source, values) per stage. In TurboTab it should become structured rows, not a markdown string, and MUST be built from the same context as the draft (today pages/10:2094 builds it with NO manuscript_context).

keyFunctions.name: NarrativeEngine._apply_manuscript_context
keyFunctions.signature: _apply_manuscript_context(self) -> None
keyFunctions.does: Overlays frozen export facts onto ctx: selected_model_results -> metrics_by_model + models_trained; manuscript_primary_model -> primary_model (explicitly BLANKED when the key is present but falsy); best_model_by_metric; best_metric_name -> also rewrites selection_criteria to 'validation <metric>'; population_counts.upload_total/analysis_total -> n_upload_total/n_analysis_total/n_total; feature_counts.original/candidate/selected/engineered; feature_names_for_manuscript -> feature_cols + features_kept; target_stats; top_features; exploratory_mode.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Precedence rules here are load-bearing and entirely undocumented outside the code. Encode them as an explicit merge policy in the Project.

keyFunctions.name: NarrativeEngine._gen_study_design
keyFunctions.signature: _gen_study_design(self) -> str
keyFunctions.does: Task type + n; outcome name; reconciles upload_total vs analysis_total (trim vs generic exclusion wording); target trimming sentence; split sentence with RECOMPUTED percentages and seed; target transform back-transformation note; cleaning-operations count and rows removed; and the lockbox sentence ('test set was frozen at data upload, before any feature engineering or feature selection') gated on NOT exploratory_mode AND ledger.get('upload_test_lockbox').resolved, with the fraction pulled from resolution_details['params']['fraction'].
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Hardcodes the ledger insight id 'upload_test_lockbox' (created at pages/01_Upload_and_Audit.py:1089). Renaming that id silently deletes the study's strongest methodological guarantee.

keyFunctions.name: NarrativeEngine._gen_predictor_variables
keyFunctions.signature: _gen_predictor_variables(self) -> str
keyFunctions.does: Feature-engineering sentence with count agreement (was/were); the feature funnel (original -> candidate -> final) in four mutually exclusive shapes; consensus vs generic feature-selection detail using _feature_selection_method_label; lists features inline when <=15 else points at 'Supplementary Table S1'.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: The 'Supplementary Table S1' promise is never fulfilled by any export — nothing writes S1 into the ZIP.

keyFunctions.name: NarrativeEngine._gen_missing_data
keyFunctions.signature: _gen_missing_data(self) -> str
keyFunctions.does: Reads imputation methods off preprocessing_per_model; single vs model-specific phrasing; optionally appends 'N of M features (P%) contained missing values' from ctx['n_features_with_missing'].
keyFunctions.transitionNote: ctx['n_features_with_missing'] is NEVER set by get_methods_context() or _apply_manuscript_context — the missing-data percentages branch is unreachable dead code in the NarrativeEngine path (the legacy publication path computes it from session_state instead).

keyFunctions.name: NarrativeEngine._gen_data_preprocessing
keyFunctions.signature: _gen_data_preprocessing(self) -> str
keyFunctions.does: If configs_differ() is False, one shared-pipeline sentence; otherwise 'Preprocessing was configured independently for each model family to respect different algorithmic assumptions:' followed by '**<Model>**: ...' per model via _describe_preprocessing.

keyFunctions.name: NarrativeEngine._gen_model_development
keyFunctions.signature: _gen_model_development(self) -> str
keyFunctions.does: Model candidate list; coach shortlist rationale ONLY when the trained lineup intersects coach_picks model_keys (_followed) — strips '⚠️ ' and 'Dominant constraint: ' from the UI register and lowercases the first letter; coach probe sentence marked advisory-and-not-reported-as-results; per-model hyperparameter prose; CV; hyperopt; NN config source rationale; class_weight balanced; and primary-model selection with three mutually exclusive endings, one of which emits the exact string 'no manuscript-primary model was explicitly selected' that manuscript_validator greps for.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: The _followed gate is a real trust invariant: the Methods must not cite a rationale the model list contradicts. Preserve it verbatim.

keyFunctions.name: NarrativeEngine._gen_model_evaluation
keyFunctions.signature: _gen_model_evaluation(self) -> str
keyFunctions.does: Per model, formats every numeric metric as '<human name>=<value>' and folds <metric>_ci_lower/<metric>_ci_upper into '(95% CI: lo–hi)'.

keyFunctions.name: NarrativeEngine._gen_results
keyFunctions.signature: _gen_results(self) -> str
keyFunctions.does: Reports only. Computes metric_best (min RMSE / max F1-or-Accuracy) and uses it to avoid claiming 'best overall performance' for a deliberately non-best primary; primary metrics with CIs; 'summarized in Table 1' pointer plus best/worst ranking sentence; top_features sentence (omitted entirely when absent — never a placeholder); and a simple-vs-complex parity finding at a 5% threshold.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: 'summarized in Table 1' collides with the CONSORT/characteristics Table 1 — the LaTeX report labels the population table tab:table1 and the metrics table tab:model_performance. The prose points at the wrong table.

keyFunctions.name: NarrativeEngine._gen_discussion
keyFunctions.signature: _gen_discussion(self) -> str
keyFunctions.does: How the [AUTHOR REQUIRED] scaffolds work. Five headed blocks: '### Principal Findings' (auto, comparative-vs-single wording, negative-R² stated plainly, _discussion_model_pattern, _discussion_regression_context, top predictors); '### Comparison with Prior Work' (pure scaffold, seeded with the study's own headline metric and target name); '### Strengths and Limitations' (auto from ledger.discussion_points_for_manuscript(), max 3 strengths / 5 limitations, plus a mandatory exploratory-mode limitation, falling back to a scaffold when the ledger is empty or absent); '### Clinical and Practical Implications' (scaffold seeded with top_features and an explicit predictive-not-causal warning); '### Conclusions' (states the recorded fact, hands adequacy to the author, then a fixed further-validation sentence).
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Each [AUTHOR REQUIRED — …] block is already a well-formed interview question with evidence attached. These are the natural terminal cards of the TurboTab scroll: promote them from inline markers to typed AuthorPrompt objects (id, prompt, cited evidence, answer).

keyFunctions.name: NarrativeEngine._gen_data_observations
keyFunctions.signature: _gen_data_observations(self) -> str
keyFunctions.does: Calls ledger.to_manuscript_narrative() (phase -> text) and runs each through _polish_data_observations_text.

keyFunctions.name: NarrativeEngine._gen_software_environment
keyFunctions.signature: _gen_software_environment(self) -> str
keyFunctions.does: Fixed boilerplate naming 'Tabular ML Lab ... (Python, scikit-learn, Streamlit)' and asserting automatic provenance tracking.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Hardcodes 'Streamlit' into every manuscript. Must be rewritten for TurboTab and ideally sourced from the reproducibility manifest instead of a literal.

keyFunctions.name: NarrativeEngine._normalize_metrics
keyFunctions.signature: _normalize_metrics(self) -> None  (uses _METRIC_KEY_MAP: rmse/mae/r2/medianae/accuracy/f1/auc/precision/recall)
keyFunctions.does: Rewrites metric dict keys to canonical casing, including '<base>_ci_lower/_ci_upper' suffixes.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Only normalizes KEYS. Values are passed through untouched — no numeric coercion, which is what makes the restore-from-JSON landmine fatal.

keyFunctions.name: NarrativeEngine._resolve_primary_model / _discussion_model_pattern / _discussion_regression_context
keyFunctions.signature: _resolve_primary_model(self, metrics: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]], task_type: str, primary_model: str) -> str  /  _discussion_model_pattern(self, task_type: str, metrics: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]) -> str  /  _discussion_regression_context(self, best_metrics: Dict[str, Any], target_stats: Dict[str, Any]) -> str
keyFunctions.does: Primary-model fallback by metric ranking; the simple-vs-complex / all-models-similar interpretation sentence (which first consults ledger.get('train_prefer_simpler') and uses its .finding when unresolved); and RMSE-in-SD-units / percent-variance-explained contextualization.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: _discussion_model_pattern hardcodes the ledger id 'train_prefer_simpler' (produced by ml/model_coach.py:870) inside a bare try/except that falls through to hardcoded thresholds — a rename degrades silently to the generic branch.

keyFunctions.name: NarrativeEngine._describe_preprocessing / _describe_hyperparameters / _model_name / _metric_name / _fmt_param
keyFunctions.signature: _describe_preprocessing(self, cfg: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[str]  /  _describe_hyperparameters(self, model_key: str, params: Dict[str, Any]) -> str  /  _model_name(self, key: str) -> str  /  _metric_name(self, key: str) -> str  /  _fmt_param(self, v: Any) -> str
keyFunctions.does: Config-to-prose for scaling/encoding/outliers/power/log/PCA; hyperparameter prose covering linear alpha/l1_ratio, tree n_estimators/max_depth/learning_rate, histgb max_iter, NN architecture/dropout/lr/epochs/scheduler/grad-clip/loss, SVM C/kernel/gamma, KNN k, Huber epsilon, with a filtered raw-param fallback; name/metric lookups; 4-significant-figure formatting.

keyFunctions.name: NarrativeEngine._check_completeness
keyFunctions.signature: _check_completeness(self) -> List[str]
keyFunctions.does: Emits warnings for missing upload/preprocessing/training/split/eda records. Surfaced only as % comments in ManuscriptDraft.to_latex() — i.e. nowhere in the running app.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: This is literally 'which question is still unanswered'. Hand it to the Router instead of burying it in LaTeX comments.

keyFunctions.name: module constants
keyFunctions.signature: _MODEL_NAMES: dict  /  _METRIC_NAMES: dict  /  _SCALE_LABELS  /  _ENC_LABELS  /  _TRANSFORM_LABELS  /  _count_phrase(count,singular,plural=None)  /  _oxford_join(items)  /  _feature_selection_method_label(method)  /  _polish_data_observations_text(text)
keyFunctions.does: _MODEL_NAMES = MODEL_DISPLAY_NAMES plus lasso/xgb/lgbm/svm/knn/logistic/dt. _polish_data_observations_text runs 8 regex rewrites turning ledger phrasing into manuscript register and collapses '..' to '.'.
