modules.purpose: LaTeX manuscript generator + pdflatex driver. Builds the full submission-shaped document: preamble (mathpazo, booktabs, hyperref, natbib, adjustbox, microtype, xcolor, doublespacing), title block, structured abstract, Introduction, Methods (from the compiled markdown), Results (population, Table 1, metrics table, baselines, calibration, explainability, sensitivity, statistical validation), Discussion, References (3 fixed citations + optional Lundberg), and a Supplementary appendix (TRIPOD pointer, reproducibility claim, decision audit trail). No direct streamlit refs, but it calls ml.publication.generate_decision_audit_trail() which reads st.session_state.

keyFunctions.name: generate_latex_report
keyFunctions.signature: generate_latex_report(title: str = "Prediction Model Development and Validation", authors: str = "[Author Names]", affiliation: str = "[Institution]", abstract: str = "[ABSTRACT PLACEHOLDER]", methods_section: str = "", table1_df: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None, model_results: Optional[Dict[str, Dict]] = None, bootstrap_results: Optional[Dict] = None, task_type: str = "regression", feature_names: Optional[List[str]] = None, target_name: str = "outcome", n_total: int = 0, n_train: int = 0, n_val: int = 0, n_test: int = 0, tripod_checklist: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None, data_config: Optional[Dict] = None, calibration_text: str = "", limitations: str = "[Discuss limitations here]", explainability_summary: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, sensitivity_summary: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, stat_validation_summary: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = None, manuscript_context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> str
keyFunctions.does: Assembles the whole .tex. Splits the incoming markdown into methods_latex + results_latex, and DISCARDS results_latex whenever model_results is truthy. Auto-scaffolds the abstract only when abstract is still the literal placeholder. tripod_checklist and data_config are accepted and never used.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Pure string builder except for the generate_decision_audit_trail() call at line 1004. Make that an injected parameter and the function becomes fully pure.

keyFunctions.name: compile_latex_to_pdf
keyFunctions.signature: compile_latex_to_pdf(latex_source: str, timeout: int = 30) -> Optional[bytes]
keyFunctions.does: Writes to a tempdir, runs pdflatex twice with -interaction=nonstopmode, returns PDF bytes or None. Returns None (not an error) when pdflatex is absent; swallows all exceptions to logger.debug.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: The single genuinely long-running, cancellable, failure-prone operation in this domain. Must become a Job with progress and a real error channel — today a 30s timeout produces an indistinguishable None.

keyFunctions.name: _build_structured_abstract_sections
keyFunctions.signature: _build_structured_abstract_sections(task_type: str, target_name: str, n_total: int, n_train: int, n_val: int, n_test: int, model_results: Optional[Dict[str, Dict]], bootstrap_results: Optional[Dict], manuscript_context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, feature_names: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> Dict[str, str]
keyFunctions.does: Returns {background_objective, methods, results, conclusions}. Uses the [INVESTIGATOR: ...] marker convention (NOT [AUTHOR REQUIRED]). Also called directly by pages/10 to build the markdown 'Abstract (Draft)' that manuscript_validator parses.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: THREE author-marker conventions coexist: [AUTHOR REQUIRED — …] (narrative_engine), [INVESTIGATOR: …] (here), [PLACEHOLDER: …] (here + publication.py). manuscript_validator only tolerates the latter two by exception. Unify to one before the rebuild.

keyFunctions.name: _convert_markdown_to_latex
keyFunctions.signature: _convert_markdown_to_latex(markdown_text: str) -> Tuple[str, str]
keyFunctions.does: Splits on r'\n## Results(?:\s*\(Draft\))?.*?\n' into (methods_latex, results_latex); converts '### X' to \\subsection, **bold** to \\textbf, `code` to \\texttt, strips '---' and stray '## ' lines, then escapes everything outside recognized LaTeX commands via nested helpers _escape_remaining_text and _convert_inline_markdown.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Round-trips structured prose through markdown and back. TurboTab should render LaTeX from ManuscriptDraft's typed fields and delete this parser.

keyFunctions.name: _metrics_to_latex_table / _table1_to_latex
keyFunctions.signature: _metrics_to_latex_table(model_results: Dict[str, Dict], task_type: str = "regression", bootstrap_results: Optional[Dict] = None) -> str  /  _table1_to_latex(table1_df: pd.DataFrame) -> str
keyFunctions.does: booktabs tables inside adjustbox with max width=\\textwidth; labels tab:model_performance and tab:table1; CIs rendered as 'val [lo, hi]'; font shrinks for wide tables.

keyFunctions.name: _escape_latex / _styled_placeholder / _normalize_generated_latex_text / _demote_results_subsections
keyFunctions.signature: _escape_latex(text: str) -> str  /  _styled_placeholder(text: str) -> str  /  _normalize_generated_latex_text(text: str) -> str  /  _demote_results_subsections(results_latex: str) -> str
keyFunctions.does: _escape_latex handles & % $ # _ { } ~ ^ < >. _styled_placeholder wraps markers in \\textcolor{gray}{\\textit{...}} while preserving the literal marker text (tests match on it). _normalize_generated_latex_text repairs generation artifacts: 'mainresults'->'main results', fused and/with, doubled stopwords, collapsed blank lines. _demote_results_subsections turns \\subsection into \\paragraph.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: _normalize_generated_latex_text is scar tissue for upstream text bugs. Its `\band(?!om|roid|ard|ate|width|rew)(?=[a-z]{4,})` rule will corrupt any legitimate word starting 'and' that is not on the exclusion list (e.g. 'andesite', 'andalusite' — plausible in geoscience datasets).

keyFunctions.name: _resolve_latex_manuscript_context / _format_abstract_population_sentence / _format_abstract_predictor_sentence / _model_display_name / _format_metrics_list / _human_join
keyFunctions.signature: _resolve_latex_manuscript_context(manuscript_context, model_results, bootstrap_results, feature_names) -> Dict[str, Any]  /  _format_abstract_population_sentence(upload_n: int, analysis_n: int) -> str  /  _format_abstract_predictor_sentence(feature_counts: Dict[str, Any], feature_names: Optional[List[str]]) -> str  /  _model_display_name(key: Optional[str]) -> str  /  _format_metrics_list(model_results, task_type='regression') -> str  /  _human_join(items: List[str]) -> str
keyFunctions.does: Frozen-context precedence for the LaTeX path; the two abstract sentences that manuscript_validator regex-parses ('Of N observations, M remained for analysis' / 'A total of N observations were available for analysis' / 'The final modeling set contained N predictors'); model naming with a 21-entry HARDCODED FALLBACK DICT duplicating MODEL_DISPLAY_NAMES.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: _resolve_latex_manuscript_context reads 'baseline_results' nowhere but generate_latex_report reads manuscript_facts.get('baseline_results') at line 772 — that key is never in the returned dict, so the baseline-comparison paragraph is unreachable dead code even though pages/10 does populate baseline_results in manuscript_context.

modules.purpose: The trust gate. Decides whether a draft is trustworthy enough to export, by re-parsing the RENDERED artifacts (markdown report text, methods text, LaTeX) with regexes and cross-checking them against the frozen manuscript_context and the Table 1 dataframe. Zero direct streamlit refs; transitively imports streamlit via ml.narrative_engine -> utils.insight_ledger.

keyFunctions.name: validate_manuscript_bundle
keyFunctions.signature: validate_manuscript_bundle(manuscript_context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]], methods_text: str, report_text: str, latex_text: str, task_type: str, table1_df: Any = None) -> ManuscriptValidationReport
keyFunctions.does: Runs 12 checks in fixed order and returns a report. How it decides a draft is trustworthy: (1) analysis population N identical in the abstract and in Methods>Study Design and equal to population_counts.analysis_total; (2) train_n+val_n+test_n == analysis_total; (3) final predictor count identical in abstract and Methods>Predictor Variables and equal to feature_counts.selected; (4) Table 1 'Overall (N=...)' header equals analysis_total (passes when Table 1 is absent); (5) every feature in feature_names_for_manuscript appears in a Table 1 row label; (6) every included model appears in BOTH Methods>Model Development and Methods>Model Evaluation; (7) selection-metric language matches task type — both the context's best_metric_name and any rendered invalid metric term in the model-development prose (regression must not mention accuracy/f1/auc/precision/recall; classification must not mention rmse/mae/r2/medianae); (8) primary-model statements internally consistent — 'selected as the primary model' and 'no manuscript-primary model was explicitly selected' must not co-occur and must agree with manuscript_primary_model; (9) abstract must not describe feature reduction when original == selected; (10) LaTeX free of raw [PLACEHOLDER] (bare, not '[PLACEHOLDER:'), [NOTE, markdown headings, markdown bold; (11) no internal model keys (any _MODEL_NAMES key containing '_') leaked into markdown or LaTeX; (12) no coaching phrases ('no action needed', 'favorable to analysis', 'workflow-derived abstract', '[applicable to') and no dangling punctuation ('..', 'Table X'/'Figure X', dash-then-period).
keyFunctions.transitionNote: This is textual post-hoc verification of prose the same process just generated. In TurboTab most of these should become type-level invariants on the Project/Record (counts computed once, models referenced by key not by rendered name), leaving only the genuinely textual checks (10)(12).

keyFunctions.name: ManuscriptValidationCheck / ManuscriptValidationReport
keyFunctions.signature: @dataclass ManuscriptValidationCheck(name: str, status: str, location: str, detail: str)  /  @dataclass ManuscriptValidationReport(checks: List[ManuscriptValidationCheck]) with @property failed_checks, @property passed, def to_rows() -> List[Dict[str,str]]
keyFunctions.does: status is the string 'PASS'/'FAIL'; passed == no FAILs. to_rows() produces the Status/Check/Location/Detail table pages/10 renders.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: to_rows() is the only view-shaped method; the rest is pure. Keep the report as data and let the Feed render it.

keyFunctions.name: _extract_section / _extract_latex_subsection
keyFunctions.signature: _extract_section(text: str, heading: str, level: int) -> str  /  _extract_latex_subsection(text: str, heading: str) -> str
keyFunctions.does: Regex-extracts a markdown section by exact heading text at a given '#' level, or a \\subsection{...} body. Called with the literal headings 'Abstract (Draft)' (level 2), 'Study Design', 'Predictor Variables', 'Model Development', 'Model Evaluation' (level 3).
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Hard-coupled to NarrativeEngine's exact heading vocabulary. The legacy publication.py fallback emits 'Study Design and Participants' and 'Performance Evaluation' — see landmines.

keyFunctions.name: _extract_analysis_n / _extract_final_predictor_count / _extract_table1_overall_n / _table1_contains_feature
keyFunctions.signature: _extract_analysis_n(text: str) -> Optional[int]  /  _extract_final_predictor_count(text: str) -> Optional[int]  /  _extract_table1_overall_n(table1_df: Any) -> Optional[int]  /  _table1_contains_feature(table1_df: Any, feature_name: str) -> bool
keyFunctions.does: Parses numbers back out of generated prose using three fixed sentence templates each; reads 'Overall (N=...)' out of a Table 1 column header; matches a feature against Table 1 index labels exactly or with a trailing comma (categorical level rows).

landmines.silentFailure: Any feed that orders cards by timestamp reorders itself when the user re-runs an earlier stage (re-running EDA after training places EDA below training). Any feed that orders by declaration puts the coach's shortlist rationale AFTER the training it informed. Neither ordering is wrong enough to look like a bug — it just makes the transcript incoherent.
landmines.mitigation: Add an explicit monotonically increasing sequence number and a stage_order constant to the Record, and record created_at separately from updated_at per section. Do this before any feed rendering is written.

landmines.what: WorkflowProvenance.from_dict silently drops any key not in the target dataclass's __dataclass_fields__, and schema_version is read but never branched on.
landmines.where: utils/workflow_provenance.py:584-655 (11 identical `{k: v for k, v in data[...].items() if k in X.__dataclass_fields__}` filters) and :588 (`prov.schema_version = data.get('schema_version', 1)`)
landmines.silentFailure: Rename or restructure any field during the rebuild and old saved sessions restore with that fact missing and schema_version still reporting 1. The manuscript compiler then treats the fact as 'NOT RECORDED' and honestly omits the section — the user sees a shorter, correct-looking manuscript with no indication that data was dropped.
landmines.mitigation: Branch on schema_version with explicit migrations, and log (or collect into the returned object) every dropped key. Test restoring a v1 payload into a v2 schema.

landmines.what: pages/10_Report_Export.py counts author inputs with a raw string count that includes the ownership preamble, while ManuscriptDraft.count_author_inputs() (which excludes it, and is pinned by a test) is never called by the app.
landmines.where: pages/10_Report_Export.py:2068 `st.session_state['methods_section'].count('[AUTHOR REQUIRED')` vs ml/narrative_engine.py:112-118 and tests/test_manuscript_trust.py::test_preamble_not_counted_as_author_input
landmines.silentFailure: The UI always reports one more outstanding author input than exist. The test that would catch it passes, because it tests the unused method.
landmines.mitigation: Call count_author_inputs(). More generally: audit for other engine methods the app has re-implemented inline — ManuscriptDraft.to_latex() is dead in the app for the same reason.

landmines.what: ml/publication.py _format_audit_timestamp assumes tz-naive timestamps are UTC, but every timestamp in the Record and Ledger is datetime.now().isoformat() — local time.
landmines.where: ml/publication.py:1747-1759 (`dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)`) versus utils/workflow_provenance.py (every record_* uses datetime.now()) and utils/insight_ledger.py:597 (created_at default)
landmines.silentFailure: Every line of the Decision Audit Trail in the LaTeX Supplementary is labelled 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC' but is actually local wall-clock time, off by the machine's offset. A reviewer reconciling the audit trail against anything else finds a systematic skew.
landmines.mitigation: Record timezone-aware UTC timestamps at the source (datetime.now(timezone.utc)) and render with an explicit conversion. Add a test asserting recorded timestamps carry tzinfo.

landmines.what: The ZIP omits the Record itself, and ships a competing copy of the same facts. provenance.json and coaching.json are written only by utils/session_manager's separate session-save; the export ZIP instead contains metadata.json, built independently from session_state.
landmines.where: pages/10_Report_Export.py:2242 generate_metadata() -> metadata.json; utils/session_manager.py:267-276 provenance.json (a different artifact, different file, different trigger)
landmines.silentFailure: metadata.json's dataset.n_rows is len(df) while the Record's n_total may be the analysis total; its splits come from split_config while SplitProvenance may hold different numbers; its models_trained comes from trained_models while TrainingProvenance.models_trained may differ after an invalidation. Two authoritative-looking records in the reviewer's hands, disagreeing, with no cross-check.
landmines.mitigation: Emit provenance.json (and the ledger) into the export package and derive metadata.json from the Record, or delete metadata.json. Add a consistency test asserting the two agree on n, splits and models.

landmines.where: pages/10_Report_Export.py — tripod_checklist.csv (:1907), table1_final.csv (:1941), table1_final.tex (:1946), methods_section.md (:2074), evidence_map.md (:2097), flow_diagram.mmd (:2132); ZIP builder at :2237-2445

modules.purpose: Ingest → combine → audit → configure the modeling problem → draw the test lockbox → choose cohort. 1,264 loc. This is the highest-stakes page in the app: it is where the leakage quarantine is established and where the invalidation DAG's root hash is computed. QUESTIONS ASKED (interview nodes): (1) 'Which file(s) hold your data?' [multi-upload csv/xlsx/xls/parquet/tsv/txt/json/jsonl/ndjson, 50 MB soft limit with 'Load anyway' escape]; (2) 'Which Excel sheet?' [sheet names, only when >1]; (3) 'Which part of this JSON holds your rows?' [layout.candidates from data_processor.inspect_json]; (4) 'Transpose this file (rows↔columns)?' [yes/no, per file]; (5) 'Name this dataset' [free text, default = filename stem]; (6) 'Replace the existing dataset with this name?' [yes/no, suppressed when name+shape match — i.e. it IS the same file]; (7) 'Add a built-in practice dataset?' [utils.datasets.get_builtin_datasets() keys]; (8) 'Rename / Remove dataset?' [per-dataset]; (9) 'How should these files be combined?' [delegated to utils.combine_ui.render_combine_step]; (10) 'Apply this suggested fix?' [Drop constant columns | Drop duplicate rows — see suggested_actions]; (11) 'What type of analysis do you want to perform?' [Prediction | Hypothesis Testing — NO default, hard st.stop() until answered]; (12) 'Target variable (what you want to predict)?' [numeric+categorical selectable cols]; (13) 'Feature variables?' [multiselect, default = ALL non-reserved candidates, + Select All / Clear All]; (14) 'Override auto-detected task type?' [yes/no → regression | classification]; (15) 'Held-out test fraction?' [slider 0.05–0.40 step 0.05, default DEFAULT_TEST_FRACTION=0.15]; (16) 'Exploratory mode (disable test-set quarantine)?' [yes/no, sticky watermark]; (17) 'Run on a cohort subset?' [delegated to utils.cohort_ui.render_cohort_chooser]; (18) destructive: 'Modify Data Setup' / 'Change Merge Setup' / 'Clear Current Session' [with confirm gate]. EXTRACTION DIFFICULTY: ENTANGLED. The page is ~40% genuine domain logic and it is the logic everything downstream depends on. The ordering is load-bearing and documented in comments (lines 1200-1203): lockbox must exist and config must be saved BEFORE cohort choice, because every cohort run inherits a slice of ONE split.

[iqr | mad | zscore | percentile, sidebar, drives the whole page AND downstream profile]; (2) 'Which column to inspect?' [all columns]; (3) 'Filter features' [All Features | Numeric (n) | Categorical (n) | High Missing (n) — pills]; (4) gallery page [1..ceil(n/regime.gallery_page_size)]; (5) 'Correlation method?' [Pearson | Spearman]; (6) 'Highlight threshold' [0.0–1.0 step 0.05, default 0.8]; (7) target-gallery page; (8) 'Feature Explorer: X axis / Y axis / Color by' [feature_cols; color options None + target + features]; (9) 'Embedding view?' [PCA Biplot | UMAP | Persistence Diagram | Mapper Graph — gated by regime.macro_shape_tiers, only when ≥16 features]; (10) 'Run this diagnostic?' × 13 actions in 3 tabs — Model Readiness: linearity_scatter, residual_analysis (regression only), normality_residuals (regression only), multicollinearity_vif, influence_diagnostics (regression only); Feature Quality: plausibility_check (only when physiology reference matches), leakage_scan, missingness_scan, data_sufficiency_check, feature_scaling_check; Advanced: interaction_analysis, dose_response_trends (regression only), outlier_influence, target_profile, quick_probe_baselines; (11) Table 1: 'Stratify by' [None + categoricals with ≤10 levels], 'Continuous variables' [numeric, default first 10 of feature_cols], 'Categorical variables' [default first 5], 'Show p-values' (on) / 'Show SMD' (off) / 'Show missing counts' (on). EXTRACTION DIFFICULTY: ENTANGLED — the plotting is view, but _auto_generate_insights() is ~340 lines of threshold-based scientific judgment that the Router and the manuscript both consume, and every @st.cache_data closure has a hand-rolled `data_id=_data_fingerprint` invalidation key that must become explicit engine arguments.

keyFunctions.signature: def _auto_generate_insights()  [line 199, ~343 lines]
keyFunctions.does: THE EDA rule engine. Emits 13 distinct Insight ids with fixed thresholds: eda_sufficiency_insufficient (sufficiency=='critical'), eda_sufficiency_borderline ('scarce'/'limited'), eda_leakage_{col} (|r|>0.95 vs target), eda_corr_cluster_{...} (BFS connected components over high_corr_pairs), eda_missing_severe (>30%), eda_missing_moderate (5–30%), eda_target_skew (|skew|>1.5, regression), eda_class_imbalance (ratio<0.35), eda_skew_group (|skew|>2.0 per feature), eda_opportunity_clean_data (0 blockers/warnings AND ≥5 features), eda_opportunity_strong_signal (max|r|>0.7), eda_opportunity_nonlinear (mean Spearman−Pearson gap>0.08), eda_opportunity_high_np (n/p>100), eda_opportunity_balanced (ratio>0.7). Each carries manuscript_text, model_scope, relevant_pages, tripod-relevant metadata.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Split: the THRESHOLD RULES are engine (pure: profile+signals+regime → List[Insight]); the ledger.upsert calls are record. Insight IDS ARE AN API — pages 03/05/06/10 resolve by exact id. Renaming one silently orphans its resolution.

modules.purpose: VERDICT: 5,162 loc that is ~95% STATIC EXPLANATORY CONTENT — migrate as DATA, not code. Evidence: 274 st.markdown blocks, 61 st.latex equations, 26 references([...]) bibliography calls, 8 st.tabs groups (one per chapter), ZERO reads of application data (no get_data, no pandas import, no data_config), and exactly TWO session_state touches — popping 'theory_target_chapter' for coaching deep-links (line 215) and seeding the chapter selectbox (line 217). The remaining ~5% is 18 self-contained interactive teaching demos that generate SYNTHETIC data with numpy and render Plotly figures. QUESTIONS ASKED: only one real navigation question — 'Choose a chapter' [Data Quality & Assumptions | Feature Engineering & Selection | Model Families | Preprocessing Theory | Evaluation & Validation | Statistical Testing | Sensitivity & Robustness | Reporting Standards (TRIPOD)] — plus 24 demo-local sliders that are toys, not answers (skew intensity, transform lambda, outlier x/y, trim quantile, correlation, ridge/lasso alpha, dimensionality p, imbalance %, leakage p, model noise, bias-variance k, decision threshold, CV folds k + noise, miscalibration, SHAP glucose/BMI/age, interaction strength, subgroup disparity, seed noise, bootstrap B). EXTRACTION DIFFICULTY: EASY for the content (it is prose + LaTeX + citations in a fixed 8-chapter × N-tab structure with 8 repeating card types: intro, section, app_connection, cite, takeaway, worked_example, visual_guide, misconception, self_check, references), ENTANGLED-BY-DUPLICATION for the demos — utils/theory_demos.py already contains 19 portable copies of the same demos with page_context-namespaced keys, and page 11 does NOT import them. The two copies have already drifted (theory_demos' demo_skewness uses height=300 and a shortened 'Train your eye' string; page 11's uses height=320 and the full text).

Wrong rows produce a plausible y vector, so permutation importance, external-validation labels, and subgroup stratification are quietly computed against mismatched outcomes. pages/07 wraps the whole reconstruction in `except Exception: pass` (line 204-205) and falls back to X_test — hiding even the loud case.
landmines.mitigation: Stop passing positions. The split should emit a TestSet carrying its own index labels (the lockbox already stores LABELS, not positions — utils/test_lockbox line 411 uses `set(_lockbox['labels'])`). Make row identity label-based end to end.

landmines.what: Page 03 rebinds `selected_features` mid-file, so one name means two different things.
landmines.where: pages/03_Feature_Engineering.py line 118 binds `selected_features = data_config.feature_cols or [non-target columns]` (the modeling feature set); line 423 REBINDS `selected_features = st.multiselect('Features', numeric_features, ...)` (the features chosen for math transforms). Line 1218 then reads it: `st.session_state['pre_fe_feature_cols'] = list(data_config.feature_cols) if data_config.feature_cols else list(selected_features)`.
landmines.silentFailure: When data_config.feature_cols is empty, pre_fe_feature_cols is set to the TRANSFORM selection instead of the original feature list. reset_downstream_results then 'restores' that wrong list into both selected_features and data_config.feature_cols (utils/session_state.py ~307-313), permanently shrinking the model's feature set on a Reset/Skip. Also line 495 (`untransformed = [f for f in _skew_ins.affected_features if f not in selected_features]`) depends on the second binding — correct there, which is why the shadowing looks intentional.
landmines.mitigation: Rename before touching anything else. During extraction, each tab's answer must be its own named field on a FeatureRecipe; there should be no page-scoped mutable name shared across seven tabs.

landmines.what: Every technique tab mutates one shared X_engineered frame and mirrors it back into three session keys by hand — 12 near-identical write triples.
landmines.silentFailure: Miss one of the three and the frame, the name list, and the log go out of sync. The removal path at 1148-1156 already does exactly this — it updates X_engineered and engineered_features but NOT engineering_log, so a removed feature keeps its 'created' entry in the log that becomes provenance and manuscript text.
landmines.mitigation: One append(operation) API returning a new recipe state. Never three parallel assignments.

landmines.what: Two independent, drifting copies of the theory demos.
landmines.where: pages/11_Theory_Reference.py contains 18 inline demos (lines 442, 581, 710, 1045, 1151, 1327, 1408, 2075, 2172, 2706, 3408, 3565, 3728, 3880, 3981, 4108, 4678, 4829); utils/theory_demos.py contains 19 portable `demo_*(page_context, expanded, wrapped)` functions covering the same concepts. Page 11 does NOT import theory_demos; only utils/coaching_ui.py uses the anchors path.
landmines.silentFailure: Already drifted — demo_skewness in utils uses height=300 and an abbreviated 'Train your eye' paragraph, page 11's uses height=320 and the full text. A rebuild that migrates the page and keeps the util (or vice versa) silently ships the losing variant, or ships both and they diverge further.
landmines.mitigation: Diff all 18/19 pairs, pick a winner per demo, delete the other. Page 11 also has demos with NO util counterpart (model-family fits at 2172, PDP-hides-interaction at 3981, subgroup disparity at 4108, target trimming at 905) and utils has demos with no page counterpart — inventory before deleting.

landmines.what: The export ZIP — joblib dumps of every model and every preprocessing pipeline, plus server-side PNG rendering of every figure — is rebuilt on EVERY page render, before the user clicks anything.
landmines.where: pages/10_Report_Export.py lines 2234-2445, unconditional module-level code. Also unconditional per render: _build_latex_export_bundle (1802), generate_latex (1819-1839, cache-keyed), generate_report (1846), validate_manuscript_bundle (1958), and PDF compilation (2019-2023, cache-keyed).
landmines.silentFailure: Not silent in behaviour (it is slow), but silent in ATTRIBUTION — a typed character in the 'Paper title' box triggers the whole pipeline, and figure-export failures are counted into _plot_export_failures and surfaced only as an aggregate warning at 2448-2454. save_matplotlib_fig (2188) does not count its failures at all, so missing SHAP images are invisible.
landmines.mitigation: This is the clearest Jobs candidate in the codebase: export = one cancellable job with progress and a per-artifact success/failure manifest. Make save_matplotlib_fig count failures like its plotly twin before porting.

landmines.what: TDA features are dataset-level constants tiled into every row — zero variance, yet they enter selection, training, and importance rankings.
landmines.where: pages/03_Feature_Engineering.py lines 839-844: `tda_features_array = np.array(tda_features_list).reshape(1,-1)` then `np.tile(tda_features_array, (n_samples,1))`. The comment at 772-774 confirms the intent (one point cloud → dataset-level summary).
landmines.silentFailure: Constant columns cannot help any model, but they survive: page 04 excludes only NON-numeric features, LASSO/RFE will simply give them zero weight, and page 01's constant-column detector runs on the AUDIT frame, not on the engineered frame. They then appear in the feature count reported to reviewers.
landmines.mitigation: Either drop them at creation with an explanation, or record them as dataset-level metadata rather than columns. At minimum re-run the constant-column check after feature engineering.

landmines.what: Baselines and the export cohort are each derived from an arbitrary or recomputed source, so they describe slightly different populations than the models.
landmines.where: pages/06 lines 2122-2124 borrow `fitted_preprocessing_pipelines[first_model]` for ALL baselines even though pipelines are per-model and can differ. pages/10 _build_analysis_cohort_df (lines 527-554) re-derives the trim thresholds from the full non-null target, whereas pages/06 lines 425-427 compute them from TRAINING rows only and never drop test rows.
landmines.silentFailure: Both produce valid-looking numbers. Table 1 describes a population the models were not trained on; baselines are preprocessed under a config the user may have selected for a different model family.
landmines.mitigation: Materialize the analysis cohort ONCE at split time as a Project artifact and have Table 1, baselines, and the flow diagram all read it. Give baselines their own explicit, documented preprocessing choice.

landmines.what: Training cancellation does not cancel anything.
landmines.where: pages/06_Train_and_Compare.py lines 1251-1266: `st.session_state.cancel_training` is initialized, and a '🛑 Cancel Training' button is rendered ONCE before the model loop; clicking it sets the flag and calls st.stop(). The flag is never read inside the per-model loop (1268-1609) or inside optimize_model_hyperparameters. Page 07's cancel (lines 319-356, 419-421, 542-544) DOES check between models and between analyses — a different, better design in the same codebase.
landmines.silentFailure: The button says 'Training canceled. Trained models saved.' — but a running fit continues to completion; the message describes a state the code did not reach.
landmines.mitigation: Real Job semantics with cooperative cancellation checkpoints. Take page 07's between-unit checks as the minimum bar and the honest per-step progress as the model.

landmines.what: Multiclass SHAP explains one class at compute time and a different class at render time.
landmines.where: pages/07_Explainability.py lines 476-495 (compute): `if isinstance(sv_raw, list)` → len==2 takes index 1 labelled 'Class 1 (Positive)', otherwise index 0 labelled 'Class 0'; `if sv_plot.ndim == 3` → `sv_plot[:, :, -1]` (LAST class). Lines 768-771 (render) repeat the ndim==3 rule on the stored array.
landmines.silentFailure: For >2 classes the stored class_label can say 'Class 0' while the array is the last class, or the stored 2D array gets re-sliced. Plots and labels are individually plausible.
landmines.mitigation: Normalize once, at compute time, into an explicit {class_index, class_label, values} record and never re-normalize at render.

landmines.what: Two independent robustness verdict systems are shown side by side and can contradict each other.
landmines.where: pages/08_Sensitivity_Analysis.py lines 253-260 (coefficient-of-variation bands: <2% highly robust, <5% moderately robust, <10% some instability, else unstable) and lines 304-321 (absolute-range bands: <0.03 'publication-ready without caveats', <0.05 'moderate', else 'high sensitivity'). Only the CV number reaches provenance (lines 227-239, record_sensitivity(seed_stability_cv=...)); only the range-based `stability` string reaches the LLM context (line 351).
landmines.silentFailure: A metric with a small absolute range but a small mean (e.g. R²=0.05±0.02) reads 'Very stable' on range and 'Unstable' on CV, on the same screen. Downstream, the manuscript records one and the interpretation records the other.
landmines.mitigation: Pick one verdict function, name it, use it everywhere, and record the raw statistics alongside the verdict.

landmines.what: Page 02 is the sole producer of dataset_profile, which three later pages silently require.
landmines.where: pages/02_EDA.py line 166 `st.session_state['dataset_profile'] = profile` is the only writer. Consumers: pages/05 lines 178, 192 (Model Coach, smart defaults' outlier/missing/skew detection, generate_preprocessing_insights), pages/06 lines 861-862 (model_viability), 927-931 (NN recommender), 1736-1769 (class-imbalance panel), pages/10 line 86 (metadata + report sections).
landmines.silentFailure: Skipping EDA is legal — no page blocks on it. The Model Coach block (05:194) is `if _profile:`, so the coach, the evidence probe, the auto-model-selection and all scoped insights simply do not render; smart defaults fall back to scaling='standard' and missing_indicators=False; page 06 shows no viability verdicts and no class-imbalance handling even on imbalanced data. Nothing says why.
landmines.mitigation: Make profile computation a Project-level artifact computed on demand (it is already a pure ml.dataset_profile call), not a side effect of visiting a page. This is the single most important Router consequence in the audit: today the app's intelligence is gated on navigation.

domain: APPLICATION STATE — st.session_state → AnalysisProject (utils/session_state.py 657loc/92 st refs, utils/test_lockbox.py 295loc, utils/cohorts.py, utils/session_manager.py, utils/state_reconcile.py) plus the invalidation DAG, the test-set lockbox/quarantine contract, and the 3 import cycles that all pass through this layer.

modules.purpose: Schema (5 dataclasses) + the invalidation DAG + data accessor + methodology→ledger bridge. THE hard file: 92 st refs, 16 importers, 10 pages.

keyFunctions.name: TaskTypeDetection
keyFunctions.signature: @dataclass TaskTypeDetection(detected: Optional[Literal['regression','classification']]=None, confidence: Optional[Literal['low','med','high']]=None, reasons: List[str]=[], override_enabled: bool=False, override_value: Optional[...]=None); property final

keyFunctions.transitionNote: Pure data, asdict-safe. Move verbatim. `.final` must stay a property, not be flattened — page 01/05/06/07/10 and state_reconcile all read `.final`, not `.detected`.

keyFunctions.name: CohortStructureDetection
keyFunctions.signature: @dataclass CohortStructureDetection(detected, confidence, reasons, override_enabled, override_value, entity_id_candidates: List[str], entity_id_detected: Optional[str], entity_id_override_enabled: bool, entity_id_override_value: Optional[str], time_column_candidates: List[str]); properties final, entity_id_final

keyFunctions.transitionNote: `entity_id_final` is a LOAD-BEARING quarantine input, not a display field. Whatever replaces this must be resolved BEFORE the lockbox is drawn.

keyFunctions.name: SplitConfig
keyFunctions.signature: @dataclass SplitConfig(train_size=0.7, val_size=0.15, test_size=0.15, random_state=42, stratify=False, use_time_split=False, datetime_col=None, target_trim_enabled=False, target_trim_lower=0.0, target_trim_upper=1.0, target_transform='none')

keyFunctions.name: ModelConfig

keyFunctions.name: init_session_state
keyFunctions.signature: init_session_state() -> None
keyFunctions.does: Seeds 38 keys with defaults via `if key not in st.session_state`, then lazily constructs InsightLedger.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Becomes AnalysisProject.__init__ / default field values. NOTE: it is called at the top of EVERY page, so it silently resurrects any key that a reset POPPED — this is how split_config reappears as defaults after a reset with no message.

keyFunctions.name: get_data
keyFunctions.signature: get_data(full_study: bool = False) -> Optional[pd.DataFrame]
keyFunctions.does: Precedence df_engineered > filtered_data > raw_data, then `apply_cohort(df)` unless full_study=True. full_study is used by exactly two callers: page 01 (line 619) and cohort_ui._advance_to (line 324).
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Split it: Project.active_frame(full_study) stays in project (it reads 3 keys + the cohort). The cohort filter itself is engine (pure: labels+frame→frame). Do NOT let engine functions take a raw dataframe from the caller without the cohort already applied — utils/cohorts.py's own docstring names this as the failure the module exists to prevent.

keyFunctions.name: _content_fingerprint
keyFunctions.signature: _content_fingerprint(df: pd.DataFrame) -> Optional[int]
keyFunctions.does: hash((df.shape, int(pd.util.hash_pandas_object(df, index=False).sum()))); returns None on unhashable cells.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Pure — move to engine. But see landmines: int64 sum overflow + pandas-version instability + the None fallback silently downgrades set_data to schema-only invalidation.

keyFunctions.name: set_data
keyFunctions.signature: set_data(df: pd.DataFrame, is_schema_change: Optional[bool] = None) -> None
keyFunctions.does: Normalizes a non-unique index (reset_index(drop=True)); stores raw_data + _raw_data_fingerprint; pops filtered_data. Then: schema change → reset_data_dependent_state(); same-schema content change → clear_cohort() + reset_downstream_results(); identical content → no-op.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: The three-way branch IS the top of the DAG. The index-uniqueness normalization is a quarantine precondition (tests/test_review_fixes.py::test_non_unique_index_reset_before_storage) — it must run before any lockbox can exist.

keyFunctions.name: reset_downstream_results
keyFunctions.signature: reset_downstream_results(clear_feature_engineering: bool = True, restore_pre_fe_features: bool = True, clear_feature_selection: bool = True) -> None
keyFunctions.does: The single source of truth for downstream invalidation. 10 ordered node groups, ~60 keys, + provenance section nulling + ledger rollback/prune. Full node-by-node breakdown in the dedicated module entry below.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Becomes AnalysisProject.invalidate(from_stage). The three booleans are really three DAG entry points (FE, feature-selection, everything-else) and should become an explicit stage enum, not flags.

keyFunctions.name: reset_data_dependent_state
keyFunctions.signature: reset_data_dependent_state() -> None
keyFunctions.does: Full reset for a new dataset: config + detections + cohort + lockbox + ledger + provenance + methodology_log, then reset_downstream_results(restore_pre_fe_features=False).
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Does NOT clear raw_data, working_table, datasets_registry, task_mode, random_seed, _data_config_features_hash, exploratory_mode, test_lockbox_fraction. Two of those omissions are landmines (see below).

keyFunctions.name: get_preprocessing_pipeline
keyFunctions.signature: get_preprocessing_pipeline(model_key: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[Pipeline]
keyFunctions.does: per-model pipeline with fallback to the legacy single pipeline.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Returns a live sklearn Pipeline — in TurboTab this must return an ARTIFACT HANDLE, and the pipeline is materialized by the Jobs worker.

keyFunctions.name: set_preprocessing_pipeline
keyFunctions.signature: set_preprocessing_pipeline(pipeline: Pipeline, config: Dict[str, Any]) -> None
keyFunctions.does: Sets the legacy single pipeline + config.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Legacy path; only page 03/05 write it. Candidate for drop once per-model is universal.

keyFunctions.name: set_preprocessing_pipelines
keyFunctions.signature: set_preprocessing_pipelines(pipelines_by_model: Dict[str, Pipeline], configs_by_model: Dict[str, Any], base_config: Dict[str, Any]) -> None
keyFunctions.does: Sets per-model pipelines/configs AND back-fills preprocessing_pipeline with pipelines_by_model.get('default') or the first value.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: `if default_pipeline:` uses truthiness on a sklearn Pipeline — a Pipeline with steps is truthy, but this is a latent __bool__/__len__ trap if the object type ever changes.

keyFunctions.name: get_splits
keyFunctions.signature: get_splits() -> Optional[tuple]
keyFunctions.does: Returns (X_train,X_val,X_test,y_train,y_val,y_test) or None if X_train is None.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Split arrays are big-but-serializable → blob/parquet side-table, not the JSON project.

keyFunctions.name: set_splits
keyFunctions.signature: set_splits(X_train, X_val, X_test, y_train, y_val, y_test, feature_names: List[str]) -> None
keyFunctions.does: Writes the 6 split keys + feature_names. Does NOT write train_indices/val_indices/test_indices — page 06 writes those separately, ~40 lines later.

keyFunctions.name: add_trained_model
keyFunctions.signature: add_trained_model(name: str, model: Any, results: Dict[str, Any]) -> None
keyFunctions.does: trained_models[name]=model; model_results[name]=results.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: `model` is a live fitted object → artifact store. `results` is JSON-safe metrics → project. This one function is the exact serializable/non-serializable seam.

keyFunctions.name: log_methodology
keyFunctions.signature: log_methodology(step: str, action: str, details: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> None
keyFunctions.does: Appends to methodology_log; for REPLACE_STEPS ({'Upload & Audit','Feature Engineering','Feature Selection Applied','Preprocessing','Model Training','Explainability'}) it last-wins-replaces the previous entry with the same step. Always calls _log_to_ledger.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Two parallel records (methodology_log list + ledger) for the same fact. InsightLedger.get_methodology_log() already reconstructs the list format — collapse to the ledger and derive the list.

keyFunctions.name: _log_to_ledger
keyFunctions.signature: _log_to_ledger(step: str, action: str, details: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> None
keyFunctions.does: Upserts a pre-resolved Insight per methodology call; fixed id `method_<step>` for _REPLACE_STEP_IDS, action-slug id otherwise; infers action_type from step; tags _AUDIT_ONLY_STEPS={'EDA'} with metadata={'audit_only':True}. Wrapped in `except Exception: pass`.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: The bare `except Exception: pass` is a silent-failure generator (landmine). In Record it must log, not swallow.

keyFunctions.name: _STEP_TO_PAGE / _STEP_TO_CATEGORY / _REPLACE_STEP_IDS / _AUDIT_ONLY_STEPS
keyFunctions.signature: module-level Dict[str,str] / Set[str]
keyFunctions.does: Maps 11 methodology step names to the 10 page ids and 10 ledger categories.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: These hard-code the 10-page workflow. TurboTab has no pages — the page id becomes a STAGE id, and every literal '01_Upload_and_Audit'…'10_Report_Export' in the ledger, provenance, and reset code must be renamed in ONE commit or the rollback/prune sets silently match nothing.

keyFunctions.name: _lockbox_signature
keyFunctions.signature: _lockbox_signature(df: pd.DataFrame, target_col: str, task_type: str, fraction: float, seed: int, group_col: Optional[str] = None) -> str
keyFunctions.does: Returns f'{content}|{df.shape}|{target_col}|{task_type}|{fraction:.4f}|{seed}|{group_col or ""}' where content = int(pd.util.hash_pandas_object(df, index=False).sum()) with a two-level fallback (shape|columns|notna-count, then str(shape)). COVERS: the entire frame's cell values, its shape, the target, the task type, the fraction (4dp), the seed, and — because ensure_lockbox:137-138 passes f'{group_col}|{"+".join(sorted(stratify_cols or []))}' into the group_col slot — the grouping column AND the requested strata. DOES NOT COVER: the index labels themselves, column ORDER (hash_pandas_object is column-order sensitive in practice but df.shape is not), or the cohort filter.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Pure — move to engine. But it hashes the WHOLE frame, so any cell change anywhere forces a redraw. In TurboTab the signature should cover only (row-label set, target values, task, fraction, seed, group_col, strata) — not unrelated columns.

keyFunctions.name: detect_repeated_subjects
keyFunctions.signature: detect_repeated_subjects(df: pd.DataFrame, candidate_cols: Optional[list] = None) -> Optional[Tuple[str, int, int]]
keyFunctions.does: Returns (column, n_subjects, n_rows) for the column with the MOST distinct values that passes all of: 2 <= nunique < len(df); 1.5 <= len(df)/nunique <= 50; and the lowercased name contains one of ('id','seqn','subject','participant','patient','record','case','person'). Skips duplicate column labels (isinstance(s, pd.DataFrame)) and unhashable columns (TypeError on nunique).
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Pure. INTERACTION WITH GROUPING: ensure_lockbox:130-133 calls it ONLY when the caller passed no group_col, so a declared entity_id_final always wins (pages/01:1073). If it fires, group_col is set → GroupShuffleSplit is attempted → but only if nunique >= _MIN_GROUPS_FOR_GROUPED_LOCKBOX (8); below that, line 191 sets group_col=None and the split falls back to a stratified row split. The substring test is what stops 'sex' (2 levels, 100 rows each → rows_per=100 > 50) and unique IDs (k >= n) from being treated as subjects; both are pinned by tests.

keyFunctions.name: ensure_lockbox
keyFunctions.signature: ensure_lockbox(df: pd.DataFrame, target_col: str, task_type: str, fraction: Optional[float] = None, seed: Optional[int] = None, group_col: Optional[str] = None, stratify_cols: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]
keyFunctions.does: Order of operations: (1) bail to get_lockbox() if df/target missing; (2) fraction ← arg else session test_lockbox_fraction else 0.15; seed ← arg else session random_seed else 42; (3) eligible = df.index[y.notna()]; bail if len(eligible) < 10; (4) if no group_col, auto-detect; drop group_col if not in df.columns; (5) compute signature; RETURN EXISTING UNCHANGED if signature matches; (6) if group_col and nunique(groups) >= 8 → GroupShuffleSplit(n_splits=1, test_size=fraction, random_state=seed), else group_col=None; (7) ONLY IF the grouped attempt produced nothing: _build_stratum() then train_test_split(eligible, test_size, random_state=seed, stratify=...) with a ValueError fallback to unstratified; (8) build the dict; (9) IF an existing lockbox had DIFFERENT labels → reset_downstream_results(clear_feature_engineering=False) + set _lockbox_redrawn=True; (10) write test_lockbox.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: This function does three jobs: decide (pure), mutate state, and fire the invalidation cascade. Split into engine `draw_lockbox(frame_summary, spec) -> LockboxSpec` and project `Project.ensure_lockbox(spec)` that compares signatures and calls invalidate(). Step 7's placement AFTER step 6 is deliberate and load-bearing (tests/test_cohorts.py::test_stratification_survives_a_grouped_split_falling_back) — do not reorder.

keyFunctions.name: _build_stratum (inner)
keyFunctions.signature: _build_stratum() -> Tuple[Optional[pd.Series], List[str]]
keyFunctions.does: Composite stratum: always the target for classification, then each stratify_col that exists and is not the target. Combines with str.cat(sep='|'), then DROPS the least important variable (parts.pop()) until counts.min() >= 2 AND (counts*fraction).min() >= 1, returning (None, []) if nothing fits.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: Pure given (y, df, eligible, fraction, task_type, stratify_cols). The returned `used` list is what lands in lb['strata'] and is asserted verbatim by tests/test_cohorts.py::test_the_strata_actually_used_are_recorded.

keyFunctions.name: AnalysisProject.invalidate — THE DAG AS A METHOD
keyFunctions.signature: PROPOSED invalidate(self, from_stage: Stage, *, keep: Set[Stage] = frozenset()) -> InvalidationReport
keyFunctions.does: Replaces reset_downstream_results' three booleans with a stage graph: DATA → FE → FEATURE_SELECTION → PREPROCESS → SPLIT → TRAIN → EXPLAIN/SENSITIVITY/STATS → REPORT. Returns a REPORT (what was cleared, what was kept) instead of mutating silently.
keyFunctions.transitionNote: The current API cannot express 'clear FE but keep the selection'; the three flags encode only the three combinations that happen to be needed. A stage graph makes the eight existing call sites declarative and makes a missing key a schema error rather than a stale value.

Same for cohorts: apply_cohort/clear_cohort become pure functions over (frame, CohortRunSpec) and the Project holds the spec. Final layering: engine (lockbox math, cohort math, fingerprints) ← project (AnalysisProject: owns lockbox+cohort+invalidate) ← record ← router ← jobs ← view. NOTE the 4th latent chain: session_state:190/442 and :600 import utils.insight_ledger, which imports ml.publication, which imports utils.insight_ledger — cycle 1 is reachable from the state layer too.

landmines.silentFailure: Engineer features in exploratory mode → turn exploratory mode off → train → export. The manuscript claims a clean held-out evaluation, and there is no warning anywhere, because the flag that would have watermarked it was removed by the very reset that was supposed to guarantee cleanliness. The in-file rationale at :412-415 ('only quarantine-clean if EVERY surviving result was computed with the lockbox on') is correct — the implementation just does not hold when a survivor is kept.
landmines.mitigation: Make quarantine_ever_off monotone: it can be cleared ONLY by a full data reset, never by a partial one. Better: tag every derived artifact with the quarantine state it was produced under, and let the manuscript ask the artifacts rather than a global flag.

landmines.what: exploratory_mode survives reset_data_dependent_state(), and it is a Streamlit WIDGET key that only page 01 knows how to claim from the deferred restore dict.
landmines.where: utils/session_state.reset_data_dependent_state:418-445 never touches it; pages/01_Upload_and_Audit.py:1158 `st.checkbox(..., key='exploratory_mode')`; session_manager._SAFE_WIDGET_KEYS:131 stores it; pages/01:1130-1143 is the ONLY place that pops it out of _pending_widget_state_restore.
landmines.silentFailure: (a) Upload a brand-new dataset while exploratory mode is on: the full reset clears everything except the quarantine-off flag, so the new study starts with no test-set protection and no banner. (b) Restore an exploratory session and go anywhere except page 01: is_exploratory() reads False, the app behaves as if quarantined, but the restored artifacts were produced without quarantine.
landmines.mitigation: quarantine_off becomes an ordinary persisted Project field with no widget backing; include it in the full reset; and on load, apply it before any stage renders.

landmines.what: session_manager's lockbox serialization is LOSSY (7 of 10 fields) while preserving the signature that suppresses a redraw.
landmines.where: utils/session_manager.py:298-306 encodes only labels/fraction/seed/n_total/n_test/signature/stratified; :565-573 restores the same 7. `strata`, `group_col` and `n_test_groups` are dropped. ensure_lockbox:139-141 returns the existing lockbox unchanged when the signature matches.
landmines.silentFailure: A restored session that was originally split BY SUBJECT comes back believing it was a plain row split: render_lockbox_status stops saying 'so no subject appears on both sides', the disclosure sentence vanishes from the manuscript, and cohort/lockbox reporting loses the grouping claim — while the labels (and therefore the actual protection) are still correct, so nothing looks wrong.
landmines.mitigation: Serialize the whole LockboxSpec. Add strata/group_col/n_test_groups to the encoder and decoder, and assert round-trip equality in a test.

landmines.what: Lockbox labels are coerced to str for any non-integer index type on save.
landmines.where: utils/session_manager.py:288-296 `_plain_label`: bool→str, int→int, numpy scalar→.item() then int-or-str, everything else→`str(x)`. The comment correctly explains the numpy-int case but the str fallback is the remaining hole.
landmines.silentFailure: A float, datetime, or string-with-different-repr index round-trips to labels that match nothing in the restored frame. train_row_mask then returns all-True for every row, is_exploratory() is False, no banner fires, and the quarantine is silently gone for the rest of the session.
landmines.mitigation: Store label_dtype alongside the labels and re-cast on load; on restore, assert |set(labels) ∩ set(frame.index)| == n_test and raise a visible SessionLoadError otherwise (the loader already has a warnings channel for exactly this).

landmines.what: _lockbox_signature and _content_fingerprint both rest on int(pd.util.hash_pandas_object(df, index=False).sum()), which silently wraps on int64 overflow, varies across pandas versions, and returns None/degrades on unhashable cells.
landmines.where: utils/test_lockbox.py:46 and utils/session_state.py:228 (`except Exception: return None` → set_data falls back to schema-only invalidation, per the docstring at :224-226).
landmines.silentFailure: Two materially different frames can produce the same sum (wraparound is a real collision channel over large frames), so set_data treats a genuine data change as a benign rerun and every stale model, metric and figure survives. Conversely a pandas upgrade changes the hash for identical data, so the first render after a deploy redraws the lockbox and wipes the user's work with a banner that says the data changed.
landmines.mitigation: Use an explicit, version-pinned digest (e.g. blake2b over the parquet bytes of a canonicalized frame) and store the digest algorithm id in the Project. Never let 'cannot fingerprint' silently mean 'unchanged' — make it mean 'assume changed'.

landmines.what: reset_downstream_results restores data_config.feature_cols only when it is ALREADY truthy.
landmines.where: utils/session_state.py:311-313: `dc = st.session_state.get('data_config'); if dc is not None and getattr(dc, 'feature_cols', None): dc.feature_cols = list(pre_fe)`. pages/03:1218 falls back to `list(selected_features)` when data_config.feature_cols is empty, so the empty-feature_cols state is reachable.
landmines.silentFailure: After an FE reset with an empty data_config.feature_cols, selected_features is restored but data_config.feature_cols stays empty. Page 06 works (it prefers selected_features), so nothing errors — but ml/publication:213-215 and pages/10 read data_config.feature_cols and produce a manuscript with an empty predictor list.
landmines.mitigation: Drop the truthiness guard and make the two lists one field. If they must stay separate during migration, assert they are equal at every stage boundary.

landmines.what: ledger.prune_auto_generated({'02_EDA','05_Preprocess','06_Train_and_Compare'}) runs on EVERY reset, including the feature-selection reset that explicitly asks to keep the selection.
landmines.where: utils/session_state.py:407-410 — outside both `if clear_feature_selection` blocks. Called from pages/04:447 and :494 with clear_feature_selection=False.
landmines.silentFailure: Applying a consensus or manual feature selection deletes every auto-generated EDA insight (skew, missingness, leakage, collinearity findings). Today they come back because the user can revisit page 02. In TurboTab's single scrolling interview there is no revisit — the findings are gone permanently, and the manuscript's limitations section quietly shrinks.
landmines.mitigation: Gate the prune on the same stage graph as the rest: pruning EDA insights is only correct when the DATA changed, not when the feature list did. Make invalidate() return the prune set so it is visible and testable.

landmines.what: Provenance sections upload and statistical_validation are never nulled, and hypothesis_test_results IS cleared.
landmines.where: utils/session_state.py:379-385 `_sections = ['eda','split','preprocessing','training','explainability','coach']` — statistical_validation and upload are absent; :353 pops hypothesis_test_results.
landmines.silentFailure: After a reset, WorkflowProvenance.statistical_validation still lists the tests that were run, get_completeness() reports statistical_validation=True, and the generated Methods section asserts hypothesis tests whose results were just deleted. The Router (which will key off get_completeness) will also believe that stage is done and never re-ask the question.
landmines.mitigation: Null statistical_validation with the rest. Keep `upload` deliberately (it survives because it describes the data configuration, which the reset preserves) but assert that explicitly in a test so the omission reads as a decision.

landmines.what: split_config is POPPED by the resetter but re-created with DEFAULTS by the next init_session_state().
landmines.where: utils/session_state.py:330 pops it inside the node-3 loop; :135 seeds `'split_config': SplitConfig()` and :183-185 re-applies any missing default at the top of every page.
landmines.silentFailure: A 60/20/20 split with target_transform='yeo-johnson' and target trimming silently reverts to 70/15/15, transform='none', no trimming after any downstream reset. Nothing tells the user; Prepare Splits just uses different settings than the ones on screen a moment ago.
landmines.mitigation: Reset to an explicit default instance and surface it in the InvalidationReport, or exclude configuration objects from the pop loop entirely (they are configuration, not results — which is the resetter's own stated contract).

landmines.what: ensure_lockbox is fed the ENGINEERED frame once feature engineering exists, so both its content signature and its subject-ID auto-detection run against generated columns.
landmines.where: pages/01_Upload_and_Audit.py:619 `df = get_data(full_study=True)` → utils/session_state.get_data:207-215 returns df_engineered when present → pages/01:1074 `ensure_lockbox(df, target_col, task_type_final, group_col=_entity_col)` → utils/test_lockbox.py:46 hashes the whole frame and :131 `detect_repeated_subjects(df)`.
landmines.silentFailure: (a) The signature changes purely because FE added columns, so revisiting the upload step after FE can redraw the lockbox and fire a downstream reset. (b) Worse: detect_repeated_subjects scans engineered column NAMES; any generated column containing 'id'/'case'/'record'/'person' with 1.5–50 rows per level flips the split to GroupShuffleSplit, producing a completely different sealed set and a subject-level split the user never asked for.
landmines.mitigation: Draw and validate the lockbox against the PRE-FE frame only (the frame that defined the modeling problem), and pass the candidate subject columns explicitly (detect_repeated_subjects already accepts candidate_cols) rather than scanning every column.

landmines.what: Two independent resets fire for one user action on a content change.
landmines.where: utils/session_state.set_data:276-280 detects a same-schema content change → clear_cohort() + reset_downstream_results(); then on the same render pages/01:1074 calls ensure_lockbox, whose signature also changed → a second reset_downstream_results(clear_feature_engineering=False) plus a NEW test set at test_lockbox.py:226-231.
landmines.silentFailure: A one-column cleaning action on a variable that is neither the target nor a feature redraws the sealed test set. Every prior number becomes incomparable, and the two resets interleave with the ledger prune/rollback so that which insights survive depends on ordering rather than on intent.
landmines.mitigation: Make the lockbox signature depend only on (eligible row labels, target values, task_type, fraction, seed, group_col, strata) — not on unrelated columns. Then a cleaning action on an unrelated column leaves the sealed set intact, which is also the methodologically correct answer.

landmines.what: ensure_lockbox returns the PREVIOUS lockbox (not None) when it cannot draw a new one, and the caller cannot tell the difference.
landmines.where: utils/test_lockbox.py:114-115 and :123-124 both `return get_lockbox()`; pages/01:1076-1104 then reads `_lb['fraction']`, `_lb['n_test']`, `_lb['seed']`, `_lb['signature']` and writes a resolved Insight asserting the holdout.
landmines.silentFailure: After a target change that leaves too few non-null rows, or a target column that no longer exists, the page happily reports and LEDGERS a holdout that describes a different modeling problem. The manuscript then contains 'A 15% test set (n=147) was held out at upload' for a study that has no valid lockbox.
landmines.mitigation: Return a discriminated result (Drawn | Unchanged | Refused(reason)) instead of an Optional dict, and let the caller/Router surface the refusal as the next question.

landmines.what: Every provenance and ledger write in pages/ is wrapped in a bare `except Exception: pass`.
landmines.where: utils/session_state._log_to_ledger:655-656; pages/01:1105-1106 and :1194; pages/03:1268-1269; pages/04:471-472; pages/06 (record_split); and ~15 more sites, all commented 'Provenance recording should never break the workflow'.
landmines.silentFailure: Any schema drift in the Record layer during the migration — a renamed section, a changed record_* signature, a page id that no longer exists — produces a manuscript that is quietly missing its Methods statements, its TRIPOD completions and its audit trail, with zero diagnostics anywhere.
landmines.mitigation: Replace the swallow with a structured error appended to a Project-level `record_errors` list that the Feed can surface. Keep the 'never break the workflow' property; drop the 'never tell anyone' property.

landmines.what: All three import cycles are currently invisible because every edge is a function-local import, and the obvious refactor (methods on AnalysisProject) turns them into module-level cycles.
landmines.where: Cycle 1: utils/insight_ledger.py:1077 ↔ ml/publication.py:98,155,1739,1829. Cycle 2: utils/cohorts.py:474 ↔ utils/test_lockbox.py:269. Cycle 3: utils/session_state.py:216,278,428 ↔ utils/cohorts.py ↔ utils/test_lockbox.py:228. Plus a fourth latent chain: utils/session_state.py:190,442,600 → utils/insight_ledger → ml/publication → utils/insight_ledger.
landmines.silentFailure: Nothing fails today, so a mechanical port that keeps the same call graph looks correct until the imports move to module scope — at which point the app fails to boot with an ImportError that points at whichever module happened to be imported first, not at the design problem.
landmines.mitigation: Fix the layering before moving anything: engine (lockbox math, cohort math, fingerprints, TRIPOD_ITEMS, model vocabulary) ← project (AnalysisProject owns lockbox + cohort + invalidate) ← record ← router ← jobs ← view. Concretely: extract TRIPOD_ITEMS and the MODEL_* vocabulary into leaf data modules; make draw_lockbox/apply_cohort pure and parameterized; and invert control so nothing below Project ever calls reset_downstream_results.

landmines.what: engineering_log is not persisted while df_engineered, feature_engineering_applied and engineered_feature_names are.
landmines.where: utils/session_manager.py:91-117 _PLAIN_KEYS includes engineered_feature_names, engineered_feature_transforms and pre_fe_feature_cols but NOT engineering_log; utils/session_state.py:305 pops it on FE reset; ml/publication.py:601 reads it for the Methods section.
landmines.silentFailure: Save and restore a session with engineered features: the engineered frame and its column names come back, the app looks fully restored, but the list of transforms that produced them is gone — so the Methods section silently stops describing how the features were built.
landmines.mitigation: Add engineering_log to the serialized recipe (it is a plain List[str]). More generally: audit every ml/publication.py session_state read (32 refs) against session_manager's persist buckets — anything the manuscript reads must survive a restore or the restore is lossy in exactly the dimension the app exists for.

landmines.what: cohort_runs_done is not persisted, and completed_runs() filters on isinstance(r, CohortRun).
landmines.where: utils/cohorts.py:462-465 and :488; utils/session_manager.py — cohort_runs_done appears in no bucket, so it is dropped on save and never restored.
landmines.silentFailure: Save a session mid-way through 'model the men, then model the women' and reload: the cross-cohort comparison table and comparison_caveats() come back empty, the run sequencer's position/of counters restart, and the multiple-comparisons disclosure that comparison_caveats() generates silently disappears from the manuscript.
landmines.mitigation: Persist cohorts_done as a list of dicts and rebuild via a CohortRun.from_dict (the dataclass is already JSON-safe). The isinstance filter must then accept the reconstructed objects — today it would silently discard restored dicts.

landmines.what: InsightLedger.from_list uses .add() (skip duplicates) rather than .upsert(), and Insight.to_dict omits manuscript_text.
landmines.where: utils/insight_ledger.py:1346-1355 (from_list → ledger.add(...) inside `except (TypeError, KeyError): continue`) and :617-644 (to_dict lists 23 fields; manuscript_text is not among them).
landmines.silentFailure: (a) A save file containing two entries with the same id silently keeps the first and drops the second. (b) manuscript_text — the field that exists specifically so coaching voice never reaches the manuscript — is lost on every save/restore, so restored sessions fall back to _clean_for_manuscript(finding) and the Discussion section quietly changes register.
landmines.mitigation: Use upsert in from_list, add manuscript_text to to_dict, and add a round-trip property test (to_list → from_list → to_list is identity) — the ledger is the Record layer's whole contract and currently has no such test.

findings.item: Row identity is TWO incompatible conventions: index LABELS (lockbox/cohort) vs POSITIONS (train/val/test_indices)
findings.detail: utils/test_lockbox.py stores `labels` as index LABELS and `train_row_mask()` tests `lbl not in test_set`. But pages/06 computes `original_indices = np.where(mask)[0]` — POSITIONAL offsets into the frame returned by `get_data()` at split time — and stores `st.session_state.train_indices/val_indices/test_indices = original_indices[...].tolist()`. Page 07 then does `df_raw.iloc[test_indices]` against a FRESH `get_data()` call. If the row set changed between Train and Explain (cohort started/cleared, `filtered_data` written by page 05, FE re-applied, a cleaning action dropping rows) the .iloc selects DIFFERENT PEOPLE with no error — SHAP/permutation/subgroup results are then computed on the wrong rows and silently exported. If the frame shrank, it is an IndexError instead. AnalysisProject must pick ONE identity (labels) and store masks, not offsets.
findings.action: project — store split membership as index labels (Index/boolean mask) in the Project; drop the positional *_indices keys entirely

findings.item: Page 03 Feature Engineering hand-rolls a partial cascade instead of calling reset_downstream_results()
findings.detail: The Save handler clears 18 keys inline but MISSES: pdp_results, bootstrap_results, baseline_results, calibration_results, cv_results, train_indices/val_indices/test_indices, target_transformer, target_label_encoder, y_train_original/y_val_original/y_test_original, feature_names, feature_names_by_model, cv_strategy, cv_groups_train, eda_results, dataset_profile, plus the ledger rollback and provenance-section clearing that reset_downstream_results() performs. Result: after FE is applied, Report Export still shows bootstrap CIs, calibration slopes and baseline comparisons for models that no longer exist, and Explainability re-uses a stale target_label_encoder. reset_downstream_results' own docstring says it is the single source of truth ("Any page that introduces a new result key must add it here") — page 03 violates it.
findings.action: project — the invalidation DAG must be the ONLY writer of downstream clears; delete the inline block

findings.item: macro_shape's @st.cache_data functions exclude the DataFrame from the cache key
findings.detail: `compute_pca(_df_numeric, ...)`, `compute_umap(_df_numeric, ...)`, `compute_persistence(_df_numeric, ...)`, `compute_mapper(_df_numeric, ...)` all take the frame as a LEADING-UNDERSCORE argument, which is Streamlit's marker for 'do not hash this'. The remaining key is scalar defaults only, so a second dataset with identical scalar params returns the FIRST dataset's cached PCA/UMAP/persistence/Mapper result. The codebase already knows the correct pattern — pages/02_EDA.py:146 passes an explicit `data_id=_data_fingerprint` alongside `_df`. macro_shape omits it.
findings.action: engine — make these pure functions with an explicit content-fingerprint argument; move memoization into the Jobs layer

findings.item: ml/eda_actions.py imports a function that does not exist, inside a bare except — 4 insights are silently never recorded
findings.detail: `from utils.storyline import add_insight` appears 4 times; utils/storyline.py defines only render_breadcrumb, _get_navigation_order, get_prev_next_pages, render_page_navigation. Each call is wrapped in `try: ... except: pass`, so physio_plausibility, missingness_association, target_outliers and collinearity insights have been silently dropped. DANGER IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: leaving the dead import in place keeps hiding 4 findings; 'fixing' the import during migration will suddenly start emitting 4 new ledger entries that flow into the manuscript narrative, changing generated text and TRIPOD status for every existing project.
findings.action: record — decide deliberately: port them to insight_ledger.upsert() as a versioned behavior change, or drop them; never leave the silent except

findings.item: Page 10 reads data_audit['missing_counts'] which page 01 never writes
findings.detail: pages/01 builds `audit_results` with keys 'cardinality', 'dtypes', 'missing' (list of records), 'duplicates', 'numeric_stats' and assigns it to `st.session_state.data_audit`. pages/10 twice tests `if data_audit and 'missing_counts' in data_audit` to build the manuscript's missing-data summary. That key is never present, so the missing-data statement in the Methods section silently falls through to the dataset_profile path or is omitted entirely.
findings.action: record — data_audit is a Record artifact; define its schema once and make the report read the declared field

findings.item: record_split() reads three SplitConfig attributes that do not exist — target trimming never reaches the manuscript
findings.detail: `target_trim_enabled=bool(getattr(split_config, 'trim_target', False))`, `target_trim_lower=float(getattr(split_config, 'trim_lower', 0.0))`, `target_trim_upper=float(getattr(split_config, 'trim_upper', 1.0))`. SplitConfig's real fields are `target_trim_enabled`, `target_trim_lower`, `target_trim_upper` (utils/session_state.py:78-80). The getattr defaults mask the typo, so SplitProvenance always records 'no trimming' even when rows were removed — the generated Methods section understates the exclusions and the flow diagram's N is wrong.
findings.action: record — bug; the Project must expose typed accessors so a renamed field is an AttributeError, not a silent default

findings.item: st.session_state['task_type'] is read but never written anywhere in the codebase
findings.detail: `_task_type = st.session_state.get('task_type', '')` then `_selection_metric = 'RMSE' if _task_type == 'regression' else 'Accuracy'`. Since the key is never set, TrainingProvenance.selection_criteria is ALWAYS recorded as 'validation Accuracy' — including for every regression study. The manuscript's model-selection sentence is wrong for half of all projects.
findings.evidence: pages/06_Train_and_Compare.py:1648-1650; no writer found for key 'task_type' repo-wide
findings.action: record — bug; Project.task_type must be a single computed property with no string-keyed shadow

findings.item: Four sources of truth for task type, consulted inconsistently by page
findings.detail: (1) `TaskTypeDetection.detected` (2) `TaskTypeDetection.final` property (override-aware) (3) `DataConfig.task_type` — explicitly marked DEPRECATED at utils/session_state.py:65 but still the value page 01 writes (4) the never-written `session_state['task_type']`. Page 06 branches on `task_type_final` but passes `data_config.task_type` into perform_cross_validation and into the y_test_proba guard; pages 07, 08 and 10 use `data_config.task_type` exclusively. Page 08 does `task_type = getattr(data_config, 'task_type', 'regression') or 'regression'` — a stale/blank DataConfig silently produces regression metrics for a classification model.
findings.action: project — one `task_type` property on AnalysisProject; delete DataConfig.task_type

findings.item: y_test_proba can be referenced unbound when task_type_final and data_config.task_type disagree
findings.detail: `y_test_proba` is assigned only inside the classification branch (`else:` of `if task_type_final == 'regression'`). The results dict then evaluates `y_test_proba if data_config.task_type == 'classification' else None`. If task_type_final=='regression' while data_config.task_type=='classification' (possible whenever the override is toggled without a config re-save), the conditional's true-branch dereferences an unbound name → NameError, swallowed by the surrounding `except Exception as e` and shown as a generic 'Training failed' with no cause.
findings.action: project — eliminated by collapsing task_type to one source; the bare Exception handler around the training loop must be narrowed in the Jobs layer

findings.item: get_data() precedence makes page 05's plausibility filter a silent no-op after Feature Engineering
findings.detail: `get_data()` returns df_engineered if present, ELSE filtered_data, ELSE raw_data. Page 05 writes `st.session_state['filtered_data'] = filtered_df` when any model uses plausibility_mode='filter'. If FE was applied first (the normal order), df_engineered wins and the plausibility filter is silently discarded — the pipeline was configured and n_output_features measured against filtered rows, but training runs on unfiltered rows. Worse, reset_downstream_results() does NOT pop filtered_data (only set_data and reset_data_dependent_state do), so it persists stale across dataset content changes.
findings.action: project — model row-filters as an explicit ordered stack of masks on the Project, not a precedence chain of shadow DataFrames

findings.item: Feature Selection silently drops all categorical predictors while telling the user it does not
findings.detail: Page 04 computes `numeric_features` only, shows `st.info("...These features are retained in your dataset and can still be used for modeling.")`, then on Apply does `data_config.feature_cols = consensus` where consensus is drawn exclusively from numeric_features. Every categorical predictor is removed from the modeling feature set, contradicting the on-screen promise. Manual selection has the same defect (`options=numeric_features`).
findings.action: router — the question 'which predictors survive selection' must return a full feature set; engine keeps numeric-only ranking but the Project must union back the non-ranked columns

findings.item: session_manager writes every DataFrame with to_parquet(index=False) while lockbox and cohort identify rows by index label
findings.detail: `_df_to_parquet_bytes` drops the index; on restore pandas assigns a fresh RangeIndex. lockbox.json restores `labels` verbatim (and deliberately coerces them to int/str to avoid a type mismatch). If raw_data/working_table carried anything other than a contiguous 0..n-1 RangeIndex at save time — any frame produced by a merge, a row-dropping cleaning action, or a cohort slice — the restored labels name different rows. `train_row_mask` then returns a wrong mask with no error, and the 'sealed' test set is silently no longer sealed.
findings.evidence: utils/session_manager.py:169-172, :278-306; utils/test_lockbox.py:16-17 ("stores index LABELS ... so membership survives"), :247-248
findings.action: project — persist the index explicitly (to_parquet(index=True)) and add a restore-time assertion that every lockbox label exists in the restored index

findings.item: Lockbox save/restore drops group_col, strata and n_test_groups
findings.detail: The encoder writes only labels, fraction, seed, n_total, n_test, signature, stratified. A grouped (split-by-subject) lockbox restores as an ungrouped one: render_lockbox_status stops disclosing 'split by subject', and any manuscript sentence derived from it understates the leakage control that was actually applied. Because `signature` is restored, ensure_lockbox will NOT redraw and thus never recover the lost fields.
findings.action: record — round-trip the whole lockbox dict; it is a Record artifact, not a cache

findings.item: Active cohort run and completed runs are not persisted at all
findings.detail: `cohort_run` and `cohort_runs_done` appear in none of _DATAFRAME_KEYS/_DATACLASS_KEYS/_PLAIN_KEYS/_NEVER_PERSIST. A save taken mid-cohort-run restores with the lockbox intact but no cohort filter, so get_data() silently returns the WHOLE study under a session that was labelled 'women'. CohortRun is a dataclass with only JSON-safe fields, so this is an omission, not a technical limit.
findings.action: project — cohort membership is core Project state; add it to the serialized schema with the same label-integrity check as the lockbox

findings.item: EDA (page 02) runs target-aware analyses on ALL rows including the sealed test set
findings.detail: test_lockbox.py's module docstring states 'Every target-aware step upstream of Train & Compare — feature-engineering fits, feature selection, target-association views — operates on training rows only, via train_row_mask()'. Page 02 never calls train_row_mask; it uses `df = get_data()` unfiltered. The target-aware actions target_profile, dose_response_trends, collinearity_map, leakage_scan and especially quick_probe_baselines (which does its OWN 80/20 train_test_split on all rows and fits models) therefore see held-out people. dataset_profile — which drives the model coach's picks — is likewise computed on all rows.
findings.action: router — the Router owns 'may this question see test rows'; engine functions must take an explicit row mask rather than deciding for themselves

findings.item: Preprocessing pipelines are stored FITTED on a sample, then re-fit at train time — two different fitted states share one slot
findings.detail: Page 05 does `pipeline.fit(X_sample); X_transformed = pipeline.transform(X_sample)` purely to record `n_output_features`, then stores the (now fitted-on-a-sample) Pipeline in `preprocessing_pipelines_by_model`. Page 06 later calls `model_pipeline.fit(X_train)` on the SAME object, mutating it in place, and stores it again under `fitted_preprocessing_pipelines`. Both dict entries can end up aliasing one mutated object. Anything that reads preprocessing_pipelines_by_model after training (page 10 export context) gets a pipeline fitted on training rows, not the configured-but-unfitted recipe it thinks it has.
