findings.action: project — separate 'recipe' (config, JSON-serializable) from 'fitted artifact' (pickle-only, job output); never let one object be both

findings.item: get_provenance() only catches ImportError, not the no-script-run-context error
findings.detail: `try: import streamlit as st; if 'workflow_provenance' not in st.session_state ... except ImportError: return WorkflowProvenance()`. In a background worker streamlit imports fine but touching st.session_state raises StreamlitAPIException/RuntimeError, which is not caught. Every engine path that records provenance will hard-crash the first time it runs off the main script thread — which is exactly what the Jobs layer introduces.
findings.action: record — provenance must be passed in explicitly, never fetched from ambient context

findings.item: Five session keys are read by Report Export but written by nobody
findings.detail: `shap_values` (pages/10:288, :1754), `partial_dependence` (pages/10:289, :1756 — only ever cleared, never populated: page 07 writes `pdp_results`), `explainability_robustness` (pages/10:290), `bland_altman_results` (pages/10:1526-1534, :1760 AND ml/publication.py:1174), `sensitivity_feature_dropout` (pages/10:877 — page 08 writes `sensitivity_dropout_results`). Bland-Altman and feature-dropout can therefore NEVER appear in the manuscript even after the user runs them.
findings.action: drop the dead aliases; record — wire sensitivity_dropout_results and a real bland_altman artifact into the Record

findings.item: Report Export computes n_train/n_val/n_test with len() over values that are legitimately None
findings.detail: `train_n = len(st.session_state.get('X_train', []))` — init_session_state sets 'X_train': None, so .get returns None (not the default) and len(None) raises TypeError. Occurs in both _build_manuscript_context and _build_methods_section_for_export. Currently masked only because the page gates on trained_models existing; any reordering during migration exposes it.
findings.action: project — Project.splits should be a single Optional[Splits] object; absent means absent, not a dict of Nones

findings.item: Report's analysis cohort N is recomputed with different trim semantics than the split actually used
findings.detail: _build_analysis_cohort_df applies target trimming using quantiles of the WHOLE frame. Page 06 deliberately computes trim thresholds from TRAINING rows only when the lockbox applies, and never drops test rows (`trim_mask = trim_mask | pd.Series(is_test_row, ...)`). The manuscript's reported analysis N and Table 1 population can therefore differ from the population that was actually modeled, with no warning.
findings.action: record — persist the realized cohort membership at split time; the report must read it, never re-derive it

findings.item: Two different precedence rules for 'the current feature list'
findings.detail: Page 03 uses `data_config.feature_cols if data_config.feature_cols else [c for c in df.columns if c != target]` — it ignores session_state.selected_features entirely. Pages 05/06/07/10 use `st.session_state.get('selected_features') or data_config.feature_cols`. After FE, selected_features is overwritten with EVERY engineered column (`[col for col in df_engineered.columns if col != target]`), so the two lists routinely disagree and page 03 re-engineers from the pre-selection list.
findings.action: project — one ordered feature list on the Project with an explicit provenance tag (uploaded / engineered / selected); delete the duplicate

findings.item: ml/eda_actions.py functions take st.session_state as a positional argument
findings.detail: All 17 action functions have the signature `(df, target, features, signals, session_state) -> Dict`. Two of them actually read it: `session_state.get('unit_overrides', {})` and `session_state.get('eda_outlier_method', 'iqr')`. The other 15 accept it and ignore it. This is the single biggest false coupling in ml/ — replacing the 5th parameter with an explicit typed options object frees the whole module.
findings.action: engine — change the signature to (df, target, features, signals, opts: EdaOptions); Project supplies opts

findings.item: Boundary Upload→WorkingTable: datasets_registry
findings.detail: `Dict[dataset_id -> pd.DataFrame]`, plus `merge_steps: List`, `last_merge_columns: List[str]`, `_combine_signature: str`, `_working_table_source_id`. Serialization: DataFrames go to parquet under datasets/entry_N.parquet with a name map in datasets/index.json; dataset_id keys are stringified on save and never converted back, so an int id restores as a str id and `single_dataset['id'] in st.session_state.datasets_registry` fails silently → 'Dataset not in memory'.
findings.action: project — typed DatasetId; restore must round-trip key types

findings.item: Boundary Upload→Target: raw_data + _raw_data_fingerprint
findings.detail: `raw_data: pd.DataFrame` (parquet-serializable, index currently lost), `_raw_data_fingerprint: Optional[int]` from `hash((df.shape, pd.util.hash_pandas_object(df, index=False).sum()))` — returns None on unhashable cells, in which case set_data falls back to schema-only invalidation and a genuine content change is silently NOT invalidated. The fingerprint is not persisted, so the first set_data after a restore sees old_fp=None and skips the content-change branch.
findings.evidence: utils/session_state.py:220-230, :259-280; not in any session_manager key list
findings.action: project — fingerprint is the DAG's invalidation input; it must be a first-class persisted field with an explicit 'unknown' state

findings.item: Boundary Upload→Target: DataConfig / SplitConfig / ModelConfig / TaskTypeDetection / CohortStructureDetection
findings.detail: All five are plain @dataclass, all fields JSON-safe, all round-tripped via asdict() + field-filtered reconstruction. DataConfig(target_col, feature_cols, datetime_col, task_type). SplitConfig(train_size, val_size, test_size, random_state, stratify, use_time_split, datetime_col, target_trim_enabled, target_trim_lower, target_trim_upper, target_transform). TaskTypeDetection and CohortStructureDetection each expose a computed `.final` property that asdict() does NOT capture — restore is lossless only because the underlying fields are stored.
findings.action: project — these five dataclasses are the cleanest existing prototype for AnalysisProject sub-objects; keep them nearly as-is

findings.item: Boundary Upload→Target: test_lockbox dict
findings.detail: `{labels: List[label], fraction: float, seed: int, n_total: int, n_test: int, signature: str, stratified: bool, strata: List[str], group_col: Optional[str], n_test_groups: Optional[int]}`. JSON-serializable IF labels are coerced to plain int/str. `signature` embeds a pandas content hash; ensure_lockbox rebuilds only on signature change, and a rebuild that changes labels calls reset_downstream_results(clear_feature_engineering=False) as a SIDE EFFECT from inside utils/, plus sets a `_lockbox_redrawn` flag the page must pop to disclose it.
findings.action: project — the lockbox belongs to Project; the cascading reset must move out of the accessor and into the invalidation DAG

findings.item: Boundary Upload→Target: cohort_run dict and cohort_runs_done
findings.detail: cohort_run = `{column, value, label, labels: List[index-label], n_rows, n_total, position, of, order, target_col, dropped_features}`. cohort_runs_done = `List[CohortRun]` (dataclass: column, label, n_train, n_test, dropped_features, completed, metrics). apply_cohort() silently returns `df.iloc[0:0]` and sets `_cohort_filter_broken` when neither the labels nor the grouping column resolve — an EMPTY table rather than a wrong one, which is the right choice but only if the UI surfaces cohort_filter_broken().
findings.action: project (membership) + view (the broken-filter banner)

findings.item: Boundary Upload→EDA: data_audit
findings.detail: `Dict[str, Any]` with keys 'cardinality': List[dict], 'dtypes': List[dict], 'missing': List[dict] (records), 'duplicates': int (numpy int64 — not JSON-safe without coercion), 'numeric_stats': dict-of-dicts from DataFrame.to_dict(). Fully recomputable from raw_data; listed in _NEVER_PERSIST is FALSE — it is simply absent from every taxonomy list, so it is dropped on save with no note.
findings.action: engine (recompute) — do not persist; but the report must stop reading it (see missing_counts finding)

findings.item: Boundary EDA: dataset_profile (DatasetProfile)
findings.detail: Nested dataclass tree: DatasetProfile{feature_profiles: Dict[str, FeatureProfile], target_profile: Optional[TargetProfile], warnings: List[DataWarning], data_sufficiency: DataSufficiencyLevel (an Enum), recommended/cautioned/discouraged_families: List[str], ...}. The Enum member makes plain asdict()+json fail without a converter. Currently in _NEVER_PERSIST (recomputed on page 02). Consumed by ml.model_coach.select_top_picks and model_viability, and by page 05/06's coach panels.
findings.action: engine (pure computation) + record (persist the derived verdicts the manuscript cites, not the whole object)

findings.item: Boundary EDA: DatasetSignals is recomputed on every page-02 load and NEVER stored
findings.detail: `compute_dataset_signals(df, target, task_type, cohort_type, entity_id, outlier_method, feature_cols)` -> DatasetSignals (all JSON-safe fields: lists, dicts, floats, Optional[Literal]). It is held only in a local, memoized by @st.cache_data with an explicit data_id. Every eda_action takes it as its 4th positional argument. Nothing downstream can see it — leakage_flags, collinearity_summary and physio_plausibility_flags never reach the Report except via whatever an action happened to write into the ledger.
findings.action: project — signals is a legitimate derived-state node in the DAG; materialize it so Router and Report can both read it

findings.item: Boundary EDA→FeatureEng: eda_results
findings.detail: `Dict[action_id -> {'findings': List[str], 'warnings': List[str], 'figures': List[plotly/matplotlib Figure], 'stats': dict}]`. The 'figures' entries make this NOT JSON-serializable and not reliably picklable (matplotlib figures). Correctly in _NEVER_PERSIST. Page 09 also reads eda_results.
findings.action: engine returns (data, figure-spec); view renders — figures must never enter Project state

findings.item: Boundary EDA→Report: table1_df / table1_metadata / custom_table1_tests / table1_group,pval,smd,miss
findings.detail: table1_df: pd.DataFrame; table1_metadata: dict; the four table1_* toggles are widget-keyed booleans/strings read directly by pages/10's _build_manuscript_table1. Page 10 REGENERATES its own manuscript Table 1 from _build_analysis_cohort_df() rather than using page 02's — so the Table 1 the user reviewed on page 02 and the one in the manuscript are computed from different row sets.
findings.action: record — one Table 1 artifact produced once, at a defined boundary; view renders it in both places

findings.item: Boundary FeatureEng: fe_work_in_progress
findings.detail: `{'X_engineered': pd.DataFrame, 'engineered_features': List[str], 'engineering_log': List}` — an unsaved scratch buffer keyed by `fe_features_hash` (md5 of the sorted feature list). Not persisted, correctly. It holds a full DataFrame copy in memory alongside raw_data, working_table, df_engineered and filtered_data — up to five copies of the dataset simultaneously.
findings.action: jobs — the interview's in-progress FE state is a draft the Jobs layer owns; do not persist the frame

findings.item: Boundary FeatureEng→FeatureSel: df_engineered and its five satellite keys
findings.detail: df_engineered: pd.DataFrame built as `pd.concat([X_engineered, y], axis=1)` — preserves the index (good: lockbox labels survive) but moves the target to the LAST column and changes column order. Satellites: feature_engineering_applied: bool, engineered_feature_names: List[str], engineering_log: List (or Dict — record_feature_engineering defensively handles both), engineered_feature_transforms: Dict[str, str] (double-transform guard consumed by page 05 and ml/publication.py:1403), pre_fe_feature_cols: List[str] (restore point for Reset/Skip).
findings.action: project — engineered frame is derived state; the log + transform map are Record

findings.item: Boundary FeatureSel: feature_selection_results and consensus_features
findings.detail: feature_selection_results: `List[FeatureSelectionResult]` (@dataclass, ml/feature_selection.py:13). consensus_features: List[str]. Both are cleared by reset_downstream_results ONLY when clear_feature_selection=True — page 04's own Apply passes clear_feature_selection=False so the selection survives the cascade it triggers. This conditional-clear flag is the most subtle part of the existing invalidation contract and must survive the port verbatim.
findings.action: project — the DAG needs an explicit 'this node is the one being recomputed, do not clear it' rule rather than a boolean parameter

findings.item: Boundary FeatureSel→Preprocess: X is passed as .values, losing the index
findings.detail: `X = df.loc[mask, numeric_features].values; y = df.loc[mask, target_col].values`, then median-imputed with a throwaway SimpleImputer. The mask correctly ANDs `df[target_col].notna() & train_row_mask(df.index)` — page 04 is the ONE page that honours the lockbox properly. But the numpy conversion means the selection results carry no row provenance.
findings.action: engine — selectors should take (DataFrame, mask) and return names; Project owns the mask

findings.item: Boundary Preprocess→Train: preprocessing_pipelines_by_model
findings.detail: `Dict[model_key -> sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline]` — PICKLE-ONLY, explicitly in _NEVER_PERSIST. Rebuilt by ml.pipeline.build_preprocessing_pipeline(...23 kwargs...). The companion `preprocessing_config_by_model: Dict[model_key -> Dict]` IS JSON-safe and IS persisted, which is the correct split: recipe travels, fitted object does not. Note reconcile_pipeline_columns() exists purely to self-heal a pipeline whose ColumnTransformer names columns that no longer exist — a symptom of the missing DAG.
findings.action: project (config) + jobs (fitted artifact, cached by config hash)

findings.item: Boundary Preprocess→Train: preprocessing_summary, preprocess_built_model_keys, unit_overrides, interpretability_mode
findings.detail: preprocessing_summary: nested Dict of {method,label} pairs + n_numeric/n_categorical/models_configured — JSON-safe, consumed by the Methods generator. preprocess_built_model_keys: List[str] — drives page 06's model checkbox pre-selection AND the 'no pipeline' badge. unit_overrides: Dict[str,str] read by ml/eda_actions.plausibility_check. interpretability_mode: str. preprocessing_summary is NOT in any persistence list.
findings.action: record (summary) + router (built_model_keys is a readiness signal, not a UI detail)

findings.item: Boundary Preprocess→Train: the coach writes page-06 widget keys directly
findings.detail: `for pick in _coach_picks: st.session_state[f'train_model_{pick.model_key}'] = True`, guarded by a one-shot `_coach_applied` flag. Page 06 reads the same key namespace at :814 and :887 and additionally force-sets it True for every key in preprocess_built_model_keys. This is the existing advisor→router seam and it is implemented as cross-page widget-key mutation — the single most fragile thing to port.
findings.action: router — this IS the Router in embryo; replace with an explicit Router decision the Feed renders, never a widget-key write

findings.item: Boundary Preprocess→Train: coach_probe_result (ProbeResult)
findings.detail: @dataclass with float/str/List[str] fields plus four computed @property verdicts (has_signal, nonlinearity_gain, data_hungry, underpowered). asdict() captures fields but NOT the properties — correct, since they are derived. Persisted as coach_probe.json (schema 2.1). Cleared by reset_downstream_results with an explicit comment that a probe verdict must never outlive the data it measured.
findings.action: record — a measured verdict is evidence; keep it in the Record with its data fingerprint attached

findings.item: Boundary Train: X_train/X_val/X_test are DataFrames but y_* type varies by split branch
findings.detail: X_* are always pd.DataFrame (X.iloc[idx]). y_* are pd.Series in the lockbox and stratified branches, but raw np.ndarray in the group-split branch (`y_arr = to_numpy_1d(y)`) and the time-split branch. set_splits() normalizes only when a target transform is applied (via to_numpy_1d); otherwise the heterogeneous type propagates to every consumer. Page 08 does `list(X_train.columns) if hasattr(X_train,'columns')` precisely because of this.
findings.action: project — Splits must be one typed object with a single normalized representation; do the coercion once at construction

findings.item: Boundary Train: target_transformer is a UNION of a string sentinel and a fitted object
findings.detail: `st.session_state['target_transformer']` is either the literal string 'log1p' or a fitted sklearn PowerTransformer. Every consumer must branch: `if _bt_transformer == 'log1p': np.expm1(...) else: _bt_transformer.inverse_transform(...)`. That branch is duplicated in page 06 (twice: test preds, train preds), the CV path (TransformedTargetRegressor with func/inverse_func vs transformer=clone), and page 08. One missed branch inverts predictions with the wrong function and produces plausible-looking wrong numbers.
findings.action: engine — one TargetTransform ADT with .forward/.inverse; picklable-only when it wraps PowerTransformer, so Project stores the SPEC and Jobs re-fits

findings.item: Boundary Train: target_label_encoder (LabelEncoder)
findings.detail: Fitted sklearn LabelEncoder, pickle-only, in _NEVER_PERSIST. Set only when the target dtype is object/category/bool; POPPED otherwise. Page 07 re-applies it to raw y (`if label_encoder is not None and y_raw.dtype == object`) — if the encoder is stale relative to the current frame's categories, .transform raises ValueError inside a bare `except Exception: pass`, silently degrading to the X_test fallback path.
findings.action: record the class mapping (JSON: List[str] classes_) in Project; rebuild the encoder in Jobs

findings.item: Boundary Train: y_train_original / y_val_original / y_test_original
findings.detail: np.ndarray copies of the pre-transform targets, written ONLY when a target transform is active and popped otherwise. All metric computation reads `st.session_state.get('y_train_original', y_train)` — the .get default silently substitutes the TRANSFORMED target if the key is missing, which happens whenever the pop/write pair desynchronizes. Metrics would then be reported on the log scale while labelled original-scale.
findings.action: project — Splits carries y in both scales as explicit fields; never use .get() with a silently-wrong default for a scale-bearing value

findings.item: Boundary Train: cv_strategy and cv_groups_train
findings.detail: cv_strategy: Literal['standard','group','time'] and cv_groups_train: Optional[np.ndarray] (group labels for TRAIN ROWS ONLY). Set as a side effect of the split branch, consumed by ml.eval.perform_cross_validation. cv_groups_train is a numpy array — not JSON-safe. Both are cleared by reset_downstream_results. If the split branch changes and these are not updated in lockstep, CV folds silently leak across the grouping variable.
findings.action: project — derive the CV scheme FROM the recorded split strategy rather than storing it as a parallel field that can desync

findings.item: Boundary Train: feature_names vs feature_names_by_model
findings.detail: feature_names: List[str] = the RAW input columns (`list(feature_cols)`). feature_names_by_model: Dict[model_key -> List[str]] = post-transform names from ml.pipeline.get_feature_names_after_transform (PCA→PC1..PCn, KMeans→kmeans_*). Page 07 has three-tier fallback logic to reconcile a length mismatch against the actual SHAP/PI array width, ending in generic 'feature_0..n' names — i.e. mislabeled importance plots are already an accepted failure mode.
findings.action: project — post-transform feature names are an output of the fitted pipeline artifact and must travel WITH it, not in a parallel dict that can go out of sync

findings.item: Boundary Train→Explain: trained_models
findings.detail: `Dict[model_key -> BaseModelWrapper]` (NNWeightedHuberWrapper | RFWrapper | GLMWrapper | HuberGLMWrapper | RegistryModelWrapper). Interface: fit(X_train,y_train,X_val,y_val,**kw)->Dict, predict(X)->ndarray, predict_proba(X)->Optional[ndarray], get_model()->Any, supports_proba()->bool. The NN wrapper holds a torch nn.Module — picklable only with torch installed and only on a compatible device. In _NEVER_PERSIST by design (utils/session_manager.py:11-16 documents the security rationale: no pickle is ever loaded from user bytes).
findings.action: jobs — fitted models are job outputs with a content-addressed cache key; Project stores only the key + config

findings.item: Boundary Train→Explain: model_results
findings.detail: `Dict[model_key -> {'metrics': Dict[str,float], 'train_metrics': Dict[str,float], 'history': Dict[str,List[float]], 'y_test_pred': np.ndarray, 'y_test': np.ndarray|Series, 'y_test_proba': Optional[np.ndarray], 'cv_results': Optional[Dict]}]`. Mixed: metrics/history are JSON-safe, the three y_* arrays are not. Note the comment '(y_test and y_test_pred are always on original scale)' — which holds only if the y_*_original write/pop pair stayed in sync.
findings.action: record (metrics, history) + jobs (prediction vectors as a job artifact)

findings.item: Boundary Train→Explain: fitted_estimators vs trained_models — two objects per model with different semantics
findings.detail: trained_models holds the WRAPPER; fitted_estimators holds the bare sklearn estimator via `model.get_model()`, EXCEPT for 'nn' where it holds `model.get_sklearn_estimator()` and force-fits it on one row if unfitted (`fitted_estimator.fit(X_train_model[:1], y_train[:1])`). Page 07 builds `SklearnPipeline([('preprocess', prep), ('model', estimator)])` from fitted_estimators + fitted_preprocessing_pipelines. Three dicts must stay key-aligned; nothing enforces it.
findings.action: jobs — one TrainedModel record per key holding {wrapper, estimator, pipeline, feature_names_out}; three parallel dicts is the bug factory

findings.item: Boundary Train→Report: bootstrap_results, baseline_results, calibration_results
findings.detail: bootstrap_results: Dict[model -> Dict[metric -> BootstrapResult]] (@dataclass, ml/bootstrap.py:12). baseline_results: Dict[name -> {'description': str, 'metrics': Dict}]. calibration_results: Dict[model -> CalibrationResult] (@dataclass, ml/calibration.py:13 — holds numpy arrays for the curve). Only bootstrap_results and sensitivity_seed_results appear in _NEVER_PERSIST; baseline_results and calibration_results are in NEITHER list, so they are silently dropped on save with no 'skipped' note.
findings.action: record — CI/calibration numbers are manuscript facts; persist the scalars, recompute the curves

findings.item: Boundary Explain→Report: shap_results carries raw arrays plus a duplicate
findings.detail: `Dict[model -> {'shap_values': ndarray(2D), 'X_eval': ndarray, 'feature_names': List[str], 'class_label': Optional[str], 'all_shap_values': <original explainer output, list-or-ndarray, possibly 3D>, 'kernel_capped': bool, 'n_eval_samples': int}]`. 'all_shap_values' duplicates the full payload for class switching — memory doubles per model. shap_matplotlib_figs: Dict of matplotlib Figures (unpicklable across processes).
findings.action: jobs (arrays as artifacts) + view (figures rendered on demand, never stored)

findings.item: Boundary Explain→Report: permutation_importance and pdp_results
findings.detail: permutation_importance: Dict[model -> {'importances_mean': ndarray, 'importances_std': ndarray, 'feature_names': List[str]}]. pdp_results: Dict[model -> {'pd_per_feature': Dict[int, sklearn Bunch], 'pd_2d': Dict[Tuple[int,int], Bunch], 'feature_indices': List[int], 'feature_names': List[str]}]. pd_2d is keyed by a TUPLE — not JSON-serializable as a dict key. Note pdp_results is written under that name while init_session_state declares 'partial_dependence' — see the dead-key finding.
findings.action: jobs (arrays) + record (top-k importance table, which is what the manuscript cites)

findings.item: Boundary Explain: cancel_explainability / cancel_training are cooperative flags polled inside the render loop
findings.detail: Both are booleans set by an st.button inside the same script run that is doing the work, then polled between models (`if st.session_state.cancel_explainability: break`). This only works because Streamlit re-runs the script; there is no actual cancellation of an in-flight sklearn call. permutation_importance at 3000 features is explicitly documented as ~141s uninterruptible.
findings.action: jobs — this is the concrete requirement the Jobs layer exists to satisfy; the current flags cannot interrupt anything and must be replaced, not ported

findings.item: Boundary Sensitivity→Report: sensitivity_seed_results / sensitivity_dropout_results / sensitivity_dropout_baseline
findings.detail: Two pd.DataFrames (seed: columns seed + metric names + optional '_error'; dropout: feature, score_without, impact, optional '_error') and a float baseline. Only sensitivity_seed_results is in _NEVER_PERSIST; the dropout pair is in no list. ml/publication.py reads sensitivity_dropout_results directly from session_state at module scope (line 1382), which is one of the 32 publication↔streamlit couplings.
findings.action: record — sensitivity verdicts are manuscript claims; pass them into publication as arguments, never via ambient state

findings.item: Boundary Hypothesis Testing: hypothesis_test_results holds only the LAST test run
findings.detail: Six separate `st.session_state.hypothesis_test_results = {...}` assignments (correlation, t-test, chi-square, ANOVA, etc.), each overwriting the previous. The audit trail survives only because log_methodology appends a 'Statistical Validation' entry per test, and pages/10 rebuilds the list by filtering methodology_log for that step. So the Record is authoritative and the state key is vestigial.
findings.action: record — make the ledger/methodology log the only store; drop the single-slot key

findings.item: Boundary →Report: methodology_log has last-wins semantics for six steps and append for the rest
findings.detail: `List[{timestamp, step, action, details}]`. REPLACE_STEPS = {'Upload & Audit','Feature Engineering','Feature Selection Applied','Preprocessing','Model Training','Explainability'} scan backwards and replace in place; everything else appends. Every call ALSO writes a pre-resolved Insight to the ledger via _log_to_ledger with a fixed id for replace-steps and an action-slug id for additive ones — so the ledger inherits the same replace/append duality through id collision, not through explicit logic.
findings.action: record — this dual-write bridge is the most load-bearing undocumented contract in the app; the id-collision-as-upsert trick must be made explicit

findings.item: _log_to_ledger swallows every exception
findings.detail: `except Exception: pass  # Never break methodology logging if ledger has issues`. Any schema drift in Insight (a renamed field, a new required arg) causes methodology decisions to stop reaching the ledger — and therefore stop reaching the Methods section, TRIPOD auto-completion and the narrative — with zero signal. This is the highest-value place in the codebase to add a loud failure during migration.
findings.action: record — replace with explicit error surfacing; a dropped methodology entry is a silently wrong manuscript

findings.item: Boundary →Report: insight_ledger
findings.detail: InsightLedger of Insight dataclasses (id, source_page, category, severity, finding, implication, recommended_action, manuscript_text, relevant_pages, affected_features, tripod_keys, model_scope, auto_generated, theory_anchor, action_page, resolved/resolved_by/resolved_on_page/resolved_at/resolution_details, acknowledged, metadata, created_at). Has to_dict/from_dict/to_list/from_list, all JSON-safe. Consumed for narrative_for_report(), to_manuscript_narrative(), discussion_points_for_manuscript(), get_tripod_status(), provenance_timeline(), get_methodology_log().
findings.action: record — this is already the Record; keep the schema, replace get_ledger()'s session_state lookup with injection

findings.item: reset_downstream_results reaches into the ledger and rolls back resolutions by page name
findings.detail: `ledger.rollback_resolutions({'05_Preprocess','06_Train_and_Compare','07_Explainability','08_Sensitivity_Analysis','09_Hypothesis_Testing'} [+ FE/FS pages])` and `ledger.prune_auto_generated({'02_EDA','05_Preprocess','06_Train_and_Compare'})`. The Record — described as append-mostly — is mutated by the invalidation path using hard-coded PAGE NAME STRINGS. When pages disappear in the Feed rebuild, these string sets silently match nothing and stale resolutions survive into the manuscript.
findings.action: record — key rollback on the DAG node that produced the insight, not on a page-name string that the migration deletes

findings.item: Boundary →Report: workflow_provenance
findings.detail: WorkflowProvenance with 11 optional section dataclasses (upload, eda, feature_engineering, feature_selection, split, preprocessing{shared, per_model: Dict[str, ModelPreprocessingConfig]}, training, explainability, sensitivity, statistical_validation, coach). to_dict via asdict(); from_dict reconstructs each section with field filtering and hand-rolls the nested per_model dict. Fully JSON-safe. reset_downstream_results nulls sections by setattr on a hard-coded name list ['eda','split','preprocessing','training','explainability','coach'] — 'statistical_validation' and 'sensitivity' are NOT in that list and therefore survive a data change, describing analyses of data that no longer exists.
findings.action: record — the section list must be derived from the DAG, not typed by hand; the two omissions are live bugs

findings.item: Boundary →Report: manuscript_context is a frozen snapshot that markdown and LaTeX both read
findings.detail: _build_manuscript_context() freezes selected_results, selected_bootstrap, workflow_feature_names, train_n/val_n/test_n, dataset_descriptor and feature_counts so 'markdown and LaTeX share the same boundary'. Its feature-name resolution has a FOUR-level fallback (selected_features → data_config.feature_cols → X_train.columns → feature_names → []), each level describing a different stage of the pipeline. Whichever level fires determines the predictor count printed in the abstract.
findings.action: project — a single authoritative final-predictor list removes the whole fallback chain and the abstract/methods disagreement it causes

findings.item: ml/publication.py reaches into st.session_state from 8 separate call sites at function scope
findings.detail: generate_methods_from_log (methodology_log), _resolve_workflow_feature_counts (pre_fe_feature_cols, engineered_feature_names, selected_features), generate_methods_section (feature_engineering_applied, engineering_log, engineered_feature_names, preprocessing_config_by_model), plus shap_results, bland_altman_results, sensitivity_seed_results, sensitivity_dropout_results, engineered_feature_transforms, methodology_log. All use local `import streamlit as st`. This is the 32-reference coupling and it is entirely READ-ONLY — every one can become a parameter.
findings.action: engine — mechanical: thread a single ManuscriptInputs dataclass through; no logic changes needed

findings.item: Import cycle ml.publication ↔ utils.insight_ledger is a genuine layering inversion
findings.detail: utils/insight_ledger.py imports model_display_name, format_resolution_detail, models_to_families, families_display from ml.publication (lines 128-520 of publication are pure formatting helpers with no ML content), while ml.publication reads the ledger's output. The formatting helpers belong to neither: they are presentation.
findings.action: view — extract the label/format helpers into a presentation module; both cycles dissolve

findings.item: Import cycles utils.cohorts ↔ utils.test_lockbox and utils.cohorts ↔ utils.session_state ↔ utils.test_lockbox
findings.detail: All three are resolved today by FUNCTION-LOCAL imports: test_lockbox.render_lockbox_status does `from utils.cohorts import active_cohort` (line 269), cohorts.record_run does `from utils.test_lockbox import get_lockbox` (line 466), session_state.get_data does `from utils.cohorts import apply_cohort` (line 216), set_data/reset_data_dependent_state do `from utils.cohorts import clear_cohort` (lines 278, 428), test_lockbox.ensure_lockbox does `from utils.session_state import reset_downstream_results` (line 228). The cycles exist because row-membership state is split across three modules that each mutate the others.
findings.action: project — lockbox + cohort + active-rows are ONE concern; merging them into the Project object removes all three cycles without any deferred-import tricks

findings.item: RFWrapper defines predict_proba and supports_proba twice
findings.detail: Lines 75-85 and 87-97 are byte-identical duplicates; the second pair silently shadows the first. Harmless today, but it means the file has been edited by paste at least once and models/ has zero test coverage to catch a divergence.
findings.action: drop the duplicate — and note models/* is entirely untested, so this is the class of defect that will not be caught during the port

findings.item: Cleaning actions that drop rows leave the lockbox labels stale until the next config save
findings.detail: `new_df = apply_fn(df)` then `set_data(new_df, is_schema_change=False)`. set_data clears the cohort and calls reset_downstream_results on a fingerprint change, but reset_downstream_results does NOT pop test_lockbox (only reset_data_dependent_state does). ensure_lockbox re-runs later on the same page render and its signature includes a content hash, so it self-heals in practice — but only if the user reaches the Step-4 config block. Navigate away first and train_row_mask silently quarantines fewer rows than n_test claims.
findings.action: project — lockbox validity must be a DAG edge from raw_data, not a side effect of visiting a page

findings.item: session_manager persists preprocessing_config but not preprocessing_summary, baseline_results, calibration_results, sensitivity_dropout_results, data_audit, engineering_log, consensus_features or feature_selection_results
findings.detail: The taxonomy comment says 'Anything not listed is dropped on save (not persisted) and ignored on load'. Eight consequential keys fall through: they are neither in _PLAIN_KEYS nor _NEVER_PERSIST, so they vanish without appearing in the manifest's skipped_keys list. A restored session silently loses its feature-selection record and its calibration numbers.
findings.evidence: utils/session_manager.py:69-162, :323-330 (manifest skipped_keys only records encode FAILURES, not omissions)
findings.action: project — make the taxonomy exhaustive-by-construction (every Project field declares its persistence class) so omission becomes a compile-time error

findings.item: visualizations.py is already clean and can move to engine unchanged
findings.detail: Five functions, all returning plotly go.Figure or a formatted string, zero streamlit imports, zero session_state: plot_training_history(history), plot_predictions_vs_actual(y_true, y_pred), plot_residuals(y_true, y_pred), plot_bland_altman(...), create_metrics_display(metrics). Untested but structurally portable as-is.
findings.action: engine — move verbatim; add tests before the port, not after

findings.item: models/* (7 files, 1000 loc) has zero streamlit and a single stable ABC — port it first
findings.detail: BaseModelWrapper(ABC) with abstract fit/predict and concrete predict_proba/get_model/supports_proba. Five concrete wrappers all conform. The only environmental dependency is torch in nn_whuber (guarded: page 06 raises 'The neural network needs the optional torch package' when NNWeightedHuberWrapper is None). This is the lowest-risk, highest-confidence first migration slice — and it is also entirely untested, which is the reason to do it first with tests attached.
findings.action: engine — port first, with characterization tests written against the current behavior before any code moves

summary:
I traced Upload → Target/Split → EDA → FeatureEng → FeatureSel → Preprocess → Train → Explain → Sensitivity → Report by reading utils/session_state.py, utils/test_lockbox.py, utils/cohorts.py, utils/session_manager.py, utils/workflow_provenance.py, utils/insight_ledger.py, ml/pipeline.py, ml/publication.py, models/*, and all ten pages. 68 findings.

THE SCHEMA (what actually crosses each boundary). Roughly 130 live session_state keys sort into four serialization classes: (1) JSON-safe config — five dataclasses (DataConfig, SplitConfig, ModelConfig, TaskTypeDetection, CohortStructureDetection) plus preprocessing_config_by_model, methodology_log, insight_ledger, workflow_provenance, test_lockbox, cohort_run; (2) parquet-only frames — raw_data, working_table, df_engineered, filtered_data, datasets_registry, X_train/X_val/X_test, table1_df, the two sensitivity DataFrames; (3) pickle-only fitted artifacts — preprocessing pipelines, fitted_estimators, trained_models (torch inside NNWeightedHuberWrapper), target_transformer (a string-OR-PowerTransformer union), target_label_encoder; (4) must-recompute — dataset_profile, DatasetSignals (currently never stored at all), eda_results (contains figure objects), shap/pdp arrays.

THE FIVE THINGS MOST LIKELY TO BREAK SILENTLY:
1. Row identity is two incompatible conventions. The lockbox and cohorts use index LABELS; train/val/test_indices use POSITIONS into whatever get_data() returned at split time. Page 07 does df_raw.iloc[test_indices] against a freshly-fetched frame — if the row set moved, explanations are computed on different people with no error.
2. Page 03 hand-rolls a partial invalidation cascade, missing 18 keys that reset_downstream_results() clears. Stale bootstrap CIs, calibration and baselines survive into the manuscript.
3. macro_shape's four @st.cache_data functions take the DataFrame as a leading-underscore arg, which excludes it from the cache key — dataset B gets dataset A's PCA.
4. Persistence writes every frame with to_parquet(index=False) while the lockbox restores index labels verbatim; a non-RangeIndex frame restores with a silently unsealed test set.
5. Three near-silent write paths: _log_to_ledger's bare `except Exception: pass`, ml/eda_actions' import of a nonexistent utils.storyline.add_insight (4 findings permanently swallowed), and record_split reading three SplitConfig fields that do not exist (target trimming never reaches the Methods section).

Plus: four sources of truth for task_type (one of which, session_state['task_type'], is read but never written, making TrainingProvenance always say "validation Accuracy"); five report keys with no writer anywhere (bland_altman_results, sensitivity_feature_dropout, shap_values, partial_dependence, explainability_robustness); page 10 reading data_audit['missing_counts'] which page 01 never writes; Feature Selection silently dropping every categorical predictor while the UI says it does not; and page 02 EDA running target-aware fits (including quick_probe_baselines' own 80/20 split) across the sealed test rows, contradicting test_lockbox.py's own docstring.

All three import cycles are one problem — row-membership state split across cohorts/test_lockbox/session_state, patched with function-local imports. Merging them into the Project dissolves all three. The coach's cross-page widget-key writes (st.session_state[f"train_model_{key}"] = True on page 05, read on page 06) are the Router in embryo and are the single most fragile thing to port. The cancel_training/cancel_explainability flags cannot actually interrupt anything and should be replaced by Jobs, not ported. Safest first slice: models/ (zero streamlit, one stable ABC, 1000 loc) and visualizations.py — both entirely untested, so write characterization tests before moving anything.
title: Stage-Boundary Data Contracts for AnalysisProject: what crosses each seam, how it serializes, and what breaks silently if moved carelessly

findings.item: Positional unit-conversion factors + reconcile_pipeline_columns silently misalign to the wrong variables
findings.detail: build_unit_harmonization_config builds `conversion_factors = []` by appending once per column while iterating `numeric_features` in order (ml/pipeline.py:41-64); build_plausibility_bounds does the same with `zip(numeric_features, conversion_factors)` (ml/pipeline.py:84). Both lists are handed positionally into `UnitHarmonizer(unit_harmonization_factors)` (ml/pipeline.py:178) and `PlausibilityGate(lower_bounds, upper_bounds)` (ml/pipeline.py:185-188) as the FIRST steps of the numeric branch, which sees a bare ndarray. reconcile_pipeline_columns then trims the ColumnTransformer's column selector (`kept = [c for c in cols if c in available]`, ml/pipeline.py:528) but does `clone(trans)` (line 531) — the factor/bound lists are copied at FULL length. Dropping one numeric column shifts every later column by one position while the factors stay put.
findings.action: engine — make UnitHarmonizer/PlausibilityGate take Dict[column_name, factor] and resolve by name at transform time using feature_names_in_. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: a mg/dL→mmol/L factor applied to age, and a cholesterol column gated against an age reference interval, so most of that column becomes NaN and is median-imputed. No exception. The manuscript still asserts 'values were harmonized to canonical units and gated against NHANES reference intervals.' Add a regression test that drops one numeric column and asserts the surviving columns' outputs are unchanged.

findings.item: Test-set lockbox stores index LABELS but session save writes parquet with index=False
findings.detail: The lockbox freezes `"labels": list(test_labels)` (utils/test_lockbox.py:213) and membership is tested by label: `return pd.Series([lbl not in test_set for lbl in index], index=index)` (utils/test_lockbox.py:248). The docstring states the contract: 'The lockbox stores index LABELS (not positions) so membership survives feature engineering and row filtering, which preserve the original index' (utils/test_lockbox.py:16-17). But `_df_to_parquet_bytes` does `df.to_parquet(buf, index=False)` (utils/session_manager.py:171), so raw_data / df_engineered / filtered_data / working_table all come back with a fresh RangeIndex. filtered_data and df_engineered are exactly the frames that PRESERVE a non-contiguous original index.
findings.action: project — serialize dataframes with the index preserved (index=True + explicit index round-trip), or move the lockbox to a content-addressed row key. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: after Save/Resume, labels [5,9,40] land on RangeIndex rows 5,9,40 of a filtered frame that no longer contains those people. train_row_mask quarantines the wrong rows, target-aware feature selection sees real test rows, and page 06's guard (`if int(is_test_row.sum()) < 2` — pages/06_Train_and_Compare.py:411) still passes because the count is right. Reported test metrics are optimistic and nothing warns.

findings.item: macro_shape's four @st.cache_data functions hash NOTHING — every dataset gets the first dataset's PCA/UMAP/TDA
findings.detail: Streamlit skips hashing parameters whose name starts with an underscore. compute_pca(_df_numeric, n_components=None, max_features=200), compute_umap(_df_numeric, ...), compute_persistence(_df_numeric, ...), compute_mapper(_df_numeric, ...) take the frame as `_df_numeric` and every other arg has a default. Call sites pass ONLY the frame: `compute_pca(df_numeric)` / `compute_umap(df_numeric)` / `compute_persistence(df_numeric)` / `compute_mapper(df_numeric)` (pages/02_EDA.py:1163, 1205, 1226, 1265). Cache key is therefore constant. pages/02_EDA.py:122-125 shows the team knew about this trap and added `_data_fingerprint` for its own caches — macro_shape never got one.
findings.action: engine — delete the four decorators when macro_shape moves out of the view (its ONLY streamlit usage is these 4 decorators plus the import). Be aware this is a BEHAVIOR CHANGE that fixes a live bug: screenshots/goldens taken before the move will differ. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT today: upload dataset B, the Macro Shape section renders dataset A's scree plot, biplot and persistence diagram with dataset B's caption text ('N components explain 90% of variance across M features').

findings.item: Target-leakage detection is wrapped in `except Exception: pass`
findings.detail: The >0.95 feature-target correlation scan that populates `signals.leakage_flags` and `signals.leakage_candidate_cols` is inside a bare try, and any failure yields silence: `except Exception: pass  # Skip leakage detection if correlation fails`. The EDA page then reports no leakage candidates, which is indistinguishable from 'checked and clean'.
findings.action: engine + record — on failure emit a ledger Insight ('leakage check could not run') exactly as ml/import_doctor.diagnose does with its `checks_failed` finding (ml/import_doctor.py:812-824). WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: a post-outcome lab value stays in the feature pool, the model scores R²=0.97, and the manuscript reports a spectacular prediction model built on a proxy for the outcome. This is the single highest-stakes swallow in the codebase and it is the same class as FINDINGS_LEDGER finding 13.

findings.item: train_row_mask silently returns all-True when the lockbox is absent, and render_lockbox_status returns silently too
findings.detail: `lb = get_lockbox(); if lb is None or is_exploratory(): return pd.Series(True, index=index)` (utils/test_lockbox.py:244-246) — no lockbox means every row is visible to target-aware steps. The status chip that would disclose this also returns without rendering anything: `lb = get_lockbox(); if lb is None: return` (utils/test_lockbox.py:261-263). Exploratory mode DOES warn (line 253-260); a missing lockbox does not. get_lockbox itself is a plain session_state read that returns None on any key rename.
findings.action: project + view — make the absence of a lockbox an explicit, rendered state, not None. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: one renamed key during the session_state→Project move silently disables the entire methodological spine of the app. Feature selection and feature engineering fit on 100% of rows, Train & Compare draws a fresh random split, every page looks completely normal, and the manuscript's Methods section still describes a held-out set frozen at upload.

findings.item: OutlierCapping sets fitted attributes in __init__ and returns X unchanged when unfitted
findings.detail: `self.lower_bounds_: Optional[np.ndarray] = None` and `self.upper_bounds_` are assigned in `__init__` (ml/preprocess_operators.py:81-82). Trailing-underscore attributes are sklearn's fitted marker, so check_is_fitted sees a fitted estimator. transform then does `if self.lower_bounds_ is None or self.upper_bounds_ is None: return X_arr` (lines 102-103) — a silent no-op. Separately, __init__ also rewrites its own params (`self.params = params or {}`, line 80), which breaks sklearn's clone contract that UnitHarmonizer's docstring explicitly calls out ('Store conversion_factors by reference (no copy) so sklearn clone works', line 13).
findings.action: engine — move fitted attrs out of __init__ and raise NotFittedError in transform. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: any migration path that reconstructs a pipeline from stored config and calls transform without fit produces uncapped data while the recipe string, the ledger entry and the Methods section all say 'outliers capped at the 1st/99th percentile.' A reviewer asking 'did the capping run?' gets yes from every artifact.

findings.item: _log_to_ledger swallows every exception, so methodology decisions vanish from the record while methodology_log looks fine
findings.detail: The bridge that writes each log_methodology call into the unified ledger ends with `except Exception: pass  # Never break methodology logging if ledger has issues` (utils/session_state.py:655-656). log_methodology appends to `st.session_state.methodology_log` FIRST (line 543) and calls _log_to_ledger after, so the plain log survives while the ledger silently does not. ml/publication.py:153-160 prefers `ledger.get_methodology_log()` and only falls back to methodology_log when the ledger is EMPTY — a PARTIALLY populated ledger wins and the fallback never fires.
findings.action: record — the ledger write must be the primary path and must surface failures. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: an Insight dataclass field rename during the Record migration makes ledger.upsert throw for, say, Preprocessing and Model Training only. The ledger is non-empty, so publication.py uses it, and the Methods section is emitted with the Data Preprocessing and Model Training paragraphs simply missing. It reads as a complete, slightly terse Methods section.

findings.item: ml/eda_actions.py imports a function that does not exist, inside bare `except:` — 4 EDA insight classes have been silently dead
findings.detail: Four sites do `from utils.storyline import add_insight` then `add_insight(...)`, wrapped in `except:` / `except Exception: pass`. utils/storyline.py has no add_insight — its docstring says 'Insight management has moved to utils/insight_ledger.py (InsightLedger)' (utils/storyline.py:4). So physio_plausibility, missingness_association, target_outliers and collinearity insights never reach the ledger and never raise. The existing guard test only scans pages/ (`for page_file in sorted(os.listdir(pages_dir))`), so ml/eda_actions.py is outside its blast radius.
findings.evidence: ml/eda_actions.py:196, 280, 427, 617 (and bare `except:` at 199, 430, 620); utils/storyline.py:4 (module defines only render_breadcrumb/_get_navigation_order/get_prev_next_pages/render_page_navigation); tests/test_unified_ledger_integration.py:611-617, 626-628
findings.action: engine + record — rewrite these to return insight payloads the caller records, and widen the legacy-pattern test to ml/ and utils/. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: the app has been asserting a clean bill of health on multicollinearity, target outliers, missingness-target association and physiologic implausibility for however long this has been broken. Note the bare `except:` also catches KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit, so a Ctrl-C during EDA is swallowed.

findings.item: set_global_seed runs at page-06 module scope, so determinism depends on Streamlit rerun ordering
findings.detail: `set_global_seed(st.session_state.get('random_seed', 42))` sits at module level in pages/06_Train_and_Compare.py:95, i.e. it re-seeds numpy's and Python's GLOBAL RNG on every script rerun of that page. set_global_seed calls `np.random.seed(seed)`, `random.seed(seed)`, `torch.manual_seed(seed)` and sets `torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True` (utils/seed.py:21-29). No other page calls it. get_global_seed reads Streamlit directly: `import streamlit as st; return st.session_state.get('random_seed', 42)` (utils/seed.py:36-37).
findings.action: jobs — each job must seed its own RNG at job start from the Project's seed and, better, thread explicit np.random.Generator objects instead of touching globals. utils/seed.get_global_seed lands in project (drop the streamlit import). WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: with a job queue, two concurrent jobs share numpy's global RNG and interleave draws, so re-running an analysis with the same seed produces different numbers — while ml/publication.py:1326 keeps writing 'Random seed was set to 42 for reproducibility.' The app would be asserting something false, which the project's own governing rule (docs/FINDINGS_LEDGER.md:19-20) forbids.

findings.item: _content_fingerprint returns None on unhashable cells, downgrading invalidation to schema-only without saying so
findings.detail: `try: return hash((df.shape, int(pd.util.hash_pandas_object(df, index=False).sum()))) except Exception: return None` (utils/session_state.py:227-230). set_data only clears downstream results when BOTH fingerprints are non-None and differ: `elif (old_df is not None and old_fp is not None and new_fp is not None and old_fp != new_fp)` (utils/session_state.py:276-277). Nested-JSON imports are a first-class supported path (data_processor._JSON_WRAPPER_KEYS, records_key) and can leave list/dict cells; data_processor.py:211-214 already swallows the check that would flatten them (`except Exception: has_nonscalar = False`).
findings.action: project — the DAG's dirty-check must not have a silent 'unknown → assume clean' branch; make it 'unknown → assume dirty' and disclose. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: a researcher re-uploads a corrected version of the same JSON (same columns, fixed values). Fingerprint is None both times, so reset_downstream_results never fires. Trained models, metrics, SHAP values and the report from the OLD data remain in state and are presented as results for the corrected data.

findings.item: Stability-selection probability divides by n_bootstrap, not by the number of fits that actually succeeded
findings.detail: Failed bootstrap fits are skipped with `except Exception: continue` (ml/feature_selection.py:252-253) without decrementing anything, then `selection_probs = selection_counts / n_bootstrap` (line 256) and `selected = [f for f, p in zip(feature_names, selection_probs) if p >= threshold]` (line 257).
findings.action: engine — track n_successful and divide by it; refuse (or flag) when the success rate is low. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: on a wide matrix where half the Lasso fits fail to converge, every feature's selection probability is halved, nothing clears the threshold, and the page reports 'stability selection identified 0 robust features' — a scientifically meaningful-looking null result that is purely an artifact of swallowed convergence failures.

findings.item: publication.py's 12 session_state reads are each wrapped in `except ImportError: pass`, so Methods paragraphs disappear silently once Streamlit is removed
findings.detail: Every session_state read in the manuscript generator is `try: import streamlit as st; ... except ImportError: pass`. Uninstalling streamlit makes the import raise ImportError, which is caught, and the guarded block is skipped entirely. Affected blocks and what they emit: line 597-620 = the entire '### Feature Engineering' section; 1171-1178 = SHAP and Bland-Altman in '### Model Interpretability'; 1220-1235 = the whole Sensitivity Analysis section; 1349-1360 = the CV-on-pre-transformed-data limitation; 1381-1392 = the feature-dropout methodology caveat; 1401-1412 = the double-transformation caveat; 1826-1834 = generate_decision_audit_trail returns '' (the whole decision appendix). Line 161 is `except (ImportError, Exception):` — the tuple is redundant, it catches everything.
findings.action: record — thread an explicit Project/Record object into generate_methods_section (utils/workflow_provenance.get_methods_context at utils/workflow_provenance.py:479-483 already exists for exactly this: 'This replaces the 100+ scattered session_state reads in Report Export'). WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: the manuscript compiles, is well-formed, and quietly omits every methodological caveat and limitation the app exists to force authors to disclose. Complete keys to re-plumb: methodology_log, pre_fe_feature_cols, engineered_feature_names, selected_features, feature_engineering_applied, engineering_log, preprocessing_config_by_model, shap_results, bland_altman_results, sensitivity_seed_results, sensitivity_dropout_results, engineered_feature_transforms.

findings.item: models/* use `is_fitted` but ml/estimator_utils only recognizes `is_fitted_`
findings.detail: BaseModelWrapper sets `self.is_fitted = False` (models/base.py:22, no trailing underscore) and RegistryModelWrapper sets `self.is_fitted = True` on fit (models/registry_wrappers.py:37); GLMWrapper, HuberGLMWrapper and RFWrapper inherit this. Only models/nn_whuber.py uses `is_fitted_` (lines 104, 126, 162, 185, 567). is_estimator_fitted checks `hasattr(estimator, 'is_fitted_')` in BOTH fallback branches (ml/estimator_utils.py:25-26, 41-42), and check_is_fitted on a non-sklearn wrapper raises TypeError, routing to the permissive branch which looks for coef_/feature_importances_/n_features_in_ on the WRAPPER (they live on the inner .model).
findings.action: engine — unify on one fitted-marker and add tests; ALL of models/* is currently test-uncovered so nothing catches this. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: `if estimator is None or not is_estimator_fitted(estimator): return None, None, None, None` (pages/07_Explainability.py:172) makes a correctly-fitted GLM/RF/Huber wrapper indistinguishable from an untrained one, so SHAP / PDP / permutation importance silently produce nothing for those models and the report's explainability section covers only the sklearn-native models.

findings.item: Explainability re-derives the test set POSITIONALLY from a frame that may have changed since training
findings.detail: Page 06 stores positions, not labels: `original_indices = np.where(mask)[0]` then `st.session_state.test_indices = original_indices[...].tolist()` (pages/06_Train_and_Compare.py:383, 683-693). Page 07 reads them back as positions into a freshly-fetched frame: `raw_candidate = df_raw.iloc[test_indices]` and `y_raw = df_raw[data_config.target_col].iloc[test_indices].values` where `df_raw = get_data()` (pages/07_Explainability.py:182-198). get_data() applies cohort filtering and prefers df_engineered over filtered_data over raw_data (utils/session_state.py:194-217), so the row set it returns can differ between the two page visits.
findings.action: project — the Project must expose the test set as row LABELS with a single accessor; positional indices across page boundaries cannot survive a job queue where the frame is re-materialized. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: switch cohorts (or apply feature engineering) between Train & Compare and Explainability, and SHAP/PDP are computed on a different set of rows than the model was evaluated on. If the frame is still long enough, no IndexError — just feature importances for the wrong people.

findings.item: macro_shape monkey-patches sklearn.utils.validation at MODULE IMPORT, globally and unconditionally
findings.detail: At import time ml/macro_shape.py rebinds `_skval.check_array = _compat_check_array` (line 41) and `_skutils.check_array = _compat_check_array` (line 45) — process-wide, affecting all sklearn code, not just gtda/umap. ml/compat.py implements the same fix properly (surgical, opt-in, idempotent via `global _PATCHED`, patches only gtda modules — ml/compat.py:22-78) and its docstring says 'This is surgical — it only affects gtda's calls, not the rest of the application' (lines 9-10). Two implementations of the same patch coexist; importing macro_shape wins because it is unconditional.
findings.action: engine — delete the macro_shape block and call ml.compat.patch_gtda_for_sklearn() explicitly from the job that needs TDA. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: in a long-lived worker process, whether sklearn's check_array is patched depends on whether some earlier job happened to import macro_shape. `_has_ensure`/`_has_force` are computed once at import (lines 27-28), so the wrapper's behavior is frozen at first-import time. Import order becomes semantically load-bearing — exactly the kind of coupling that survives a move and then fails months later.

findings.item: EDA's _data_fingerprint is schema-only — it cannot see value changes
findings.detail: `_data_fingerprint = (len(df), len(df.columns), tuple(sorted(df.columns)))` (pages/02_EDA.py:125) is threaded as `data_id=` into _compute_profile, _compute_signals, _get_skewed_features, _compute_outlier_heatmap, _compute_corr, _top_corr_pairs, _sort_by_target_corr and _compute_interactions. It captures shape and column NAMES only. Contrast utils/session_state._content_fingerprint, which hashes values (utils/session_state.py:228). Any cleaning action that changes values without changing shape — recode_missing (ml/import_doctor.py:876-887 sets values to NaN in place, same shape), coerce_numeric, unit override — leaves the fingerprint identical.
findings.action: project — the invalidation DAG must key on a content hash, not a schema tuple. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: the researcher recodes 999 → missing in a blood-pressure column, returns to EDA, and every cached panel (profile, signals, skew list, outlier heatmap, correlation matrix, target-correlation ordering, suggested interactions) still shows the pre-cleaning numbers. The 999s are visibly gone from the raw preview, so the page looks internally consistent.

findings.item: @st.cache_resource shares one mutable model registry across every session, and one call site hands out the shared params dict
findings.detail: `@st.cache_resource def _get_registry_cached(): return get_registry()` appears three times (pages/05_Preprocess.py:31-33, pages/06_Train_and_Compare.py:795-799, pages/07_Explainability.py:30-32). cache_resource returns THE SAME object to all sessions — not a copy. get_registry() itself builds a fresh dict per call (ml/model_registry.py:178-180), so the singleton-ness comes entirely from the decorator. ModelSpec.default_params and ModelCapabilities.notes are mutable and live inside it. Page 06 defensively copies — `spec.default_params.copy()` (pages/06_Train_and_Compare.py:1437) — but Report Export does not: `params = selected_model_params.get(model_key, spec.default_params if spec else {})` (pages/10_Report_Export.py:1372).
findings.action: engine — get_registry() is already pure; drop the cache_resource wrappers entirely and let the Project hold per-analysis params. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT (borderline, requires a mutating caller): any code path that writes into the dict returned at pages/10_Report_Export.py:1372 changes the default hyperparameters for every subsequent analysis in the process, including other users' sessions on a shared server. The reported hyperparameters would be another study's.

findings.item: Two different has_outliers thresholds for the same field name, and the coach re-thresholds on top of them
findings.detail: For FEATURE columns: `profile.has_outliers = profile.outlier_rate > 0.01  # >1% outliers` (ml/dataset_profile.py:215). For the TARGET: `profile.has_outliers = profile.outlier_rate > 0.05` (ml/dataset_profile.py:258). ml/model_coach.py then applies a THIRD check to the already-thresholded target field: `target_outliers = bool(tp and tp.has_outliers and (tp.outlier_rate or 0) > 0.01)` (lines 394 and 1355).
findings.action: engine — decide one threshold and make the coach read outlier_rate directly rather than the pre-thresholded boolean. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT today: a target with 3% outliers gets has_outliers=False, so the coach never recommends Huber loss even though its own stated rule is >1%. During the move, unifying the two dataclass fields (they share a name) will silently flip model recommendations one way or the other, and nothing in the test suite will notice.

findings.item: detect_outliers returns an all-False mask for an unrecognized method name
findings.detail: After the iqr/mad/zscore/percentile branches, the function falls through to `return mask, info` where mask is still `pd.Series(False, index=series.index)` from line 27. An unknown method is indistinguishable from 'zero outliers found'. The EDA heatmap compounds this: `except Exception: row[method.upper()] = 0.0` (pages/02_EDA.py:822-823).
findings.action: engine — raise ValueError on an unknown method. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: rename 'zscore' to 'z_score' anywhere during the migration (it is a user-facing selectbox value at pages/02_EDA.py:398-403 and a config string in preprocessing) and every outlier report in the app becomes 0.0% — a clean bill of health on data the app never inspected. The outlier heatmap renders as a solid zero grid, which reads as 'no outliers' rather than 'broken'.

findings.item: The JSON wrapper-key guess still lives in the engine while the disclosure lives in the view
findings.detail: FINDINGS_LEDGER C4 ('Several wrapper keys present → resolved by _JSON_WRAPPER_KEYS iteration order, silently') was fixed by adding inspect_json, which computes candidates and returns a note the page renders (data_processor.py:400-420). But _json_obj_to_frame still contains the original silent first-wins loop for when records_key is None: `for wrapper in _JSON_WRAPPER_KEYS: value = obj.get(wrapper); if isinstance(value, list) and value: return ...` (data_processor.py:283-287). The user's answer travels as a Streamlit WIDGET KEY: `st.session_state.get(f"records_key_{_fk}", "")` → cached_parse_upload → load_tabular_data (pages/01_Upload_and_Audit.py:311, 385-413; utils/perf_cache.py:22-35).
findings.action: jobs + engine — the ingest job must carry records_key as an explicit parameter, and _json_obj_to_frame should refuse (not guess) when multiple wrapper keys are present and no key was supplied. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: the upload job is written without threading the per-file widget answer, so a payload with both 'data' and 'results' silently loads 'data' — regressing a finding the ledger records as FIXED, with no test failure because the test exercises inspect_json (the view path), not the loader default.

findings.item: apply_plausibility_filter resets the index, destroying lockbox and cohort label correspondence
findings.detail: `return df.loc[mask].reset_index(drop=True)` (ml/pipeline.py:124). Called from the Preprocess page (pages/05_Preprocess.py:860). Every downstream label-based mechanism — test_lockbox labels (utils/test_lockbox.py:213, 248) and cohort labels (utils/cohorts.py:420, 446-447) — assumes the original index survives row filtering; the lockbox docstring states this as a contract (utils/test_lockbox.py:16-17).
findings.action: engine — return `df.loc[mask]` without the reset. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: cohorts partially survive because apply_cohort has a fallback that re-derives membership from the grouping column (`if col and col in df.columns: return df.loc[cohort_mask(df, col, value)]`, utils/cohorts.py:450-452). train_row_mask has NO such fallback, so the lockbox silently loses membership while the cohort silently keeps it — the two mechanisms disagree about which rows are which, with no error.

findings.item: Session save reports only a COUNT of skipped items, and load silently drops unknown keys
findings.detail: Five save paths append to skipped_keys and swallow the reason: dataclass configs (utils/session_manager.py:236-237), insight_ledger (264-265), workflow_provenance (275-276), test_lockbox (309-310), coach_probe (320-321). The UI shows only `f"\n- **Note:** {len(skipped)} items skipped (non-serializable)"` (line 729). On load, dataclass reconstruction failure is `except Exception: pass` (lines 518-519) and the comment at line 523 is explicit: '# unknown keys are silently ignored'. Restore also begins with `try: reset_data_dependent_state() except Exception: pass` (lines 421-425).
findings.action: project — this module is the direct ancestor of Project serialization; name every skipped key in the message and make an unrecognized key a loud migration event. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: the lockbox fails to encode, the sidebar says '1 item skipped (non-serializable)', the researcher resumes, and the analysis silently continues with no sealed test set. Note the good counter-example already in the file: provenance, lockbox and coach_probe RESTORE failures each append a human-readable warning (lines 552-556, 580-585, 597-601) — the save path should match.

findings.item: datasets_registry keys are coerced to str on both save and load
findings.detail: Save: `index[str(dataset_id)] = member_name` (utils/session_manager.py:222). Load: `registry[str(dataset_id)] = _read_parquet(zf, member)` (line 504). Any non-string key (the pages write `st.session_state.datasets_registry[dataset_id] = df` at pages/01_Upload_and_Audit.py:285 and 518) comes back as a string.
findings.action: project — pin dataset_id to str at creation, or store the original type alongside. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: if dataset_id is ever an int or UUID object, `registry[dataset_id]` misses after a restore and the multi-file combine UI shows an empty dataset list — reading as 'no datasets added yet' rather than 'your datasets are here under different keys'.

findings.item: data_processor can install a caller-supplied index from JSON, breaking every label invariant downstream
findings.detail: For pandas orient='split' payloads: `if isinstance(obj.get("index"), list) and len(obj["index"]) == len(df): df.index = obj["index"]` (data_processor.py:273-274), inside a `try/except Exception: pass  # fall through` (276-277). set_data only resets the index when it is NON-UNIQUE (`if not df.index.is_unique: df = df.reset_index(drop=True)`, utils/session_state.py:249-253), so a unique but arbitrary index (strings, timestamps, floats) survives into raw_data.
findings.action: engine — normalize to a RangeIndex on ingest and keep the file's index as an ordinary column. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: lockbox labels become the JSON's strings; _plain_label coerces them via `str(x)` (utils/session_manager.py:296); after a parquet round-trip the frame has an integer RangeIndex, so `lbl not in test_set` is True for every row and train_row_mask returns ALL TRUE. Feature engineering and feature selection then fit on the full dataset including the held-out rows, with no warning anywhere upstream of Train & Compare.

findings.item: next(iter(dict.values())) picks a 'representative' preprocessing config by insertion order
findings.detail: `first_pca = next(iter(pca_details.values()))` with the comment '# Use the first PCA config as representative' (ml/publication.py:626-628), and `first_cfg = next(iter(_per_model_configs.values()))` (line 798), plus `all_cfgs = list(_per_model_configs.values()); shared_scaling = all_cfgs[0].get(...)` (lines 807-808). The source dict is `st.session_state.get('preprocessing_config_by_model', {})` — insertion-ordered by whatever sequence the Preprocess page built pipelines in.
findings.action: record — key these by the model actually being described, or assert that the configs agree before collapsing them. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: preprocessing_config_by_model is JSON-round-tripped or rebuilt in a different order by the Project (sorted keys, DB row order, concurrent job completion order), so the Methods section reports 'PCA dimensionality reduction (12 components)' from XGBoost's config while describing Ridge's pipeline. A specific, checkable, wrong number in the manuscript.

findings.item: Macro Shape colors rows via .loc on an index it assumes is shared
findings.detail: `df_numeric = df[numeric_features].dropna()` then `color_vals = df.loc[df_numeric.index, target_col].values` (pages/02_EDA.py:1140, 1144). This is correct only because dropna preserves labels. If df_numeric is ever reset (or df is), and df has a RangeIndex 0..N-1 while df_numeric was reset to 0..M-1, the .loc lookup SUCCEEDS (those labels exist) and returns the first M target values instead of the surviving rows' values.
findings.action: engine — return the color vector from the compute function alongside the embedding, aligned by construction. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: a UMAP/PCA scatter colored by the wrong target values. The plot renders, the colorbar has the right range, and the visible cluster structure appears uncorrelated with outcome — leading the researcher to conclude there is no outcome-related structure in the data.

findings.item: calculate_regression_metrics drops non-finite pairs and reports only to the logger
findings.detail: `finite = np.isfinite(y_true) & np.isfinite(y_pred); if not finite.all(): logging.getLogger(__name__).warning(...); y_true, y_pred = y_true[finite], y_pred[finite]` (ml/eval.py:29-37). The metrics are then computed on the SUBSET and returned as ordinary floats with no indication of how many pairs were dropped. The docstring names the exact trigger: 'a degenerate target-transform back-mapping (e.g. a power transform fit on a near-constant target) can produce NaN/inf predictions.'
findings.action: engine — return n_dropped in the metrics dict and have the job surface it into the ledger. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: a degenerate target transform makes 30% of test predictions NaN; those rows are dropped; R² is computed on the 70% the model handled well and reported as the test-set R². The warning goes to a terminal nobody reads under Streamlit, and to a worker log nobody reads under a job queue. Inflated headline metric, published.

findings.item: The de-facto Router logic lives in the view, and four modules disagree about what 'done' means
findings.detail: utils/theme.render_sidebar_workflow computes step completion by probing session_state directly: data_configured / features_selected / pipeline_built / models_trained / explainability_run / sensitivity_run / report_generated / feature_engineering_applied (utils/theme.py:744-758). Three other definitions exist: WorkflowProvenance.get_completeness returns a 10-key dict keyed on `self.<stage> is not None` (utils/workflow_provenance.py:461-477); utils/insight_ledger.WORKFLOW_PHASES groups the 10 pages into 5 phases (lines 495-501); utils/storyline.PAGE_ORDER + RECOMMENDED_PAGE_IDS defines the navigable spine and a 'quick' mode that skips pages (lines 11-34, 55-64).
findings.action: router — pick get_completeness() as the single source of truth (it is already serializable and already feeds TRIPOD), and delete the theme.py probe. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: the Router asks a question the user already answered (or skips one they did not) because it consults a different completeness definition than the one the manuscript's TRIPOD tracker consults. The interview and the manuscript then disagree about what was done.

findings.item: NHANES reference is lru_cached for the process lifetime and keyed on a parameter the function ignores
findings.detail: `@lru_cache(maxsize=1) def load_nhanes_reference(reference_url: Optional[str] = None)` reads `os.getenv("NHANES_REFERENCE_URL")` INSIDE the body when the arg is None (ml/physiology_reference.py:51-58), so the cache key is None regardless of the env var. A fetch failure falls back silently: `except (URLError, HTTPError, ValueError): pass` → `return DEFAULT_NHANES_REFERENCE` (lines 65-68). load_reference_bundle is likewise `@lru_cache(maxsize=4)` (line 71) and its docstring says 'Cached per process.'
findings.action: engine — pass the resolved URL in explicitly and make fallback an explicit return value the caller can record. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: in a long-lived worker, one transient network blip at first call freezes the bundled defaults for the entire process. Every subsequent analysis is gated against default reference intervals while `"reference_version": nhanes_ref.get("version")` (ml/pipeline.py:105) faithfully records the default version — so the record is honest but the researcher believes they configured a live reference. Note socket timeouts are not URLError and are NOT caught, so failure mode differs by network condition.

findings.item: Sensitivity seed loop swallows failed seeds and then reports the survivor count as the analysis size
findings.detail: `except Exception: pass` inside the per-seed loop (ml/sensitivity.py:92-93), followed by `description=f"Results across {len(variations)} different random seeds (baseline seed={baseline_seed})."` (line 99). ml/publication.py:1253-1260 writes this into the manuscript: 'using {d.get("n_seeds", "multiple")} random seeds to assess sensitivity of ...'.
findings.action: engine — count attempts and failures separately and expose both. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: 6 of 8 seeds fail (OOM in a worker, a convergence error), the analysis silently becomes a 2-seed study, the coefficient of variation is computed across those 2 seeds, and publication.py:1278-1281 reports 'the coefficient of variation across seeds was 0.8%' — a robustness claim built on two runs, presented as the same analysis that would have used eight.

findings.item: Univariate feature screening records p=1.0 for tests that CRASHED
findings.detail: `except Exception: p_values.append(1.0); test_stats.append(0.0); test_names.append("failed")` (ml/feature_selection.py:178-181). p=1.0 is a perfectly ordinary p-value; the only distinguishing signal is the string 'failed' in a parallel test_names list, and the p_values array is what feeds `p_values = np.array(p_values)` and the multiple-testing correction on the next lines.
findings.action: engine — use NaN and exclude failed columns from the correction denominator. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: a feature whose correlation test crashed (constant after masking, dtype issue) is reported as p=1.00 — 'no association with the outcome' — and is dropped. It is also counted in the multiple-testing denominator, deflating everyone else's corrected p-values. Both effects are invisible in the results table if it renders p rather than test_names.

findings.item: import_doctor's duplicate-label branch swallows check failures WITHOUT the disclosure the main loop adds
findings.detail: The main check loop collects failures and appends an explicit `checks_failed` ShapeFinding whose why_it_matters says 'treat a clean result here as incomplete rather than as a guarantee' (ml/import_doctor.py:800-824) — this is the fix for FINDINGS_LEDGER finding 13. But the duplicate-label early-return branch above it does `for check in (check_empty_rows_and_columns, check_footer_rows): try: out.extend(check(df)) except Exception: continue` (lines 792-796) with no such disclosure and an early `return out` at line 798.
findings.action: engine — apply the same `failed`/`checks_failed` disclosure to the duplicate-label branch. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: a file with duplicate column labels AND a footer row reports only the rename suggestion; the footer check crashed and nothing says so. Finding 13's own test (TestDuplicateLabels::test_a_failed_check_is_disclosed_not_swallowed) exercises the main loop, so this branch is uncovered by the regression that closed the finding.

findings.item: Bare `except:` sets skewness to 0.0 — perfectly symmetric — on any failure
findings.detail: `try: profile.skewness = float(valid.skew()) except: profile.skewness = 0.0` at ml/dataset_profile.py:203-206 and again at 250-253. Bare except also catches KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit.
findings.action: engine — use None and let consumers treat it as unknown. WRONG-BUT-PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT: skewness=0.0 is the value that means 'no transform needed'. A column whose skew computation fails is reported as perfectly symmetric, the Feature Engineering page does not recommend a log transform, and a heavily right-skewed biomarker goes into a linear model untransformed.

findings.item: perf_cache's cached_target_correlations computes Spearman by a rank identity that differs from pairwise-deletion Spearman
findings.detail: `spearman = sub.rank().corrwith(target.rank())` (utils/perf_cache.py:145). The docstring is honest about it: 'With missing values the rank-based Spearman can differ from pairwise-deletion Spearman in the 3rd decimal; the consumers threshold at coarse cutoffs (0.7, 0.08) where this is immaterial.' That justification is a statement about the CURRENT consumers.
