Enforced concretely by the manuscript register separation (CODE_REVIEW 'Manuscript-trust wave'): Insight.manuscript_text carries reviewer-facing phrasing for every auto-generated producer so coaching voice ('a reviewer would question…', 'consider…') 'can no longer reach the Discussion verbatim, and the regex cleaner is now a fallback rather than the mechanism'. The NEW Router is precisely the component that will be tempted to short-circuit this — it is promoted from advisor to decision-maker, and a Router that records its own reasoning into Record turns advice into evidence.
findings.evidence: docs/ARCHITECTURE_SCROLLYTELLING_BRIEF.md §8; CODE_REVIEW.md 'Manuscript-trust wave' (1); utils/insight_ledger.py:580 theory_anchor / manuscript_text field
findings.action: router (Router writes to Project and reads Record; it must have NO write path into Record)

findings.item: INVARIANT — the no-pickle / _NEVER_PERSIST session contract is a SECURITY property, and the code is deliberately better than its docs
findings.detail: ARCHITECTURE.md:182-188: save/load is a ZIP of JSON+Parquet, 'Deliberately not pickle-based: pickle files are rejected on load for security, and fitted models/pipelines are never persisted (_NEVER_PERSIST) — after restoring a session, models are re-trained by re-running Train & Compare. What round-trips: data, configuration, ledger entries, provenance records, and methodology logs.' Backed by utils/session_manager.py:60 _ACCEPTED_SCHEMA_VERSIONS={'2.0','2.1'}, :65-67 _MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES/_MAX_EXTRACTED_BYTES/_MAX_MEMBERS zip-bomb caps, :123 _SAFE_WIDGET_KEYS, :138 _NEVER_PERSIST. CODE_REVIEW verdict: 'Holds (better than documented)'. THE RISK: the AnalysisProject design already has to_dict/from_dict, and a Jobs layer needs to hand fitted estimators between processes. Serializing a Project 'because it's easy now' quietly converts a rejected-by-design format into the default one.
findings.action: project (Project.to_dict must inherit _NEVER_PERSIST and the pickle refusal by construction, not by convention)

findings.item: INVARIANT — 'nothing is written to disk; each browser session is fully isolated.' A job queue is the single most likely violator
findings.detail: ARCHITECTURE.md:13 and :171-174: 'session-state-only project/dataset management (nothing is persisted to disk; sessions are saved as user-downloaded archives)'. CODE_REVIEW verifies it: the SQLite layer and utils/persistence.py are dead code with no callers; session archives are built in-memory; PDF compiles in an auto-cleaned tempdir. The README caveat the reviewers raised is that 'All processing happens in your browser session' is already inaccurate for server-side Streamlit. A Jobs layer needs somewhere to park intermediate state and results between worker and web process — that is a disk write, and it is invisible to any function-level inventory because no function does it today.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md:13,171-180; CODE_REVIEW.md 'Privacy: Nothing is written to disk' row
findings.action: jobs (decide the persistence story explicitly and update ARCHITECTURE.md in the same commit — design principle #7)

findings.item: INVARIANT — lockbox timing: sealed at stage 1, respected through 2–5, opened EXACTLY ONCE at stage 6. A scrolling interview makes 'exactly once' hard
findings.detail: docs/ARCHITECTURE_SCROLLYTELLING_BRIEF.md §4A: '~15% drawn into a sealed vault… Every target-aware step (EDA, FE fits, feature selection, the coach probe) operates on train_row_mask() rows only… The vault opens exactly once, at stage 6.' CODE_REVIEW's remediation adds the laundering guard: 'An explicit, watermarked Exploratory mode preserves fast full-data screening, and toggling it in EITHER direction resets downstream results so exploratory selection can never launder into a clean manuscript.' In a single scrolling feed the user can scroll back up and change an earlier answer AFTER stage 6 has opened the vault — a page-ordered app gets 'before anyone looks' for free from navigation order; a feed does not. The Router must own vault-open-once as an explicit state transition.
findings.evidence: docs/ARCHITECTURE_SCROLLYTELLING_BRIEF.md §4A; CODE_REVIEW.md remediation ('Both leakage criticals'); utils/test_lockbox.py:26,28
findings.action: router + project (lockbox draw/open must be Project state transitions the Router gates, not an emergent property of scroll position)

findings.item: INVARIANT — reset_downstream_results supports PARTIAL resets; a naive 'invalidate everything downstream of node N' DAG cannot express them
findings.detail: CODE_REVIEW 2026-07 section: applying a feature selection must clear stale pipelines/splits/models while PRESERVING the selection just made — `reset_downstream_results(clear_feature_engineering=False, clear_feature_selection=False)`, described as 'a new flag that clears stale pipelines/splits/models while preserving the selection just made.' Feature-Engineering Skip and Reset route through the same helper, and Reset must RESTORE the pre-FE selected_features list (previously it never did, leaving selection referencing engineered columns that no longer existed — the reported NHANES crash: 'Some column names are not columns of the dataframe: {meds_hbp_has_data, meds_chol_has_data}'). ARCHITECTURE.md:278 adds the completeness rule: 'Any page that introduces a new result key must add it to reset_downstream_results().'
findings.action: project (the invalidation DAG needs per-edge suppression AND a restore-previous-value path, not just cascade-clear)

findings.item: INVARIANT — reconcile_pipeline_columns: drift must self-heal loudly, never crash cryptically; its sibling reconcile_state_with_df is imported but never called
findings.detail: CODE_REVIEW 2026-07 'Backstop (defense in depth)': 'pages/06 reconciles the feature list vs the data before Prepare Splits, and rebuilds any preprocessing pipeline whose columns drifted before fit() (ml.pipeline.reconcile_pipeline_columns) — loud warning, self-heal, never a cryptic crash. Any future drift path degrades gracefully.' That is a design stance, not a function: the rebuild must keep a reconciliation checkpoint at the split boundary even if the DAG is 'correct'. Contrast utils/reconcile.py's reconcile_state_with_df() — CODE_REVIEW C7: 'The intended safety net… is imported but never called by any page (only scripts/smoke_check.py).' Two reconcilers, one wired, one not.
findings.action: project (keep an explicit reconciliation checkpoint before every fit); drop or wire reconcile_state_with_df — do not port it dormant

findings.item: INVARIANT — CV strategy is bound to the SPLIT strategy, and cv_strategy/cv_groups_train are cleared WITH the split
findings.detail: CODE_REVIEW 2026-07: 'CV previously used shuffled KFold regardless of the split. A group split (longitudinal) or time split now gets GroupKFold/StratifiedGroupKFold / TimeSeriesSplit, so CV can't leak across entities or time and inflate the score. CV still runs on training rows only; cv_strategy/cv_groups_train are recorded at split time and cleared with the split.' Also: 'Under the lockbox, the Train & Compare Test % slider is now disabled and pinned to the lockbox fraction… so a live control can never contradict the actual held-out set. Group/time splits (which draw their own test set) keep the slider live and say so.' Both are couplings between two Project fields that a field-by-field port will separate. Tests: tests/test_cv_strategies.py.
findings.evidence: CODE_REVIEW.md 2026-07 'Strategy-aware cross-validation' and 'Test-set slider guardrail'; tests/test_cv_strategies.py
findings.action: project (cv_strategy is a derived field of the split, with a shared lifetime); router (a control that cannot contradict state must be disabled, not merely validated)

findings.item: INVARIANT — get_data() applies the cohort filter ONCE, and exactly two callers are allowed to escape it
findings.detail: utils/session_state.py:194-217. Precedence df_engineered > filtered_data > raw_data, then `from utils.cohorts import apply_cohort; return apply_cohort(df)`. Docstring: 'the rows of that cohort are ALL any page sees — the filter is applied here, once, rather than in each of the nine pages that would each have to remember. Pass full_study=True for the two things that must span the whole study: drawing the test lockbox (every cohort inherits its slice of ONE split) and choosing the target and features (fixed across runs, which is what makes the runs comparable at all).' Production callers of full_study=True: exactly two — pages/01_Upload_and_Audit.py:619 and utils/cohort_ui.py:324. The invariant is enforced by a default parameter and a docstring. A Project exposing `project.data` will silently make every consumer a full-study consumer, breaking cohort runs, or silently make the lockbox cohort-scoped, breaking cross-run comparability.
findings.action: project (two distinct named accessors — cohort_view and full_study — never one attribute with a flag)

findings.item: INVARIANT — per-model pipeline forking is the differentiator and it is real; a Project schema that collapses to one pipeline destroys the product
findings.detail: ARCHITECTURE.md:29: 'This layer forks per model. When a user selects Ridge + Random Forest + MLP, three separate preprocessing pipelines exist simultaneously.' Design principle #5: 'Per-model pipelines are first-class… This is not a complication to manage — it's the core value proposition.' CODE_REVIEW verified it holds: '05_Preprocess.py:738-874 builds distinct pipelines per model; 06_Train_and_Compare.py:1050-1059 fits each model's own pipeline on train only.' The Project fields are plural by design: preprocessing_pipelines_by_model, preprocessing_config_by_model, fitted_preprocessing_pipelines, feature_names_by_model, fitted_estimators. A Jobs layer that parallelizes 'train the models' must fan out per (model, pipeline) pair, not per model against a shared transform.
findings.action: project + jobs

findings.item: INVARIANT — CODE_REVIEW's seven 'Design principles for future front-end changes' are the rebuild's acceptance criteria, each traced to a real defect
findings.detail: Verbatim: (1) 'Defaults carry the rigor; captions carry the disclosure; options carry the speed. The zero-click path must be the methodologically correct one. Never make rigor opt-in.' — directly constrains the Router's default next question. (2) 'State first, widgets second. Before drawing UI, name the session-state keys: who writes, who reads, who invalidates' — root cause of calibration_results and selected_models read-never-written; I found two MORE live instances this pass (working_df, dict-vs-dataclass), so the class is NOT closed. (3) 'Every number on screen names its data' — train/val/test/full-cohort chip; HARDER in a feed where a stale card stays visible above the fold. (4) 'UI copy is a contract with code' — a rewrite rewrites all copy, so every describing sentence must be re-verified against the computation. (5) 'Never render a dead branch; gate visibly. Requires X — run it on page Y beats silent omission' — in a single scroll there is no 'page Y'; the Router must supply the equivalent. (6) 'The manuscript is the regression test. Every UI result either flows to the export or is explicitly UI-only.' (7) 'Docs are claims… the doc edit belongs in the same commit.'
findings.evidence: CODE_REVIEW.md '## Design principles for future front-end changes' (items 1-7)
findings.action: router (1,3,5); project (2,6); view (3,4); all (7)

findings.item: INVARIANT — 'Absent is better than false': the invalidation cascade must visibly clear ALL FOUR planes, not just the data plane
findings.detail: docs/ARCHITECTURE_SCROLLYTELLING_BRIEF.md §4B: a 'clear' wave ripples downstream across all four lanes, 'wiping stale results — pipelines, splits, models, insights, provenance sections. Tagline: Absent is better than false.' Acceptance checklist §9: 'The invalidation cascade visibly clears all four lanes.' A DAG that only tracks data-derived artifacts and leaves the ledger and provenance sections intact reproduces critical finding C5 exactly ('reset_data_dependent_state() never clears shap_results, bootstrap_results, baseline_results, sensitivity_seed_results, hypothesis_test_results, methodology_log, or workflow_provenance… the manuscript embeds the previous dataset's SHAP plots with no warning'). The Record layer is described as 'append-mostly' in the target architecture — but the cascade REQUIRES it to be truncatable, and the ledger already implements rollback_resolutions / prune_auto_generated for exactly this.
findings.evidence: docs/ARCHITECTURE_SCROLLYTELLING_BRIEF.md §4B, §9; CODE_REVIEW.md C5; brief §0 table (InsightLedger: rollback_resolutions, prune_auto_generated)
findings.action: record + project ('append-mostly' must explicitly carve out rollback_resolutions/prune_auto_generated and provenance-section clearing)

findings.item: tests/test_insight_id_integrity.py — an AST scanner that will silently stop testing anything the moment the rebuild renames Insight or the ledger variable
findings.detail: Docstring: 'extracts, via AST (no imports, no Streamlit runtime): PRODUCED ids: every `...Insight(id=...)` constructor call with a string or f-string id, across pages/, utils/, ml/. REFERENCED ids: string literals passed to ledger.resolve/acknowledge/get/remove calls (receiver name containing "ledger")…'. SCAN_DIRS = ['pages','utils','ml'] and _receiver_mentions_ledger() literally checks `'ledger' in ast.dump(node).lower()`. CODE_REVIEW records it caught a third live instance on its first run (train_prefer_simpler). Under the rebuild: SCAN_DIRS no longer exist (pages/ is deleted), the receiver may be `project.record` or `self._ledger`, and the constructor may not be named Insight. The scanner then finds zero produced and zero referenced ids and PASSES — a green test that verifies nothing, guarding the exact defect class (stale identifiers) that a rename-heavy refactor generates most.
findings.action: record (port the scanner FIRST, against the new names, and assert a nonzero produced-id count so it can never pass vacuously)

findings.item: Known test-fidelity hole exactly at the model-object boundary — the transition's safety net does not cover models/
findings.detail: CODE_REVIEW 'Note on test fidelity': 'tests/integration/conftest.py injects a bare sklearn Ridge into trained_models, but the real Train page stores wrapper objects — the suites exercise downstream pages against a state shape the app never produces, which is how the Feature Dropout clone() breakage stayed invisible.' The concrete instance: pages/08:382 calls clone(model_obj) on wrapper objects that do not implement get_params, raising TypeError per feature, swallowed → all impacts 0. This compounds with the measured fact that ALL of models/* is uncovered by any test. So the layer the rebuild most needs to move intact (Engine/models) is simultaneously the least covered AND the one whose existing coverage tests a shape the app never produces.
findings.evidence: CODE_REVIEW.md 'Dynamic testing summary' note; tests/integration/conftest.py:67; pages/08_Sensitivity_Analysis.py:382 vs :104
findings.action: engine (write characterization tests against the REAL wrapper objects before moving models/; do not trust the green suite)

summary:
COMPLETENESS SWEEP — 14 uncovered .py files (4,068 loc) plus doc-level invariants and WIP collisions. No files modified.

UNCOVERED FILE INVENTORY (everything in ml/, models/, utils/, root not already inventoried by another agent): utils/theme.py (938 loc), utils/llm_ui.py (892), utils/theory_demos.py (869), utils/dataset_db.py (797), utils/perf_cache.py (146), utils/datasets.py (115), utils/table_export.py (58), setup.py (35), utils/widget_helpers.py (21), utils/column_utils.py (19), launcher/make_icon.py (175), and three 1-line __init__.py files. models/ and pages/ are fully covered by prior agents; scripts/ and tests/ excluded per brief.

THE FOUR HIGHEST-VALUE SILENT BREAKS FOUND:
1. ml/macro_shape.py:82/240/337/495 — four @st.cache_data functions whose only argument is underscore-prefixed (Streamlit skips hashing those) and whose call sites (pages/02_EDA.py:1163,1205,1226,1265) pass nothing else. The cache key is a CONSTANT, and st.cache_data is process-global: the first dataset's PCA/UMAP/persistence/Mapper is served to every later dataset and every later user. The author demonstrably knows this hazard — pages/02_EDA.py:122-124 comments on it and passes data_id=_data_fingerprint to the profile/signals caches — macro_shape just never got the fix.
2. Global-RNG mutation: utils/datasets.py:17,49,77 + utils/seed.py:21-27 + models/nn_whuber.py:314-315 all call np.random.seed / torch.manual_seed on PROCESS state. Safe today (one script run at a time), silently corrupting under a Jobs worker pool — and reproducibility is a headline manuscript claim, so it fails where it costs most, in a way no existing test can catch.
3. utils/theme.py:685 — render_sidebar_workflow is not styling. It contains the ONLY implementation of the app's step-completion state machine (10 predicates over session_state) and the quick/advanced split that decides which questions are optional. That is the Router's readiness function, filed under CSS. Delete theme.py as "just styling" and the step model is gone.
4. Two NEW instances of the read-never-written class that CODE_REVIEW design principle #2 was written to close: utils/llm_ui.py:225 reads session_state["working_df"] (nothing writes it; page 01 writes working_table) and :213 type-guards dataset_profile as a dict when the session holds a DatasetProfile dataclass. Both fail closed and produce a thinner, plausible answer. The class is not closed.

DOC INVARIANTS A FUNCTION-LEVEL INVENTORY MISSES (all quoted, all traceable): the governing rule "the app may be silent, and it may refuse, but it must never assert something false" with "high confidence is the only tier the UI pre-selects, so high means the app is asserting" — which binds directly onto the new Router, because auto-advance IS pre-selection; the plane authority order "advise/witness/publish — never draw the Advisory plane writing into the Narrative plane," which forbids exactly the Router→Record shortcut the promotion invites; the no-pickle/_NEVER_PERSIST session contract, a security property reviewers found is BETTER than its docs and that a Project with to_dict/from_dict will erode by convenience; "nothing is written to disk," which a job queue is the most likely thing ever to violate; lockbox-opens-exactly-once, which a page-ordered app gets free from navigation order and a scrolling feed does not; partial invalidation (reset_downstream_results(clear_feature_engineering=False, clear_feature_selection=False)), which a naive downstream-cascade DAG cannot express; and get_data()'s cohort filter with exactly two full_study=True escapes (pages/01:619, utils/cohort_ui.py:324) enforced by nothing but a default parameter.

TWO STRUCTURAL WARNINGS ABOUT THE SAFETY NET ITSELF: (a) tests/test_insight_id_integrity.py is an AST scanner keyed on the literal names "Insight" and a receiver containing "ledger", scanning SCAN_DIRS=["pages","utils","ml"]. After the rebuild those names and that directory are gone, so it finds zero ids and PASSES — a green test guarding the exact defect class a rename-heavy refactor produces. Port it first, with a nonzero-count assertion. (b) CODE_REVIEW already records that tests/integration/conftest.py injects a bare sklearn Ridge where the app stores wrapper objects — "the suites exercise downstream pages against a state shape the app never produces" — and models/* has zero test coverage. The layer that must move intact is both the least covered and the one whose existing coverage tests a fiction.
